title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Information Collection; Comment Request; Applications for Licensing or Registration To Issue Payment Stablecoins Under the GENIUS Act
summary: The OCC is seeking comment on a new information collection and application forms for entities seeking OCC approval to issue payment stablecoins, or for foreign payment stablecoin issuers to register with the OCC, under the GENIUS Act. Comments are due by 2026-09-25. This is a procedural notice, but it signals the application process for affected issuers in the United States.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Multiple Bureau of the Fiscal Service Information Collection Requests
summary: The Treasury Department published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice seeking public comment on two Bureau of the Fiscal Service information collection requests for existing Treasury securities forms. Comments are due by 2026-08-26. No new substantive requirements are created; this is an OMB review notice.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Multiple Internal Revenue Service Information Collection Requests
summary: The Treasury Department is seeking OMB review and public comment on several IRS information collection requests, with comments due by 2026-08-26. The notice lists extensions and revisions to existing collections, including forms and surveys related to tax withholding, estate taxes, and electronic payee statements.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request on the Burden Related to the Disclosure of Returns and Return Information in Connection With Written Contracts or Agreements for the Acquisition of Property or Services for Tax Administration Purposes
summary: The IRS is requesting public comments on an existing Paperwork Reduction Act information collection about disclosure of tax returns and return information under contractor agreements for tax administration. No form or requirement changes are being made; comments are due by 2026-09-25.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Comment Request on the Burden Related to the Requirements for Completing and Submitting Form 8655
summary: The IRS is seeking public comments on the continued information collection for Form 8655 (Reporting Agent Authorization) under the Paperwork Reduction Act. It does not change the form or requirements, and comments are due by 2026-09-25. The notice is aimed at businesses that use reporting agents for federal employment tax functions.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request on Employee Plans Compliance Resolution System
summary: The IRS is requesting comments on an existing information collection for the Employee Plans Compliance Resolution System under the Paperwork Reduction Act. It does not change the filing requirements or forms, and comments are due by 2026-09-25.

title: Open Meeting of the Taxpayer Advocacy Panel Joint Committee
summary: The IRS Taxpayer Advocacy Panel Joint Committee will hold an open virtual meeting on 2026-08-19 to gather public comments and suggestions on improving IRS customer service. Advance registration is required by 2026-08-14 to attend or speak. This is an informational notice only and does not create obligations.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 15c1-6
summary: The SEC published a 60-day Paperwork Reduction Act notice seeking comment on the information collection associated with Rule 15c1-6 for broker-dealers. It does not change the rule itself. Comments are due by 2026-09-25.

title: Sunshine Act Meetings
summary: The SEC announced a closed Sunshine Act meeting on July 30, 2026 to discuss enforcement actions, administrative proceedings, litigation claims, and examination matters. This is an informational notice only and does not create new obligations for firms.

title: ETF Opportunities Trust and Hedgeye Asset Management, LLC
summary: SEC notice that ETF Opportunities Trust and Hedgeye Asset Management have applied for exemptive relief to allow subadvisory agreement changes without shareholder approval and to relax certain fee disclosure requirements. Interested persons may request a hearing by August 17, 2026. The notice itself does not impose new obligations.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Order Granting Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Adopt a New Continued Listing Requirement
summary: The SEC approved Nasdaq’s rule change adopting a new continued listing requirement: listed companies must maintain at least $5 million in market value of listed securities. The order also lets Nasdaq’s Hearings Panel grant up to a 180-day exception for companies seeking to regain compliance. This affects companies listed on Nasdaq Global Select, Global Market and Capital Market markets.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Monthly Fees for Its Proprietary Market Data Feeds
summary: The SEC published notice of TXSE’s proposed rule change to charge monthly fees for its proprietary market data feeds. TXSE says it will implement the fees when it begins operating as a national securities exchange and waive them until 2027. Interested persons may comment on the filing; no firm obligation is created yet.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Connectivity Fees
summary: The SEC is publishing TXSE’s proposed rule change, filed with immediate effectiveness, to add monthly connectivity fees for physical and logical connections, including order entry, drop copy, and market data ports. The proposal would apply to members and non-members and is intended to take effect when TXSE begins operations as a national securities exchange.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend IEX Rule 2.160 and Rule 18.110 Regarding the General Securities Sales Supervisor Registration Category and the Corresponding Series 9/10 Qualification Examination; and Amend Rule 2.160 Regarding the Description of the Regulatory Element Continuing Education Requirements
summary: IEX filed and immediately made effective amendments to its rulebook to add the General Securities Sales Supervisor registration category and Series 9/10 exam recognition, and to update the regulatory element continuing education description to align with FINRA changes. The filing is relevant to IEX members and associated persons, especially firms preparing for IEX options trading. No separate compliance date is stated in the notice.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Establish Fees for Its Exchange Designated Complex Instruments (“EDCI”) Feed
summary: Cboe filed a proposed rule change, immediately effective under SEC Rule 19b-4, to establish fees for its Exchange Designated Complex Instruments data feed. The notice seeks public comment on the fee schedule for market data distributors and users of the EDCI subset of the COB feed. No compliance date is stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq ISE, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Rules at Options 7, Section 4 (Complex Order Fees and Rebates)
summary: The SEC published Nasdaq ISE’s immediately effective proposed rule change to compress its tiered Priority Customer complex order rebate schedule in Options 7, Section 4. It affects exchange members and order flow providers trading complex options orders. No compliance date is stated in the excerpt, but comments are being solicited and the filing is already effective upon submission.

title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
summary: The Federal Reserve issued a correction to a prior Change in Bank Control notice concerning Gregory A. Dunlap Revocable Trust and related parties joining a control group to acquire voting shares of Country Bank Shares, Inc. and indirectly Farmers and Merchants Bank. No new substantive requirement is created; this is a corrected notice of a permitted ownership change.

title: Formations of, Acquisitions by, and Mergers of Bank Holding Companies
summary: The Federal Reserve published a notice inviting public comment on a bank holding company acquisition application under the Bank Holding Company Act and Regulation Y. The notice lists one proposed transaction and sets a comment deadline of 2026-08-27.

title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
summary: The Federal Reserve is publishing a notice of a bank control application under the Change in Bank Control Act for a proposed acquisition of shares in County Bank Shares, Inc. and indirectly Farmers and Merchants Bank. Interested persons may comment by 2026-08-12. This affects the named bank holding company and bank, and the notice itself does not create new obligations for firms generally.

title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
summary: OFAC added one or more persons to the SDN List under E.O. 14059 and E.O. 13224, blocking their property and prohibiting U.S. persons from dealing with them. This is effective as issued on 2026-07-23 and is relevant immediately for sanctions screening, blocking, and payment/relationship controls.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Requesting Comment Notice of Application for Reward for Original Information
summary: The IRS is seeking public comments on an existing Paperwork Reduction Act information collection for Form 211, used to request rewards for original information about alleged tax-law violations. There is no change to the collection itself. Comments are due by 2026-09-28.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 15c1-5
summary: The SEC issued a 60-day notice seeking comments on extending the Paperwork Reduction Act collection for Exchange Act Rule 15c1-5. It reminds broker-dealers controlled by, controlling, or under common control with an issuer to give customers written notice of the control relationship at or before the transaction. Comments are due by 2026-09-28.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Order Approving Proposed Rule Change by the Options Clearing Corporation To Establish a Commercial Paper Program
summary: The SEC approved OCC’s rule change to establish a commercial paper program, allowing it to raise up to $1 billion of prefunded liquidity from private placements of unsecured debt. The change is for OCC as a U.S. clearing agency/CCP and is intended to support settlement obligations and liquidity risk management. No firm compliance date is stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing of Amendment No. 1 and Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Amend the Opening Auction Process Provided Under Rule 11.23(b)(2)(B) To Delay the Opening Auction Under Certain Market Conditions
summary: The SEC approved, as modified by Amendment No. 1, a Cboe BZX rule change that delays the opening auction under certain market conditions and allows odd lot trades to set the official opening price. The change applies to Cboe BZX market participants and is effective as approved under the exchange rule filing process.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.9(d) Regarding Intermarket Sweep Orders
summary: The SEC announced it is extending the deadline for action on Cboe BZX’s proposed rule change for Intermarket Sweep Orders. The Commission must now act by 2026-09-21 on whether to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings. This is an administrative timing notice and does not itself change rules.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.9(d) Regarding Intermarket Sweep Orders
summary: The SEC issued a notice extending its deadline to act on Cboe BYX’s proposed rule change on intermarket sweep orders. The Commission now has until 2026-09-21 to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings. This is a procedural status update only; it does not itself change exchange rules or create obligations.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Compliance Rule Regarding the National Market System Plan Governing the Consolidated Audit Trail
summary: The SEC published a notice of Texas Stock Exchange’s proposed rule change to align its CAT Compliance Rule with the amended CAT NMS Plan. Industry members would need to report whether certain equity sell orders are short sales relying on the bona fide market making exception under Regulation SHO. No effective date is stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change Pursuant to IEX Rule 15.110(a) and (c) To Establish a Rebate for the External Distribution of Real-Time IEX Market Data Products
summary: The SEC published notice of an IEX proposed fee schedule change to create a rebate for redistributing real-time IEX market data to new external subscribers. The filing is effective on filing and is scheduled to be operative from 2026-09-01. It is a market-data pricing notice for participants in IEX data distribution arrangements, not a rule that directly imposes obligations on firms generally.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; ICE Clear Credit LLC; Order Approving Proposed Rule Change Relating to the Treasury Clearing Service Initial Margin Approach Model Description Document, Treasury Clearing Service Guaranty Fund and Stress Test Approach Model Description Document, and Treasury Clearing Service Risk Parameter Setting and Review Policy
summary: The SEC approved ICE Clear Credit’s proposed rule change for its U.S. Treasury clearing service risk documentation. The changes are non-substantive clarifications and typographical fixes to the initial margin model description, guaranty fund and stress test document, and risk parameter policy. This is binding for ICE Clear Credit and its clearing members once effective under the exchange rules.

title: Collaborating with other businesses
summary: The CMA published a short guidance note on how businesses can collaborate without breaching competition law, with pointers on contacting the CMA about beneficial collaborations and on environmental sustainability initiatives. It is aimed at any businesses considering collaboration and is informational rather than a new rule. No compliance date is stated.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Renewal; Comment Request; Renewal Without Change of the Generic Clearance for the Collection of Qualitative Feedback on Agency Service Delivery
summary: FinCEN is seeking comments on renewing, without change, its existing generic clearance for voluntary qualitative feedback on agency service delivery under the Paperwork Reduction Act. Comments are due by 2026-09-28. This is a notice about an information-collection approval process, not a new AML/BSA requirement for firms.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Introduce a Data Vendor Program
summary: Cboe BZX has filed a proposed rule change to the SEC to create a Data Vendor Program, define eligible Data Vendors, and grant fee waivers for certain market data products. The filing is open for comment and is not yet a final rule. No firm deadline is stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the FINRA Rule 6700 Series (Trade Reporting and Compliance Engine) (TRACE) To Expand the Scope of the Non-Member Affiliate-Principal Transaction Indicator to Also Include Member Affiliates
summary: The SEC approved a FINRA rule change expanding TRACE’s affiliate-principal transaction indicator to cover member affiliates as well as non-member affiliates. FINRA also renames the indicator to Affiliate-Principal Transaction and updates related TRACE reporting and dissemination rules. The rule is now approved and becomes binding under FINRA’s rulebook once effective.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.8(c) Regarding Intermarket Sweep Orders
summary: The SEC published a notice extending the period for action on Cboe EDGA Exchange’s proposed rule change concerning Intermarket Sweep Orders and non-displayed orders. The Commission set September 22, 2026 as the new deadline to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings. This is a procedural notice only and does not itself change any requirements.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; ICE Clear Credit LLC; Order Approving Proposed Rule Change Relating to the Treasury Clearing Rules and Treasury Clearing Service Treasury Operations Policies and Liquidity Risk Management Framework
summary: The SEC approved ICE Clear Credit LLC’s proposed changes to its Treasury Clearing Rules, Treasury Operations Policy and Treasury Liquidity Risk Management Framework. The revisions update governance, loss-resource amounts, liquidity and risk management provisions for U.S. Treasury clearing. The rule change is now approved and applicable once ICC implements it under the SEC order.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Extension: Rule 10b-17
summary: The SEC is seeking comments on extending the Paperwork Reduction Act collection for Rule 10b-17. Issuers of publicly traded securities would continue to have to give notice of certain dividends, stock splits, reverse splits, and rights or subscription offerings. Comments on the 60-day notice are due by 2026-09-28.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change Pursuant to IEX Rule 15.110(a) and (c) To Amend the Exchange's Fee Schedule
summary: The SEC published notice of an IEX proposed rule change, immediately effective, to increase the monthly fee for real-time access to its TOPS market data feed from $500 to $1,000, operative from 2026-10-01. The filing is open for public comment but is not itself a final rule.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Designation of a Longer Period for Commission Action on Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.8(c) Regarding Intermarket Sweep Orders
summary: The SEC has extended its review period for Cboe EDGX’s proposed rule change on Intermarket Sweep Orders and non-displayed orders. No substantive rule is finalized yet; the Commission must act by 2026-09-22 on whether to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings.

title: Cohen & Steers Realty Shares, Inc., et al.
summary: SEC notice of an application by Cohen & Steers entities seeking exemptive relief to launch multi-class ETF funds with ETF and mutual fund share classes. It is a notice of a pending application, not an order or rule, and invites hearing requests by 2026-08-18.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Introduce a Data Vendor Program
summary: Cboe EDGA filed a proposed rule change, effective immediately under SEC SRO procedures, to add a Data Vendor Program and new definitions in its fee schedule. The program would give eligible data vendors fee waivers for Cboe One Summary and Premium external distribution fees. Market participants and exchange members should assess eligibility and comments; no specific compliance date is stated.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Amend Certain Parts of Its Opening and Closing Auctions
summary: The SEC approved TXSE’s rule change to amend its opening and closing auction processes, including late auction order handling, new order names, and the use of Participation Bands plus related dissemination rules. TXSE must give members at least 30 calendar days’ notice before initial implementation, and later parameter changes generally require five business days’ notice, with some narrower-band changes needing one business day.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change To Amend FINRA Rules 5110 (Corporate Financing Rule-Underwriting Terms and Arrangements) and 5123 (Private Placements of Securities)
summary: The SEC approved FINRA amendments to Rules 5110 and 5123. The changes update how underwriting compensation is valued, add exclusions, treat non-convertible preferred securities like non-convertible debt, and expand certain private placement filing exemptions for offerings sold to specified accredited investors. FINRA members involved in public offerings and private placements should apply the updated rules when in effect.

title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
summary: The Federal Reserve published a notice inviting comments on applications under the Change in Bank Control Act for several parties to acquire voting shares of F&M Bancshares, Inc., and indirectly F&M Bank. Comments are due by 2026-08-14. This is a perimeter/ownership-control notice affecting bank and bank holding company acquisitions, not a rule change.

title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
summary: OFAC published a sanctions action adding one or more persons to the SDN List under E.O. 13902. U.S. persons are generally prohibited from dealing with them and any property or interests in property subject to U.S. jurisdiction are blocked, effective from the action date stated in the notice.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Order Granting Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Amend Nasdaq Rule 5711(d) (Commodity-Based Trust Shares)
summary: The SEC approved Nasdaq’s rule change to amend Rule 5711(d), which updates generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares, including a 15% buffer for certain assets. This is binding for Nasdaq listings and trading of these products, with no separate firm deadline stated in the excerpt.

title: Notice of an Application of the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association for an Exemption Pursuant to Section 36 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 From Certain Conditions of Note H to Exchange Act Rule 15c3-3a
summary: SEC notice invites comment on SIFMA’s application for exemptive relief from certain conditions in Note H to broker-dealer reserve computation rules for U.S. Treasury clearing margin. It does not itself change requirements or grant relief. Broker-dealers and related market participants may be affected if the SEC later approves the exemption.

title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
summary: The FRB published a notice of Change in Bank Control Act applications for proposed acquisitions of shares in a bank or bank holding company. Interested persons may comment by 2026-08-17. This affects the named bank/group transaction and is relevant to ownership-change and control reviews, but it does not itself create new conduct requirements for firms.

title: FDIC Board of Directors Approve New Actions
summary: The FDIC Board approved two notices of proposed rulemaking: one on Community Reinvestment Act regulations and one on extensions of credit to insiders. These are proposals, not final requirements, so firms should review the drafts and be prepared to comment if relevant.

title: VALIC Company I and The Variable Annuity Life Insurance Company
summary: The SEC published a notice of an application by VALIC Company I and The Variable Annuity Life Insurance Company seeking exemptive relief to enter into and materially amend subadvisory agreements without shareholder approval and to reduce related disclosure requirements. Interested persons may request a hearing by August 24, 2026.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq Texas, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Introduce Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus Data Feeds
summary: Nasdaq Texas filed a proposed rule change to add two new consolidated market data feeds, Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus. The SEC is seeking comments, and the exchange says the amendment is effective on filing but will announce the operative date later. No action date is stated in the notice itself.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq Texas, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Various NTX Options Rules
summary: Nasdaq Texas filed an SEC notice seeking immediate effectiveness for amendments to its NTX options rules, including new order types, market maker definitions, routing and risk-protection changes, and conforming updates to align with other Nasdaq options exchanges. The SEC is soliciting comments. The filing is relevant to options market participants, but no firm deadline is stated in the excerpt.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing of Amendment No. 1 and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Amend NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Generic) Commodity-Based Trust Shares
summary: The SEC approved, on an accelerated basis, NYSE Arca’s amendment to its generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares under Rule 8.201-E. The change affects exchange listing/trading eligibility for these products in the US and is effective immediately on approval, with comments still being solicited on Amendment No. 1.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Introduce Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus Data Feeds
summary: The SEC has published Nasdaq’s proposed rule change to add two new consolidated market data feeds, Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus, combining existing Nasdaq, Nasdaq Texas and Nasdaq PSX data. It is a proposal open for comment rather than a final rule. Market participants using Nasdaq equity data may be affected if adopted.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Texas, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 7.35 (Auctions) for ETP IPO Securities
summary: NYSE Texas filed, and the SEC is soliciting comments on, a proposed rule change that would let eligible ETP IPO securities choose to start trading in the Early Trading Session instead of the standard IPO auction. This affects NYSE Texas-listed ETP IPO securities and is not yet binding. No compliance date is stated in the notice.

title: Millions of people and businesses protected against debanking
summary: UK legislation will require banks and other payment service providers to give at least 90 days’ notice before closing open-ended payment accounts and to provide a clear written explanation. The rules are expected to apply to relevant new contracts from 2026-04-28, subject to Parliamentary approval and exceptions for financial-crime compliance. They also extend to basic personal bank accounts.

title: New rules to end Buy-Now, Pay-Later wild-west, protect millions of shoppers and drive growth
summary: The UK government says it will lay legislation on 19 May to bring Buy-Now, Pay-Later into regulation. BNPL firms will have to do affordability checks, give clearer information, provide faster refunds and allow complaints to the Financial Ombudsman, with oversight shifting to the FCA. The reforms also accompany changes to the Consumer Credit Act and apply from next year.

title: New targeted support regime to enable more people to make the most of their money
summary: The FCA published draft rules for a new targeted support regime for authorised firms to help consumers with pensions and investments. The government will also publish proposed legislative changes to enable the regime, with a consultation open until 2025-08-29 and draft legislation expected on 2025-07-15. Firms offering advice, guidance or investment/pension support should review the proposals.

title: UK tightens Oil Price Cap in blow to Putin's war machine
summary: The UK and EU are lowering the crude Oil Price Cap from $60 to $47.60 per barrel for Russian oil. The new cap takes effect at 23:01 BST on 2025-09-02, with a 45-day wind-down for pre-existing compliant trades ending at 23:01 BST on 2025-10-17. UK businesses involved in shipping, insuring or servicing Russian oil must adapt.

title: Penalty issued for breach of Russia Sanctions
summary: HMT/OFSI has imposed a £300,000 penalty on Markom Management Limited for breaching UK Russia sanctions by causing a payment to a designated person. The press release also reminds firms to strengthen sanctions controls and report suspected breaches. It is informational, but highlights current enforcement risk and the related OFSI consultation on tougher penalty processes.

title: New IRA and suspected terror facilitator sanctioned
summary: HMT announced an asset freeze and director disqualification sanctions against the New IRA and Kieran Gallagher from 2025-11-06. UK persons and firms must not deal with or make funds, financial services or economic resources available to them, and breaches are criminal offences. The measures apply to persons in the UK and extra-territorially to UK persons and companies worldwide.

title: UK sanctions imposed on a person and organisation involved in terrorism in landmark action
summary: HM Treasury announced an asset freeze and director disqualification against Gurpreet Singh Rehal and an asset freeze against Babbar Akali Lehar and related entities under the UK counter-terrorism sanctions regime. From 4 December 2025, UK persons must not deal with their funds or make funds, economic resources or financial services available to them, absent a licence or exception.

title: Pubs and Live Music Venues Relief
summary: HMT announced a 15% business rates relief for eligible pubs and live music venues in 2026-27, with bills then frozen in real terms for 2027-28 and 2028-29. The notice explains eligibility and examples for local authorities and affected businesses. No direct obligations are created for banks or financial firms.

title: Consumer Credit Act reformed to protect consumers and support modern finance
summary: HMT published a policy statement on reform of the Consumer Credit Act 1974, setting out the government’s response to the Phase 1 consultation and the changes it will take forward. The reforms will repeal many remaining CCA provisions, recast some into FCA rules, and retain others in legislation. It affects consumer credit firms in the UK; further FCA consultations may follow on specific rule changes.

title: Fairer taxes for high-value homes
summary: HM Treasury has launched an eight-week consultation on the design of a new High Value Council Tax Surcharge for residential property in England worth £2 million or more. The proposal would start from April 2028, with five-yearly revaluations and an appeals/deferral framework. It is aimed at taxpayers, local government, tax, legal and property stakeholders.

title: Boost for Britain’s financial services and greater protections for consumers as new legislation is introduced
summary: The UK government has introduced the Financial Services and Markets Bill to Parliament. It would overhaul parts of financial services regulation, including simpler consumer redress, wider credit union membership, future access to face-to-face banking, fewer overlapping regulators, a lighter SMCR burden, and changes to ring-fencing. It is not yet law, so no immediate compliance date is set.

title: UK issues largest penalty for financial sanctions breaches since Russia’s 2022 illegal invasion of Ukraine
summary: HM Treasury’s OFSI imposed a £1,000,920.59 monetary penalty on Sabre Global Technologies Limited for breaching UK Russia sanctions and circumvention. The press release says the firm kept providing services to a designated airline and tried alternative payment routes. It is a warning to UK firms on sanctions controls and settlement policy; no action deadline is set.

title: UK financial system strengthened with new safeguards for major technology providers
summary: The UK government has designated four major cloud and technology providers as Critical Third Parties from 13 July 2026, bringing them under direct oversight by the Bank of England, PRA and FCA. This is intended to improve resilience of services used by banks, insurers and FMIs and may lead to CTP-specific rules and supervisory information gathering.

title: Government delivers fairer deal for shoppers as Buy-Now, Pay-Later rules come into force
summary: UK Buy-Now, Pay-Later products are now brought under FCA regulation. Providers must carry out affordability checks and give consumers stronger rights and support when things go wrong, including refund and complaint rights. The change takes effect from 2026-07-15 and applies to BNPL firms offering credit to consumers in the UK.

title: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 Recognition Requirements for Investment Exchanges Clear
summary: This UK statutory instrument sets out recognition requirements for investment exchanges and clearing houses applying for or holding recognition orders. It also explains how those requirements may be met and confirms that exchanges and clearing houses are not limited to investments only. It applies from commencement under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provisions.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: autumn 2021 update
summary: HM Treasury published an updated Charter for Budget Responsibility setting out the UK government’s fiscal policy framework, debt and welfare targets, and the role of the Office for Budget Responsibility. It is a policy/update document laid before Parliament under the 2011 Act, not a new rule or consultation. No firm compliance date is set in the text.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related technical rule changes, effective January 5, 2022. It updates filing specifications, submission types, and validations for EDGAR filers, including security-based swap entities and certain funds, with some structured-data requirements tied to later compliance dates in the underlying rules.

title: Determination Regarding Excepted Foreign States
summary: Treasury determined that Australia and Canada are excepted foreign states for CFIUS purposes, effective 2022-01-05. This affects foreign investment screening/notifications and related onboarding or transaction processes involving covered activities tied to those jurisdictions.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2021
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports, mainly confirming actions on COVID-19 cost tracking, cross-government programme cost monitoring, OPSS data strategy, defence estate planning and school funding. It does not create new rules or compliance deadlines for firms. Where dates are mentioned, they are implementation or response targets for government bodies, not regulated firms.

title: Determination Regarding Excepted Real Estate Foreign States
summary: The US Treasury, acting through CFIUS, determined that Australia and Canada qualify as excepted real estate foreign states under CFIUS real estate rules. This affects the scope of certain foreign-investment screening treatment under 31 CFR Part 802 and remains in effect absent further Committee action. No firm action date is stated.

title: Federal Reserve Bank Capital Stock
summary: The Federal Reserve finalised amendments to Regulation I to automate non-merger-related adjustments to member banks’ Federal Reserve Bank capital stock subscriptions and made related technical and conforming changes to FR 2056. The rule applies to member banks and takes effect on 2022-02-14.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting December 2021
summary: This is a government policy paper summarising the December 2021 meeting of the Financial Inclusion Policy Forum. It is informational only and does not create or change any obligations for firms.

title: Bulletin 2022-01: Medical Debt Collection and Consumer Reporting Requirements in Connection With the No Surprises Act
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin reminding debt collectors, consumer reporting agencies, and furnishers to follow FDCPA and FCRA requirements when collecting, furnishing, and reporting medical debt covered by the No Surprises Act. It is effective immediately as of 2022-01-20 and does not create new rules, but highlights conduct that may violate existing law.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s January 2022 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports on defence procurement, test and trace, Crossrail, DWP fraud and error, and Greensill-related business support issues. It is a parliamentary accountability document, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory notice, and it does not create direct obligations for firms.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2022
summary: HM Treasury sets the 2022 public service pensions increase multiplier tables, confirming a 3.1% uplift from 11 April 2022 for public service pensions, preserved pensions and lump sums. It says the Pensions Increase (Review) Order is expected to be laid in March 2022.

title: Transnational Criminal Organizations Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC issued a final rule reissuing and amending the Transnational Criminal Organizations Sanctions Regulations, effective 2022-01-21. It updates the US sanctions framework implementing Executive Orders 13581 and 13863, adding interpretive guidance, definitions, general licenses and other provisions. Firms with US sanctions exposure should review screening, controls and any dealings with blocked persons or property.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2020 to June 2021
summary: HM Treasury published annual data on basic bank accounts for July 2020 to June 2021. It reports market stock and distribution for the nine designated UK providers under the Payment Accounts Regulations 2015, but does not create new requirements. The FCA remains responsible for compliance with the regulations.

title: Notification to Institutions Covered by the FDIC's Recordkeeping for Timely Deposit Insurance Determination Rule Regarding Amendments to the Deposit Insurance Coverage Rules
summary: The FDIC notified covered insured depository institutions under Part 370 that amendments to deposit insurance coverage rules for certain trust and mortgage servicing accounts will take effect on 2024-04-01. Covered institutions must have updated deposit insurance calculation, recordkeeping and IT capabilities operational by that date.

title: Minutes of the Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes: 15 December 2021
summary: Minutes of the first UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes. It is a policy paper recording discussions under the TCA on VAT fraud cooperation and tax claims recovery; it does not create new rules or deadlines.

title: Review of the UK funds regime: a call for input
summary: HMT publishes a summary of responses to its call for input on the UK funds regime and sets out next steps for possible future reforms to fund taxation, fund structures and the authorisation process. It is an information-only policy paper; it does not itself change rules or impose deadlines.

title: Burundi Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC removed the Burundi Sanctions Regulations from the CFR effective 2022-02-11 after the US terminated the underlying national emergency. Firms should note the Burundi sanctions regime is no longer in force, though actions, proceedings, rights and penalties arising before 2021-11-18 remain preserved.

title: Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements for Security-Based Swap Dealers, Major Security-Based Swap Participants, and Broker-Dealers; Correction
summary: The SEC issued a technical correcting amendment to its recordkeeping and reporting requirements for security-based swap dealers, major security-based swap participants, and broker-dealers. The correction updates Form X-17A-5 Part II and Part IIC and is effective 2022-02-11. No new substantive requirements are introduced.

title: Emergency Import Restrictions Imposed on Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Afghanistan
summary: U.S. CBP and Treasury finalized emergency import restrictions on specified archaeological and ethnological material from Afghanistan. The restrictions took effect on 2022-02-18 and run until 2026-04-28 unless extended. Firms involved in importing goods from Afghanistan, especially customs and trade operations, must apply the new prohibited/controlled material list and related import controls.

title: Bulletin 2022-02: Compliance Bulletin on the Electronic Fund Transfer Act's Compulsory Use Prohibition and Government Benefit Accounts
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin confirming that EFTA’s compulsory use prohibition applies to government benefit accounts. It is effective immediately for covered firms and affects how consumer accounts are required or offered in connection with government benefits.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to the Public Accounts Committee on several prior reports. It explains the government’s position and planned follow-up actions on topics including the Green Homes Grant Voucher Scheme, civil service efficiency, data programme management and environmental land management. It does not itself create new regulatory obligations, and no compliance date is set.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 21 December 2021
summary: Minutes of the first UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes meeting. It records discussion of cooperation under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, but does not create or change any rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Bulletin 2022-03: Servicer Responsibilities in Public Service Loan Forgiveness Communications
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin and policy guidance on how student loan servicers should communicate with borrowers about Public Service Loan Forgiveness, especially the temporary PSLF Waiver. It highlights UDAAP risks and says servicers should provide complete and accurate information. The bulletin is effective March 1, 2022; borrowers had an October 31, 2022 deadline to benefit from the waiver.

title: Bulletin 2022-04: Mitigating Harm From Repossession of Automobiles
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin, effective 2022-03-03, warning auto loan lenders, servicers and their service providers that repossession practices may violate UDAAP standards under the Dodd-Frank Act. It highlights scenarios such as wrongful repossession, deceptive or unfair conduct, and related debt collection issues. Firms involved in auto repossessions should review servicing, collections and vendor controls immediately.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 3 February 2022
summary: This is a policy paper reporting that the UK Chief Secretary to the Treasury and the Scottish Government’s finance secretary held talks on the upcoming review of the Scottish Government’s Fiscal Framework. It does not set out new rules, obligations, or deadlines for firms.

title: Expansion of the Clarksburg Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalises a rule expanding the Clarksburg American Viticultural Area in California by about 27,945 acres. The change updates the codified AVA boundary in 27 CFR part 9 and is effective 2022-04-08. It affects wine producers and label users that reference the Clarksburg AVA.

title: Import Restrictions Imposed on Categories of Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Nigeria
summary: U.S. CBP and Treasury impose immediate import restrictions on specified archaeological and ethnological material from Nigeria, effective 2022-03-17. Imports of listed items are restricted unless the statutory conditions in the customs regulations are met. This affects importers and customs operations handling cultural property.

title: HM Treasury’s review of Pool Reinsurance Company Limited 2020-2022
summary: HM Treasury published the final report of its review of Pool Reinsurance Company Limited, setting out the government’s agreed strategic direction for the next five years. It describes intended changes to Pool Re’s reinsurance model, risk transfer and scheme rules, but it is a policy/review report rather than a binding rule. No compliance date is set in the text.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting - December 2021
summary: Record of a December 2021 meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA about the FCA’s annual Perimeter Report. It is a summary publication only; it does not change the regulatory perimeter, obligations, or deadlines for firms.

title: Removing the impact of changes in inflation from the welfare cap
summary: HM Treasury sets out the methodology for adjusting welfare spending forecasts to remove the impact of changes in inflation when assessing the welfare cap. It explains how the OBR should treat uprating effects, the spreadsheet approach used, and key assumptions. This is guidance/explanation only and does not itself create new obligations.

title: Spring Statement 2022: documents
summary: UK Spring Statement 2022 is a budget/policy document setting out fiscal and tax measures, including changes to National Insurance thresholds, fuel duty, VAT relief for energy-saving materials, and business support. It is aimed at the UK economy broadly and does not itself create direct regulatory obligations for financial firms.

title: Government response to the 2021 Fiscal Risks Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s 2021 Fiscal Risks Report discusses public debt, COVID-19 and climate-related fiscal risks, and explains the government’s fiscal stance and response. It is a policy response/statement with no direct regulatory requirements for firms and no compliance deadline.

title: Temporary Cut to Fuel Duty
summary: The UK government announced a temporary 5 pence per litre cut to fuel duty for petrol and diesel across the UK for 12 months, effective from 6pm on 23 March 2022. This is a policy announcement to support motorists and reduce pump prices; it does not create regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Spring Statement 2022: Business support factsheet
summary: This factsheet is an informational summary of business-support measures linked to the UK Spring Statement 2021 and later budget measures. It does not set out new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Debt management report 2022 to 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s annual debt management report for 2022-23 describes the government’s borrowing plans, debt management framework, and the remit for the Debt Management Office, NS&I and Exchequer cash management. It is informational and sets out policy context rather than creating new obligations for firms. Relevant mainly for market awareness and sovereign debt/liquidity monitoring.

title: National Insurance Contributions (Increase of Thresholds) Bill
summary: Draft UK Bill to raise National Insurance contribution thresholds for Class 1, 2 and 4 contributions. It changes threshold amounts in social security legislation, with some changes effective from 6 April 2022 and 6 July 2022, and requires Treasury regulations to align Class 2 thresholds with Class 4. It affects UK employers and self-employed contributors.

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1, removing specified erroneous paragraphs from section 1.263A-3 in the annual income tax regulations revision. This is a technical codification update for affected taxpayers, effective on publication, with no new substantive rule content.

title: Joint statement by HM Treasury, the CMA, the FCA and the PSR on the future of Open Banking
summary: HM Treasury, the CMA, the FCA and the PSR issued a joint statement on plans for a new oversight model for Open Banking beyond the current CMA remedies. It proposes a Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee and a future entity to govern Open Banking’s development, funding and representation arrangements. This is an announcement of next steps, not a binding rule.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2022-23
summary: This is a parliamentary report from the Royal Trustees explaining the calculation of the Sovereign Grant for 2022-23 under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011. It does not impose obligations on regulated firms or set financial-services requirements.

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS/Federal Register issued a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1, fixing editorial/technical errors in the income tax rule on stock basis in certain triangular reorganizations. It clarifies the applicability dates in § 1.358-6 for reorganizations occurring on or after specified historic dates.

title: Income Taxes
summary: This IRS CFR correction republishes 26 CFR Part 1 to fix an editorial/technical error in § 1.351-3 on records and filing requirements. It restates the effective/applicability dates for taxpayers and applies to taxable years beginning on or after May 30, 2006, with specific exchange-date rules for paragraphs (a)(3) and (b)(3).

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1, fixing technical errors in the income tax regulations for certain modified guaranteed contracts. The correction states the applicable dates for section 1.817A-1 and removes an obsolete paragraph in section 1.818-2. It applies to taxable years beginning after October 13, 2020, with a limited taxpayer election back to years after December 31, 2017.

title: Income Taxes
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 1 on excess deductions when an estate or trust terminates. It corrects the text of the rule for beneficiaries claiming deductions in the termination year. Applies to estates, trusts and beneficiaries; effective as a code correction on publication.

title: Centre for Finance, Innovation and Technology - Steering Committee
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper on the Centre for Finance, Innovation and Technology steering committee. It describes the committee’s membership, remit and timetable for developing non-binding recommendations for a future UK fintech innovation body. No firm obligations or compliance dates are created in this paper.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2021
summary: Minutes of the Government Financial Reporting User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 4 October 2021. The document records agenda items and updates on central government reporting, sustainability reporting, Whole of Government Accounts, a BEIS consultation, and related timetable and thematic review matters. It does not itself set any new requirements or deadlines.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2020-21
summary: HM Treasury publishes examples of best-practice narrative and accountability reporting for 2020-21 central government annual reports and accounts. It is guidance and illustrative benchmarking only, aimed at entities preparing ARAs across government; it does not itself create new reporting obligations or deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes –  7 April 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports on several public-sector topics, including gigabit broadband, state pension underpayments, local government finance and NHS payment schemes. It records agreed actions and target implementation dates for the named departments, but does not itself create bank-specific regulatory obligations.

title: Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 121
summary: The SEC staff issued Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 121, effective 2022-04-11, giving interpretive accounting guidance for entities that safeguard crypto-assets held for platform users. It applies to SEC reporting companies, entities with pending SEC registration statements, Regulation A filers, and certain SPAC-related businesses. Firms in scope should assess recognition, measurement and disclosure treatment for these arrangements.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: April 2022
summary: Minutes and agenda for an HMT advisory group meeting on government financial reporting, including updates on reporting cycles, local government issues, sustainability reporting and review actions. This is informational only and does not create requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: World Bank Spring Meetings 2022: UK Governor’s statement
summary: The UK Governor’s statement to the World Bank Spring Meetings calls on the World Bank, IMF and international community to provide additional support for Ukraine, neighbouring countries and developing economies. It is a policy statement with no direct obligations or compliance deadline for firms.

title: Protecting UK wholesale cash infrastructure
summary: HMT sets out its policy intent to protect UK wholesale cash infrastructure by giving the Bank of England future powers to oversee and prudentially regulate parts of the wholesale cash market. It explains the case for reform and says legislation will follow when Parliamentary time allows. No immediate obligations are created in this paper.

title: Treasury Minutes – 26 April 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to PAC recommendations across several public-spending and operational reports, including EU Exit border planning and HMRC performance. It asks departments to implement or report back on specific actions, with some target dates through October 2022, Winter 2023 and Spring 2023. This is an accountability/expectations document, not a rule change.

title: Liquidity Risk Measurement Standards
summary: The FDIC published a CFR correction to 12 CFR part 329 (Liquidity Risk Measurement Standards). It fixes technical text in sections 329.22 and 329.40 and applies to FDIC-supervised institutions. No substantive policy change is described, but the corrected rule text is part of the current handbook/rulebook.

title: Potential Reforms to UK’s Capital Allowance Regime – Inviting views
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper inviting views on potential reforms to the UK capital allowances regime. It asks businesses to respond by 1 July 2022 and does not itself change tax rules or create obligations.

title: Government approach to authorised push payment scam reimbursement
summary: Government policy paper announcing an intended legislative route to let the Payment Systems Regulator require banks and other payment service providers to reimburse authorised push payment scam victims. It signals future change but does not itself create binding obligations or a deadline.

title: Terms of engagement between HM Treasury and Pool Reinsurance Limited (Pool Re)
summary: HM Treasury and Pool Re issued an updated framework agreement setting out Pool Re’s governance, accountability, reporting, audit and financial arrangements. It applies to Pool Re and its ONS-classified subsidiaries/joint ventures and confirms how the relationship with HM Treasury should operate. The document is effective from May 2022 and should be reviewed periodically, but it does not itself create new legal powers.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2022
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments. It is a government response and progress update, not a rule, supervisory notice, or enforcement action. No direct obligations for financial firms are created; it is mainly background and awareness material.

title: Annual Information Return/Reports
summary: The IRS, DOL and PBGC issued final revisions to Form 5500 and Form 5500-SF annual return/report forms and instructions for employee benefit plans. The changes apply to plan years beginning on or after 2022-01-01 and include reporting updates for defined benefit plans, multiple-employer and pooled employer plans, plus annual technical updates.

title: Overall government support for the cost of living: factsheet
summary: A UK government factsheet summarises cost-of-living support measures for households in 2022-23. It is informational only and does not create or change regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Web General Licenses 13Q and 13R
summary: OFAC published updated Ukraine-/Russia-related general licenses 13Q and 13R for divestment or transfer of certain GAZ Group-related holdings and related settlement activity. U.S. persons using the license must file a detailed transaction report within 10 business days after the license expires. The licenses were time-limited and 13R expired on May 25, 2022.

title: Publication of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Web General Licenses 15K and 15L
summary: OFAC published Ukraine-/Russia-related General Licenses 15K and 15L for GAZ Group-related transactions, with GL 15K expiring on 2022-04-27 and GL 15L expiring on 2022-05-25. U.S. persons that used the authorizations must file a detailed transaction report within 10 business days after the license expires. The publication also confirms the scope limits and exclusions.

title: Loans in Areas Having Special Flood Hazards; Interagency Questions and Answers Regarding Flood Insurance
summary: The OCC and other federal agencies issued revised interagency flood insurance Q&As to help lenders comply with Federal flood insurance law. The guidance updates expectations on escrow of premiums, detached structure exemptions, force placement and acceptance of private flood insurance. It is effective from the issuance date of 2022-05-11 and applies to federally regulated lending institutions and related lenders.

title: Publication of Financial Services Sectoral Determination and Directives 1A, 2, 3, and 4 Under Executive Order 14024 of April 15, 2021
summary: OFAC published the Financial Services Sectoral Determination and Directives 1A, 2, 3 and 4 under Executive Order 14024, making Russia-related sanctions on financial services, sovereign debt, correspondent accounts, new debt/equity, and certain Russian state entities immediately effective or effective from specified March 2022 dates. U.S. persons and financial institutions must ensure sanctions screening and transaction restrictions are in place.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determinations
summary: OFAC publishes sanctions determinations under Executive Orders 14024 and 14071, designating the Russian aerospace, electronics and marine sectors and a category of services to Russian persons. The services determination takes effect on 2022-06-07; the sectoral determinations were effective when published on OFAC’s website. Firms with Russian touchpoints or sanctions exposure must screen and block accordingly.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 7A, 26A, 31, and 32
summary: OFAC published four Russian sanctions general licenses under 31 CFR part 587. The licenses authorize specified overflight, emergency landing, air ambulance, wind-down, and IP-related transactions, and replace prior general licenses 7 and 26. Two licenses expire on 2022-07-12; the others have no expiry stated.

title: Establishment of the Rocky Reach Viticultural Area
summary: TTB establishes the new Rocky Reach American viticultural area in Washington state, within the existing Columbia Valley AVA. The rule is effective 2022-07-05 and affects wine labeling/origin descriptions for vintners using grapes from the area.

title: Establishment of the Upper Lake Valley Viticultural Area and Modification of the Clear Lake Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalises a codified wine-label rule establishing the Upper Lake Valley viticultural area in California and expanding the existing Clear Lake viticultural area so it fully contains it. The rule is effective 2022-07-05. It affects wine producers and label users in the named area and updates the AVA boundaries in 27 CFR part 9.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 25A, 33, 34, and 35
summary: OFAC published four Russian sanctions general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 25A authorizes certain telecom/internet communications transactions; GL 33 authorizes wind-down activity for specified blocked entities until 2022-06-07; GL 34 and GL 35 provide additional temporary authorizations. Firms dealing with Russia-related sanctions exposure should check the scope and expiry dates immediately.

title: Critical third parties to the finance sector: policy statement
summary: HM Treasury sets out its policy proposal for a regime to designate certain finance-sector third parties as critical and let regulators oversee their material services. The statement explains the rationale and intended powers but does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – June 2022
summary: This is a Treasury progress report to Parliament on implementing previously accepted Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across many government programmes. It updates status and revised target dates where relevant, but it does not create new requirements for firms or set regulatory obligations.

title: Inaugural UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum
summary: HMT published a policy paper on the inaugural UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum and the Exchange of Letters signed with Japan’s FSA to formalise cooperation under the UK-Japan trade agreement. It describes information exchange, consultation, deference and technical mediation arrangements, plus working groups on insurance, sustainable finance and financial innovation. No compliance deadline or binding firm requirement is set out.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-02: Deceptive Representations Involving the FDIC's Name or Logo or Deposit Insurance
summary: CFPB circular explains when misleading use of the FDIC name, logo, or deposit-insurance claims may be deceptive under the CFPA, including for products involving new technologies such as crypto-assets. It does not create new rules or deadlines; it is an interpretive supervisory communication for covered persons and service providers.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-01: System of Consumer Financial Protection Circulars to Agencies Enforcing Federal Consumer Financial Law
summary: The CFPB announced a new series of Consumer Financial Protection Circulars to explain how it intends to enforce federal consumer financial law and to promote consistency across agencies. The circular describes the program and invites feedback; it does not itself impose a new rule or deadline on firms.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements in Connection With Credit Decisions Based on Complex Algorithms
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining that creditors using complex or “black-box” algorithms for credit decisions must still provide ECOA/Regulation B adverse-action notices with specific, accurate reasons for denial or other adverse action. It says using technology does not excuse compliance. No new compliance date is set; this is interpretive guidance for creditors subject to ECOA.

title: Cost of Living Support
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper setting out the UK Cost of Living Support package and related factsheets, including the new Energy Profits Levy on UK oil and gas companies. It is an informational package and distributional analysis published on 15 June 2022, describing measures announced from 26 May 2022 rather than creating a regulatory requirement itself.

title: United Kingdom Debt Management Office Annual Business Plan 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury’s Debt Management Office sets out its 2022-23 business plan, including planned gilt issuance, green gilt issuance, cash management, liaison with market participants and the Bank of England, and operational efficiency work. It is an informational planning document only and does not itself create new rules or deadlines for firms.

title: Fees for Reviews of the Rule Enforcement Programs of Designated Contract Markets and Registered Futures Associations
summary: The CFTC set the 2021 fee schedule for reviews of rule enforcement programs at designated contract markets and registered futures associations. Each self-regulatory organization must remit the applicable fee electronically by 2022-08-16. The notice applies to DCMs and the National Futures Association and is based on the CFTC’s cost-recovery methodology.

title: Review of the UK’s AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory regime
summary: HMT published a review of the UK’s AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory regime. It is an intelligence/policy paper that discusses post-implementation review findings and future reform ideas for the Money Laundering Regulations and supervision, but it does not itself change rules or set a compliance deadline.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting May 2022
summary: This is a government summary of the May 2022 Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting. It is an information-only publication about cross-sector discussion and collaboration on financial inclusion; it does not create new requirements, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Independent Report preceding the Fiscal Framework review: terms of reference
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for an independent report preceding the Fiscal Framework review. It is an information paper setting out the scope of the review, with no direct requirements, deadlines, or compliance actions for firms.

title: Joint Statement on the U.S.-UK Financial Innovation Partnership Meeting 29th June 2022
summary: HMT published a joint U.S.-UK Financial Innovation Partnership statement on a meeting about crypto and digital asset ecosystems. It is an informational policy paper with no new rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC issued a final rule amending the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, effective 2022-07-01, to implement and align with Executive Order 13886 and related terrorism sanctions authorities. Firms dealing with U.S. persons or U.S.-linked property must ensure sanctions screening, blocking, and controls reflect the updated designation and blocking criteria immediately.

title: Debt Collection Practices (Regulation F); Pay-to-Pay Fees
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion under Regulation F stating that debt collectors may not collect pay-to-pay or convenience fees unless the debt agreement or law expressly authorizes them, including when fees are collected through a third-party processor. It is effective immediately from 2022-07-05 and applies to debt collectors subject to the FDCPA/Regulation F.

title: Financial Reporting Advisory Board annual report: 2021 to 2022
summary: HMT’s Financial Reporting Advisory Board annual report for 2021-22 summarizes the board’s advice and oversight of public sector accounting and reporting, including delays in local government audits, IFRS 16 deferral, and work on sustainability reporting. It is an informational annual report with no new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2020-21
summary: HM Treasury explains how 2020-21 Scottish Income Tax outturn data updates the Scottish Government’s funding and block grant adjustment. It is an informational policy note for Scotland, with no new requirements, deadlines, or compliance actions for firms.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2020-21
summary: HMT explains the 2020-21 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation and its effect on Welsh Government funding for 2023-24. It is an explanatory policy paper, not a rule, and it does not create obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 25B, 36, 37, and 38
summary: OFAC published four web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified telecom/internet communications transactions, certain wind-down activity involving Severstal, and related transactions subject to stated exclusions and expiries. GLs 25B, 36, 37 and 38 were issued on 2022-06-02 and published on 2022-07-07; some expire on 2022-08-31 and 2022-07-01.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2021 to 2022
summary: This is the UK government’s annual report and accounts for the National Insurance Fund Investment Account for the year ended 31 March 2022. It explains the fund’s investment activity, performance, and audited accounts, and is laid before Parliament. It does not create new requirements for banks or other regulated firms.

title: Fees for Reviews of the Rule Enforcement Programs of Designated Contract Markets and Registered Futures Associations; Correction
summary: The CFTC corrected the 2021 schedule of fees for reviews of rule enforcement programs for designated contract markets and registered futures associations. Self-regulatory organizations must remit the applicable fee electronically by 2022-08-16. The correction fixes assessed fee data in Table 2 from the June 17, 2022 Federal Register notice.

title: Fair Credit Reporting; Permissible Purposes for Furnishing, Using, and Obtaining Consumer Reports
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion under FCRA section 604 on permissible purposes for consumer reports. It says a consumer reporting agency may provide a report only if it has reason to believe all information pertains to the consumer requested, and disclaimers do not fix a missing permissible purpose. Effective July 12, 2022. Applies to consumer reporting agencies and consumer report users in the US.

title: Publication of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Web General Licenses 2 and 10
summary: OFAC published the text of two Ukraine-/Russia-related general licenses, GL 2 and GL 10, both of which had already expired. They related to wind-down and divestment activities under the sanctions program and did not create new ongoing permissions or obligations for firms at publication.

title: Global Anti-Corruption Programme
summary: HMT/FCDO published a policy paper on the Global Anti-Corruption Programme, describing UK government activity to support anti-corruption reform, transparency, asset recovery and good practice in five priority countries through March 2022. It is informational only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Levelling Up Fund Round 2: prospectus
summary: This policy paper sets out guidance for local authorities and certain local applicants on how to bid for Round 2 of the UK Levelling Up Fund. It is informational only and does not itself create regulatory obligations for banks. The fund runs until 2024/25.

title: Treasury Minutes – July 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes is the UK government’s response to Parliamentary committee reports on a range of topics, including private renting, Bounce Back Loans, criminal justice, defence procurement, and restoration and renewal. It records government positions and intended future actions, such as a renters reform bill and a new property portal, but does not itself create binding requirements.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 27 June 2022
summary: This is a UK government policy communiqué on discussions between the UK and Scottish governments about the upcoming review of the Scottish Government’s fiscal framework. It reports talks only and does not create or change obligations, deadlines, or rules.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and Rule 301, effective 2022-07-19. The changes reflect recent EDGAR system releases, new filing submission type SPDSCL for HFCAA-related submissions, and updated filing fee payment methods. Filers using EDGAR, including issuers and other registrants, must follow the revised manual for electronic submissions.

title: Finance Bill 2021-2022: Report Stage
summary: UK Finance (No. 2) Bill report stage materials set out amendments to the new qualifying asset holding company regime, including technical fixes, definitions and clarifications to the tax rules. This is relevant to firms using or structuring QAHCs and investment vehicles in the UK. No filing date is given in this extract.

title: Departmental Minute from HM Treasury: UK Infrastructure Bank Guarantees
summary: HM Treasury published a departmental minute notifying Parliament that it intends to create a contingent liability for up to £10 billion of UK Infrastructure Bank guarantees to support infrastructure investment, climate goals and regional growth. It is a notice of intent, not a rule or obligation, and no action or deadline is set for firms.

title: UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury issued a joint statement on the sixth UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It summarises discussion themes only and does not create or change any requirements for firms.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 39, 40, 41, 42, and 43
summary: OFAC published five Russian sanctions general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified wind-down, civil aviation safety, and other transactions involving named blocked parties, with some expiring on stated dates and others with no expiry. Firms dealing with Russia-linked persons, goods or services must check whether their activity is covered and by when.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 45 and 46
summary: OFAC published two new general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 45 authorizes certain wind-down transactions for covered financial contracts through 2022-10-20, and GL 46 authorizes certain auction-process and related settlement transactions for Russian credit derivatives. Firms dealing with Russia-related sanctions activity should check whether any transactions now fall within these temporary authorizations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13 and 13A
summary: OFAC published General Licenses 13 and 13A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize certain tax, fee, duty, permit, licence and registration transactions for U.S. persons, and in GL 13A also entities owned or controlled by U.S. persons, through 2022-09-30. Firms dealing with Russia sanctions must confirm any activity stays within the licence scope.

title: Publication of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Web General Licenses 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25
summary: OFAC published nine Ukraine-/Russia-related general licenses under 31 CFR Part 589, including an expired wind-down license and authorizations for certain exports, humanitarian, energy, telecommunications, and internet-related transactions. These licenses affect sanctions screening and transaction processing for US persons and firms dealing with sanctioned Russian/Ukraine-related regions and persons.

title: Publication of Covid-Related Web General Licenses Related to Syria Sanctions Regulations, Iran Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, and Venezuela Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC published three COVID-related general licenses for Syria, Iran, terrorism-related sanctions, and Venezuela, authorizing specified pandemic-related transactions through 2023-06-17. Firms dealing with sanctioned jurisdictions or persons should review whether any COVID-19 goods, services, or related dealings now fall within the new authorizations and continue to respect other export-control limits.

title: Treasury minutes - August 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes records the UK government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports, including IR35 tax reform, evaluation and modelling, local growth, DHSC accounts, Ajax, and higher education. It sets out agreed actions and target implementation dates such as December 2022, March 2023 and December 2023, but it does not itself create new rules.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8I and 8J
summary: OFAC published Venezuela General Licenses 8I and 8J under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. GL 8J supersedes the expired GL 8I and authorizes certain PdVSA-related transactions for named covered entities until 2022-12-01, subject to detailed limits. Sanctions teams and operations need to apply the current licence conditions; other Venezuela prohibitions remain in force.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 6, 6A, 6B, 25C, 30A, and 44
summary: OFAC published six web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving agricultural commodities, medicine, medical devices, COVID-19 activities and related clinical trials. The licenses were previously issued on OFAC’s website; GL 30A expires on 2022-12-16 while the others have no stated expiry. Firms dealing with Russia-related sanctioned activity should check the scope before relying on them.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 40 and 40A
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 40A, replacing expired GL 40. The license authorizes certain liquefied petroleum gas export/reexport transactions involving the Government of Venezuela or PdVSA through 2023-07-12, subject to stated exclusions. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related sanctions matters should confirm whether their activity falls within the authorization and update sanctions controls accordingly.
