title: Government response to the National Infrastructure Commission report Infrastructure, Towns and Regeneration
summary: Government policy paper responding to the National Infrastructure Commission’s report on infrastructure, towns and regeneration in England. It discusses how the government intends to respond to recommendations on transport and digital infrastructure, but it does not create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Memorandum of understanding between the Scottish Fiscal Commission and HMT
summary: HM Treasury published a memorandum of understanding with the Scottish Fiscal Commission setting out cooperation and information-sharing arrangements so the Commission can produce independent forecasts and evaluations of devolved income, revenue and social security expenditure. It is a policy paper, not a rule or supervisory notice, and it does not impose direct obligations on firms.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-04: Insufficient Data Protection or Security for Sensitive Consumer Information
summary: The CFPB issued a circular stating that inadequate data protection or information security for sensitive consumer information can be an unfair act or practice under the CFPA, even without an actual breach. It highlights weak authentication, password management and software update controls as risky for covered persons and service providers. No new deadline is set, but firms should assess controls now.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 40B, 47A, and 48A
summary: OFAC published three Russian sanctions general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 40B authorizes certain civil aviation safety transactions, GL 47A authorizes wind-down transactions for certain blocked persons, and GL 48A extends and clarifies certain dealings through specified expiry dates. Firms dealing with Russian counterparties or aviation-related goods and services should review permitted activity and deadlines immediately.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 40A, 43A, 47, 48, and 49
summary: OFAC published five Russian sanctions general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorising specified transactions for civil aviation safety, divestment/transfer and wind-down activity, and other limited dealings. The licences were issued on 2022-08-02 and some expire between 2022-08-31 and 2023-01-31. Firms dealing with Russia-linked counterparties must confirm transactions fit the exact licence scope.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 38A and 50
summary: OFAC published two Russia-related general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 38A authorizes certain pension-payment transactions and replaces GL 38, while GL 50 authorizes closing individual accounts at blocked financial institutions and transferring remaining funds, subject to limits. Effective 2022-08-19; no expiry date is stated.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8, 8A, 8B, and 8C
summary: OFAC published web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize certain energy-related transactions involving specified Russian banks and, in GL 8A, the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, through 2022-06-24; GL 8C expires 2022-12-05. Firms dealing with Russia-related transactions should check whether activity falls within the limited authorisations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, and 30
summary: OFAC published eleven general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing limited wind-down and other sanctioned activities for specified Russian entities and transactions. The licenses include expiry dates ranging from April 13, 2022 to October 20, 2022 and must be checked against sanctions screening and transaction handling. This affects U.S. persons and firms dealing with sanctioned counterparties.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 1A, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7
summary: OFAC published several general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities sanctions program, including licenses authorizing specified transactions involving named Russian entities and replacing/superseding earlier licenses. These licenses affect sanctions screening and transaction handling for U.S.-sanctioned activity and should be applied immediately where relevant.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 9, 9A, 9B, 9C, 10, 10A, 10B, 10C, 11, and 12
summary: OFAC published the text of General Licenses 9, 9A, 9B, 9C, 10, 10A, 10B, 10C, 11 and 12 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize certain otherwise prohibited Russia-related transactions, mainly involving specified debt/equity and related settlement activity, subject to stated expiry dates. Firms dealing with Russia sanctions must confirm whether any permitted activity is still within the relevant license period.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 14, 15, 16, 17, 17A, 18, 19, and 20
summary: OFAC published eight general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize or carve out certain Russia-related transactions, including clearing and settlement activity, dealings with certain blocked Usmanov entities, and limited imports of specified Russian-origin energy and coal products under pre-existing contracts, subject to stated conditions and expirations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination
summary: OFAC published a determination under Executive Order 14068 making imports of Russian Federation-origin gold into the United States prohibited, subject to existing law and any OFAC licence or authorization. The measure took effect on publication of the determination on OFAC’s website.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-05: Debt Collection and Consumer Reporting Practices Involving Invalid Nursing Home Debts
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining that debt collection and consumer reporting practices tied to nursing home debts invalid under the Nursing Home Reform Act can violate the FDCPA and FCRA. It does not itself create new requirements, but signals enforcement risk for firms involved in collecting or furnishing information on such debts.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: documents
summary: HM Treasury’s Growth Plan 2022 is a policy paper setting out the government’s economic and tax agenda, including energy support, investment zones and planned tax cuts. It is primarily informational for firms and does not itself create binding regulatory requirements, though it signals future tax and market policy changes. No firm-specific action date is stated in the document excerpt.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Stamp Duty Land Tax
summary: HMT published a factsheet explaining announced changes to Stamp Duty Land Tax in England and Northern Ireland as part of the 2022 Growth Plan. It is an explanatory policy paper and does not itself set out the legal change or any compliance deadline.

title: The Growth Plan: Factsheet on cancellation of National Insurance rise and Health and Social Care Levy
summary: The UK government confirmed legislation to cancel the April 2022 National Insurance rise and the planned April 2023 Health and Social Care Levy. This affects UK employers and payroll/payments processes and takes effect through the introduced legislation, rather than through guidance or consultation.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Investment Zones
summary: HMT published a factsheet on proposed Investment Zones under the Growth Plan 2022. It describes early discussions with local authorities and the government’s intention to use lower taxes and planning changes to encourage development and business investment across the UK. It does not create any direct obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Corporation Tax
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet explaining the Chancellor’s announcement that the UK Corporation Tax rise would be cancelled. It is an informational policy paper, not the tax change itself. No action date or compliance deadline is set in this document.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Income Tax
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet explaining the Chancellor’s announced changes to the Basic and Additional Rates of Income Tax in the Growth Plan 2022. It is an informational policy paper only and does not itself create or change obligations for firms. No action date is set in the document.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License M and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations General Licenses M, M-1 and M-2, which authorize certain online graduate educational services and related software exports for specified Iranian students. GL M-2 replaced M-1 and expires on 2023-09-01. Firms with Iran-related sanctions exposure should confirm activity stays within the license terms and expiration date.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8 and 8A
summary: OFAC published two general licenses under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations. GL 8 and GL 8A authorize certain humanitarian trade transactions involving the Central Bank of Iran, and GL 8A also covers the National Iranian Oil Company and entities it controls. Firms dealing in sanctioned goods or payments must check the scope and limits of the licenses immediately.

title: Statement on Competition and Innovation
summary: The CFPB rescinds its No-Action Letter Policy and Compliance Assistance Sandbox Policy, effective 2022-09-30, because the PRA authorization expired and will not be renewed. Firms can no longer submit new applications under those policies from that date, though Trial Disclosure Policy requests continue to be accepted and existing submissions will be notified of any further action.

title: Treasury Minutes – September 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s September 2022 Treasury Minute is the government’s response to Public Accounts Committee reports on several non-financial policy topics, including child maintenance, secure training centres, the British Steel Pension Scheme, and the police uplift programme. It sets out whether departments accept recommendations and their planned follow-up actions, with some target implementation dates in 2023 and spring 2024. It does not create financial-services obligations.

title: Central African Republic Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC has finalized and reissued the Central African Republic Sanctions Regulations, effective 2022-09-29. The rule updates the consolidated sanctions text with additional definitions, interpretive guidance, general licenses and other provisions for persons subject to U.S. sanctions compliance requirements.

title: Regulation Crowdfunding, General Rules and Regulations
summary: This CFR correction updates Regulation Crowdfunding disclosure rules in 17 CFR Part 227 by adding a paragraph to § 227.201. It applies to issuers using Regulation Crowdfunding and affects written communications and broadcast scripts covered by the rule. The correction is effective as published in the CFR correction notice.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License D-2
summary: OFAC published General License D-2 under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain internet communications services, software, hardware and related services for Iran, subject to stated restrictions. It replaced GL D-1 and is effective from its issuance on 2022-09-23. Firms with sanctions exposure to Iran should assess permitted transactions and update controls.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 3 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published web general licenses and their subsequent iterations under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations, including expired GLs 3 through 3G and GL 3H. The licenses authorize specified transactions and financing involving certain Venezuela-related bonds. This is relevant for sanctioned-transaction screening and handling of Venezuela exposures, with no new deadline stated in the text.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 9 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published previously issued Venezuela sanctions general licenses, including expired GLs 9 through 9F and GL 9G, under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified dealings in certain PdVSA-related debt and certain bonds, subject to limits. This is relevant to firms handling Venezuela-related payments, securities, custody, or trade flows and sanctions screening.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related Rule 301 amendments, effective 2022-10-13. The update aligns filing instructions and submission types with prior EDGAR system releases and electronic-filing requirements, including Form 13F confidential treatment requests, certain Advisers Act applications, and Form 144 electronic filing. Filers subject to SEC electronic submission rules should use the updated manual immediately.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determinations
summary: OFAC published two Russia sanctions determinations: one adds the Russian quantum computing sector to sectoral sanctions under E.O. 14024, and the other prohibits certain quantum computing services to persons in Russia under E.O. 14071. The services prohibition takes effect on 2022-10-15; the sectoral determination took effect on publication.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13B
summary: OFAC published General License 13B under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain day-to-day administrative transactions for U.S. persons and their controlled entities in Russia, including some taxes, fees, import duties, and permits, through 2022-12-07. It replaces General License 13A and does not authorize dealings otherwise prohibited with blocked persons or certain Russian state accounts.

title: Advisory Committee
summary: HM Treasury publishes a policy paper describing the Advisory Committee’s advisory role and membership in relation to government credit-risk assessments and bespoke financial interventions under the Energy Markets Financing Scheme. It is informational only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Economic Advisory Council – Terms of Reference
summary: HM Treasury publishes the Terms of Reference for a new Economic Advisory Council of external experts announced by the Chancellor. It is informational only and does not create requirements for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2022
summary: Minutes and agenda for an HMT user and preparer advisory group meeting on government financial reporting, including updates on central and local government reporting, thematic reviews, sustainability reporting, IPSASB/ICAEW and IFRS 17. This is informational only and does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: Joint Statement: UK – U.S. Covered Agreement. Second meeting on the Joint Committee
summary: HM Treasury, the US Treasury and the USTR issued a joint statement on the second meeting of the UK-U.S. Covered Agreement Joint Committee. It summarises discussion topics between the two governments on prudential measures for insurance and reinsurance; it does not create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Fair Credit Reporting; Facially False Data
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion stating that consumer reporting agencies that fail to use reasonable internal controls to prevent facially false or logically inconsistent data from appearing in consumer reports are not using reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy under the FCRA. It is effective October 26, 2022.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-06: Unanticipated Overdraft Fee Assessment Practices
summary: The CFPB issued Circular 2022-06 stating that unanticipated overdraft fee practices can be unfair under the CFPA even where a firm complies with TILA, EFTA, Regulation Z and Regulation E. Banks and credit unions offering overdraft programs should review fee assessment practices, especially APSN-style transactions, for alignment with UDAAP expectations.

title: Treasury Minutes – November 2022
summary: This Treasury Minutes document is the UK government’s response to Public Accounts Committee reports on COVID-19 vaccination, PPE contracts and Randox contracts. It sets out the government’s views and actions on those issues, but does not itself create new obligations for firms. No compliance deadline is set for regulated entities.

title: Bulletin 2022-06: Unfair Returned Deposited Item Fee Assessment Practices
summary: CFPB issued a compliance bulletin saying blanket returned deposited item fee practices are likely unfair under the CFPA. It says the Bureau will use its enforcement and supervisory discretion accordingly and will not seek monetary relief for potentially unfair practices assessed before 2023-11-01. Applicable immediately to covered depository institutions and similar regulated entities.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: documents
summary: This is the UK Autumn Statement 2022, a government fiscal policy and economic update. It announces tax and spending measures, including changes affecting business taxation and public spending, but it is not itself a regulatory rule, supervisory notice, or binding obligation for firms.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Energy Taxes Factsheet
summary: The UK government’s Autumn Statement factsheet announces changes to the Energy Profits Levy and the introduction of an Electricity Generator Tax. It is aimed at energy companies and sets out tax changes announced on 17 November 2022. As a fiscal measure with immediate policy effect, it is binding for affected UK taxpayers from the stated Autumn Statement date.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Business Rates Factsheet
summary: This UK government factsheet describes the Autumn Statement 2022 business rates support package worth £13.6 billion. It is informational only and does not itself create or change any obligations for firms. The note refers to business rates bills from 1 April 2023, but sets out no new compliance requirements in the document itself.

title: Terms of Reference: Review of the Energy Bill Relief Scheme
summary: HM Treasury publishes terms of reference for a review of the Energy Bill Relief Scheme, setting out the review’s context, scope, governance and timetable for reporting. It does not create or change obligations for firms.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Cost of living support Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury’s factsheet explains the Autumn Statement 2022 cost-of-living support for households, including income support, energy bill help, benefits uprating, and tax and wage changes. It is informational only and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-07: Reasonable Investigation of Consumer Reporting Disputes
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining how the FCRA applies to consumer reporting agencies and furnishers handling consumer disputes. It says they cannot impose extra hurdles to submitting disputes, and they must provide relevant dispute information to furnishers. It is an interpretive circular, not a new rule, and has no stated compliance date.

title: Minutes of the Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes: 6 October 2022
summary: HMT published minutes of the UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes, describing the committee’s meeting under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is informational only and does not itself change VAT, tax recovery, or fraud-cooperation requirements.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on the United Kingdom-Singapore FinTech Bridge
summary: The UK and Singapore signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen cooperation on FinTech policy, regulator-to-regulator engagement, and business-to-business support. It sets out quarterly discussions, sharing of FinTech developments, and possible joint innovation projects, but creates no enforceable obligations. It takes effect on signature and is intended to support future collaboration rather than impose new requirements.

title: EM on EU regulation 389/2012 (13979/22, COM(2022)539)
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU proposal to amend Regulation 389/2012 on excise-duty information exchange and notes it would extend data sharing to duty-paid movements. It says the change would not create new business obligations and is relevant to Northern Ireland under the Protocol. The proposal was expected to take effect from 13 February 2023, but this EM itself imposes no requirements.

title: Publication of Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5, 6, and 7 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published nine web general licenses and their later iterations under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations for transactions related to the Panamanian seizure of Balboa Bank & Trust. The licenses were already available on OFAC’s website and are now expired, but they also include a reporting requirement for U.S. persons within 10 business days while they were in effect.

title: Publication of Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations Web General License 1A and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published three General Licenses under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations for the wind-down and liquidation of Banco Continental, S.A. The licenses are now expired, but they showed a time-limited authorization, restrictions on unblocking and other dealings, and a reporting requirement for U.S. persons within 10 business days after wind-down activities end.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 53
summary: OFAC published General License 53 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes U.S. persons to carry out certain transactions needed for Russian diplomatic and consular missions, including employee compensation, subject to stated carve-outs. The license was issued on 2022-11-10 and published on 2022-12-01.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 51 and 52
summary: OFAC published General Licenses 51 and 52 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 51 authorizes certain wind-down transactions involving Aquarius through 2022-10-15; GL 52 authorizes specified journalistic and news-bureau transactions for U.S. persons, subject to stated exclusions. Firms must screen and apply the new sanctions permissions immediately.

title: Publication of Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations Web General License 4 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published eight General Licenses under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations, covering certain wind-down and related transactions involving Soho Panama, S.A. and the Panamanian mall/complex. The licenses were already issued in 2016–2017 and are now expired, but they include reporting requirements for U.S. persons that participated while they were effective.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 28A
summary: OFAC published General License 28A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving Transkapitalbank and Afghanistan and related correspondent account activity for U.S. financial institutions until 2023-01-18. It also supersedes General License 28. Firms dealing with sanctions-sensitive payments or correspondent banking should update screening and payment processing controls.

title: Publication of Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 2, 3, 3A, and 3B
summary: OFAC publishes four general licenses under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations, including expired licenses 2, 3, 3A and 3B. The licenses authorized limited transactions for specified Panama-based hotel and newspaper operations for stated periods and set conditions and exclusions. This is relevant to sanctions screening, transaction handling and blocked-property controls.

title: Environmental Impacts of Spending Review 2021
summary: HM Treasury published an analysis paper on the environmental impacts and ratings from Spending Review 2021, with supporting narrative on how it assesses environmental impacts and will improve its approach. It is informational and does not impose requirements on firms.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes progress report updating Parliament on the Government’s implementation of accepted Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across many prior sessions. It is an informational progress update, not a rule, supervision notice, or enforcement action. No direct obligations or deadlines are created for firms.

title: Ring-fencing reforms
summary: HM Treasury publishes its response to the independent review of ring-fencing and proprietary trading. It says the government intends to consult in mid-2023 on near-term reforms and to issue a call for evidence in Q1 2023 on aligning the ring-fencing and resolution regimes. This is an awareness paper, not a rule or consultation itself.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to the Public Accounts Committee across several topics, including waste crime, regulation after EU exit, whole-of-government accounts, electronic monitoring services, and local air quality breaches. It records government positions and implementation updates, but it does not itself create new regulatory requirements. No direct bank-specific obligation or deadline is set out.

title: Response to the remit and recommendations for the Financial Policy Committee: December 2022
summary: The FPC set out its response to HM Treasury’s remit letter and recommendations, updating its views on UK financial stability, banks’ resilience, market-based finance, LDI funds and energy market financing. It signals ongoing monitoring and future policy work, but does not itself create new binding requirements for firms.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the UK and the Republic of Chile
summary: HM Treasury published a UK-Chile memorandum of understanding on financial services collaboration. It is a policy paper describing cooperation to share best practices and developments in financial sector policy, regulation and pro-competitive practices, with no new binding obligations or deadlines.

title: Intent To Make Preemption Determination Under the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z)
summary: The CFPB published a request for comment and notice of intent to make a preemption determination under TILA/Regulation Z for a New York State commercial financing law, and may consider similar laws in California, Utah and Virginia. Comments are due by 2023-01-20. It is not yet a binding rule, but may affect state-law disclosure requirements for covered credit transactions.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 54
summary: OFAC published General License 54 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving VEON Ltd. debt or equity securities issued before 2022-06-06, and related clearing and settlement activities. Firms must still ensure no other RuHSR restrictions apply, including dealings with blocked persons. The licence was issued on 2022-11-18 and published on 2022-12-16.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination and Web General Licenses 55, 56, and 57
summary: OFAC published a sanctions determination and three general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The determination expands prohibited services for maritime transport of Russian-origin crude oil, with a price-cap carve-out and a transition period. GLs 55-57 authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions, including Sakhalin-2-related services, for stated periods.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General License 21
summary: OFAC published Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations General License 21, which authorizes limited safety, environmental, docking, crew safety and emergency repair transactions for specified blocked vessels and persons until 2022-12-15. Firms dealing with the named vessels or counterparties must ensure any permitted payments go to blocked accounts and avoid new commercial contracts, cargo offloading, or other prohibited dealings.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13C
summary: OFAC published General License 13C under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain tax, fee, import duty, permit, license, registration and certification payments for U.S. persons and entities they own or control, for ordinary day-to-day operations in Russia, through 2023-03-07. It supersedes General License 13B.

title: Joint statement by HM Treasury, the CMA, the FCA and the PSR to update on the future of Open Banking
summary: HM Treasury, the FCA, the CMA and the PSR issued a joint statement on the future of UK Open Banking. It outlines plans for a new long-term regulatory framework and a successor entity to the OBIE, with priorities around Open Banking payments, scale and sustainable funding. No binding requirements or deadlines are set.

title: Terms of reference for the review of regulation for emerging technologies
summary: HMT published terms of reference for a review of how the UK can better regulate emerging technologies. The review will be led by Sir Patrick Vallance and cover sectors including digital technology, life sciences, green industries, and later advanced manufacturing and creative industries. This is a scoping document only; it does not itself change any rules or deadlines.

title: Financial Inclusion Report 2021/22
summary: This is HM Treasury’s Financial Inclusion Report 2021/22, an informational policy paper summarising government progress and priorities on access to cash, banking, credit, insurance, fintech, vulnerability, savings and debt support. It does not itself create new obligations. It references the Financial Services and Markets Bill and related policy measures, but is not a rule or consultation.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update
summary: HM Treasury publishes a progress update on its Women in Finance Charter commitments, including its senior female representation as of March 2022 and future internal priorities. It is an informational policy paper for the Treasury’s own signatory commitments, with no new requirements for regulated firms.

title: Home Mortgage Disclosure (Regulation C); Judicial Vacatur of Coverage Threshold for Closed-End Mortgage Loans
summary: The CFPB issued a technical amendment to Regulation C to restore the closed-end HMDA reporting threshold to 25 loans in each of the two preceding calendar years, effective 2022-12-21, after a court vacated the 100-loan threshold. Banks, credit unions, savings associations and for-profit nondepository mortgage lenders in scope should use the reverted threshold for HMDA reporting.

title: Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination
summary: OFAC published a sanctions determination setting a $60 per barrel price cap on crude oil of Russian Federation origin under Executive Order 14071. It took effect on 2022-12-05 and applies to parties involved in the relevant Russia-related oil trade and services restrictions.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8D and 40C
summary: OFAC published two Russia sanctions general licenses, GL 8D and GL 40C, under 31 CFR part 587. GL 8D authorizes certain energy-related transactions involving specified Russian banks and the Central Bank of Russia through 2023-05-15; GL 40C authorizes certain civil-aviation-safety transactions for specified blocked entities. Firms dealing with Russia-linked activity should check the scope and exclusions immediately.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: January 2023
summary: HMT publishes economic evidence for the 2023-24 Pay Review Bodies pay round. It sets out inflation, GDP, labour market and fiscal context to inform public-sector pay recommendations; it does not create regulatory obligations for firms. No action date is specified beyond the January 2023 publication date.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 2, 4, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published Venezuela sanctions general licenses 1, 2, 2A, 4, 4A, 4B and 4C, which authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions and, for some licenses, require post-transaction reporting. U.S. persons relying on GL 1 must file a detailed report within 10 business days. The publication is relevant to persons dealing with Venezuela-related transactions and sanctioned entities such as CITGO and PDV Holding.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8K and 41
summary: OFAC published Venezuela general licences 8K and 41, authorising certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving PdVSA for named covered entities. GL 8K runs until 2023-05-26 and replaces GL 8J; GL 41 is also published as a web general licence and renews monthly for up to six months from each effective date or renewal.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 12, 13, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC republishes seven expired Venezuela general licenses (GLs 12, 13, 13A-13E) under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. The text shows the scope and expiry of authorizations for certain PdVSA/Nynas-related transactions and related blocked-account payment mechanics. It is relevant for sanctions screening, transaction handling and historical compliance with US Venezuela sanctions.

title: UK - US financial services co-operation – statement on the seventh meeting of the Financial Regulatory Working Group
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement on the seventh UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It summarises discussion topics and cooperation themes only; it does not create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Publication of Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 3 and 4
summary: OFAC published two Global Magnitsky general licenses authorizing limited wind-down, divestment, transfer, clearing and settlement activities involving Pingtan Marine Enterprise Ltd. and certain vessels through 2023-03-09. Firms dealing with sanctioned persons or blocked property must ensure any permitted payments go to blocked accounts and no new prohibited transactions are entered.

title: EM on EU regulation 282/2011 (COM(2022)704)
summary: HM Treasury explains EU proposals for VAT in the digital age, including changes to marketplace liability, OSS/IOSS, reverse charge, digital reporting and e-invoicing. It is an explanatory memorandum about proposed EU measures, with potential Northern Ireland impact, not a binding rule. No immediate action date is set because the proposals may change before adoption.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2023
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on public-sector decarbonisation, animal health infrastructure, energy supplier regulation, and DWP fraud/error. It records government responses and target implementation dates, but does not itself create or amend rules for firms. No direct compliance action is required from banks, beyond general awareness of government policy direction.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving Bitzlato
summary: FinCEN issued an order effective 2023-02-01 prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving Bitzlato, a non-US virtual asset service provider found to be of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance. Covered financial institutions and domestic financial institutions must stop the specified transactions from that date.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volumes I and II and related rule changes, effective 2023-01-24. Filers using EDGAR must follow the revised access and filing requirements, including who may sign Form ID and how title/position must be stated. The updated manual is incorporated by reference into the CFR.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: Autumn 2022 update
summary: The UK Charter for Budget Responsibility was updated in January 2023 and laid before Parliament. It restates the government’s fiscal objectives, debt and borrowing targets, welfare cap framework, and guidance to the OBR. It also sets out requirements for future amendments and publication of debt-management and Budget Report content.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2023-01: Unlawful Negative Option Marketing Practices
summary: The CFPB issued a circular stating that negative option marketing practices can violate the CFPA’s ban on unfair, deceptive or abusive acts or practices if sellers misstate terms, fail to get informed consent, or create unreasonable cancellation barriers. It is an enforcement/interpretive communication for market participants, not a new rule, and no compliance date is set.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5F and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published updated Venezuela general licenses 5F through 5J authorizing certain transactions, financing, and other dealings in Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% Bond on the stated dates. The latest iteration supersedes the prior one and remains subject to all other Venezuela sanctions restrictions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 6, 10, 11, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published Venezuela sanctions general licenses 6, 6A, 10, 10A and 11, including authorisations for certain blocked-person transactions and wind-down activities involving named Venezuelan entities. U.S. persons using the licences had reporting duties after licence expiry. This is an update to the sanctions authorisation framework, not a broader rulemaking.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 14, 15, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published on its website Venezuela general licenses 14, 15, 15A, 15B and 15C, which authorize specified transactions otherwise prohibited under Venezuela sanctions. The licenses affect certain US government business and certain payment/card/remittance activities involving named Venezuelan banks, and are relevant immediately to sanctions screening and transaction handling.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for Threat-LED Penetration Testing
summary: G7 issued non-binding fundamental elements for threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) for financial-sector authorities, entities and service providers. The paper sets out principles for scoping, resourcing, testing, information sharing and remediation, and encourages cross-border coordination for multinational entities. It does not itself impose obligations or deadlines, but authorities may use it to shape local TLPT regimes.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements of ransomware resilience for the financial sector
summary: G7 published non-binding high-level guidance on ransomware resilience for financial entities and their critical third-party providers. It sets out governance, cybersecurity and business continuity considerations, including board oversight and sanctions awareness, but does not impose legal requirements or a deadline. Firms can use it as a reference for strengthening cyber and operational resilience.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for third party cyber risk management in the financial sector
summary: G7 revised its non-binding fundamental elements for third-party cyber risk management in the financial sector. The update adds a stronger focus on ICT supply chain risk and a new element on third-party cyber risk, intended as guidance for entities and authorities rather than a binding rule. No compliance deadline is set.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for Effective Assessment of Cybersecurity in the financial sector
summary: The G7 publishes non-binding fundamental elements for assessing cybersecurity in the financial sector. It sets out desirable outcomes and assessment components to help firms, supervisors and assessors evaluate cyber maturity, board oversight, and resilience. It does not create mandatory requirements or dates.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for third party cyber risk management in the financial sector 24.10.2018
summary: This G7 policy paper sets out non-binding fundamental elements for managing third-party cyber risk in the financial sector, including governance, due diligence, monitoring, incident response, contingency planning and cross-sector coordination. It is aimed at financial sector entities and authorities as guidance for tailoring local policy and controls, with no compliance date or direct legal obligation.

title: Chancellor and Minister for Local Government and Building Safety commission new study on infrastructure planning
summary: The Chancellor commissioned the National Infrastructure Commission to study infrastructure planning, especially the role of National Policy Statements. The document sets the study’s terms of reference and says the NIC will deliver a final report by spring 2023. It does not itself change any rules or obligations.

title: Determination Regarding Excepted Real Estate Foreign States
summary: Treasury determined that New Zealand and the United Kingdom qualify as excepted real estate foreign states under CFIUS rules, effective 2023-02-10. This affects investment-security screening for relevant real estate transactions involving those countries and remains in place until further notice.

title: Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (Regulation X); Digital Mortgage Comparison-Shopping Platforms and Related Payments to Operators
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion explaining how RESPA section 8 applies to digital mortgage comparison-shopping platforms. Operators may violate the anti-kickback/referral fee rules if they steer consumers using non-neutral ranking or placement in return for payments. It is effective immediately on 2023-02-13 and affects platform operators and mortgage-related settlement service providers.

title: Determination Regarding Excepted Foreign States
summary: Treasury determined that the United Kingdom and New Zealand are ‘excepted foreign states’ for CFIUS purposes, effective 2023-02-10. This affects foreign investment screening status under the U.S. investment security regime and remains in place unless CFIUS acts again.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 31B
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 31B, which authorizes certain U.S. persons to transact with specified Venezuelan National Assembly-related persons and entities, and replaces General License 31A. It is effective from 2023-01-09. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related counterparties should check sanctions screening and transaction permissions immediately.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 16, 17, 18, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC republishes seven Venezuela general licenses covering certain transactions with specified Venezuelan banks and personal remittances, including successive replacements of earlier licenses. The licenses authorize activity through stated expiry dates and set conditions and exclusions for U.S. financial institutions and others dealing with blocked persons. Firms must check whether any Venezuela-related activity is covered before relying on these licenses.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 21A and 21B
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 21A and 21B under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, authorizing limited safety, crew welfare, emergency repair, and environmental mitigation transactions for specified blocked vessels and related persons. GL 21A was effective until 2023-01-14 and was superseded by GL 21B, which runs until 2023-04-13. Firms dealing with the named vessels or persons must follow the license limits.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 6C, 28B, and 54A
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 6C, 28B and 54A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified Russia-related transactions, including certain agricultural, medical and COVID-19-related dealings, and wind-down/rejection activity involving TKB entities and Afghanistan, with effective dates from 2023-01-17. Firms dealing with Russia, sanctioned parties or cross-border payments should update sanctions screening and procedures.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, and 28
summary: OFAC published six Venezuela general licenses that authorize specified transactions and exports involving the Government of Venezuela, including telecoms, mail, internet communications, diplomatic/consular funds transfers, and certain oilfield-related activities. These licenses were previously issued on OFAC’s website and are effective as stated in the individual licenses; one listed license had already expired.

title: Autumn Budget and Spending Review 2021: documents
summary: This is the UK Autumn Budget and Spending Review 2021, a government policy document setting out fiscal plans, spending allocations and tax/economic measures. It is an intelligence publication rather than a rule, and it does not itself create compliance deadlines for firms. Financial institutions should review the budget measures for downstream legislative or tax impacts.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to Public Accounts Committee reports on several departmental topics, including children’s social care, accounting officer assessments, housing, workforce skills and government property. It sets out responses and target implementation dates for follow-up actions, but it does not itself create financial-services regulatory obligations.

title: Annual Information Return/Reports
summary: The US Departments of Labor and Treasury, plus PBGC, issued final revisions to Form 5500 and Form 5500-SF annual return/report forms and instructions for employee benefit plans. The changes apply to plan years beginning on or after 2023-01-01 and affect reporting by pension and welfare benefit plans, plan sponsors, administrators and service providers subject to ERISA and the Code.

title: Publication of Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5 and 6
summary: OFAC published two Global Magnitsky general licenses authorizing limited divestment, settlement and wind-down transactions involving specified sanctioned entities. The authorizations run until 2023-03-27 and exclude other blocked persons unless separately authorized. Sanctions screening and payment processing teams should apply the licenses immediately.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2021 to June 2022
summary: HM Treasury published annual statistics on basic bank accounts for July 2021 to June 2022. It reports account openings, closures, upgrades and refusals at the nine UK designated providers under the Payment Account Regulations, and notes FCA supervision of compliance. It does not itself change rules or deadlines.

title: Publication of Nicaragua Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 3 and 4
summary: OFAC published the text of Nicaragua Sanctions Regulations General Licenses 3 and 4. Both licenses were already issued and are now expired; they had temporarily authorized wind-down transactions involving specified Nicaraguan mining entities through July 18, 2022 and November 23, 2022, respectively. No new permissions are created by this publication.

title: Order Designating the Unique Product Identifier and Product Classification System To Be Used in Recordkeeping and Swap Data Reporting
summary: The CFTC designated Derivatives Service Bureau unique product identifiers and product classification system for swaps in the credit, equity, foreign exchange and interest rate asset classes. Registered entities and swap counterparties must use these identifiers for certain swap recordkeeping and data reporting requirements. The order is effective February 24, 2023.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 19, 20, 21, 22, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published on its website Venezuela general licenses 19, 20, 20A, 20B, 21 and 22, which authorize specified transactions involving Banco Central de Venezuela, the Government of Venezuela, and certain international organizations. These licenses are relevant to sanctioned-activity screening and transaction processing for firms dealing with Venezuela. The text confirms the licenses and their scope; no separate action date beyond the stated issue dates is created here.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 36, 36A, 37, 38, and 39
summary: OFAC published web general licenses for the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations, covering wind-down or other authorised activities involving specified blocked persons and vessels. The licenses are time-limited, with some already expired or superseded, and include restrictions on dealings with blocked persons and U.S. financial institutions. Sanctions teams should confirm current licence status before relying on them.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 56A and 57A
summary: OFAC published General Licenses 56A and 57A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 56A authorizes certain services for EU-related crude oil and petroleum products transactions into Bulgaria, Croatia and landlocked EU member states; GL 57A authorizes certain vessel-emergency services. Both replace prior licenses and are effective from 2023-02-03.

title: Terms of reference for the independent review of university spin-outs
summary: HMT published terms of reference for an independent review of university spin-outs. The review will consult universities, investors and founders and compare the UK’s approach with other regimes to identify best practice. It is an informational policy paper and does not itself create obligations.

title: Spring Budget 2023 customs measures
summary: HMRC/HMT published a policy paper setting out Spring Budget 2023 customs measures to simplify import and export processes. It explains the package and proposes further customs reform ideas, informed by a prior call for evidence. It does not itself create binding requirements or set a compliance date.

title: Investment Zones
summary: HM Treasury’s March 2023 policy paper sets out the government’s proposed Investment Zones policy offer and framework for selected areas in England and the devolved administrations. It is an overview and invitation to develop local proposals around priority sectors, not a binding rule or consultation with a stated close date. No direct compliance deadline is created for firms.

title: Spring Budget 2023 – Disability White Paper Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet summarising disability reforms announced in the Health and Disability White Paper. It is a policy/communications document only and does not create regulatory obligations for firms. No action date or compliance deadline is stated.

title: Enterprise Management Incentives Call for Evidence: Summary of Responses
summary: HM Treasury publishes a summary of responses to its Enterprise Management Incentives call for evidence. It reports stakeholder views on the EMI tax-advantaged employee share scheme and says the government will consider next steps. No new requirements, deadlines, or rules are introduced.

title: Government response to the 2022 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report discusses the UK government’s fiscal strategy, debt and borrowing outlook, and measures to manage public finances. It is informational only and does not create binding requirements for firms. No compliance date or direct obligation is set for banks or other regulated firms.

title: Spring Budget 2023 Factsheet: Cutting & Simplifying Tax for Businesses to Invest and Grow
summary: HMT published a Spring Budget 2023 factsheet on tax measures for businesses, covering capital allowances, R&D support and tax simplification for SMEs. It is informational only and does not itself create obligations or deadlines.

title: Spring Budget 2023 – Labour Market Factsheet
summary: This HM Treasury factsheet explains labour market measures announced in Spring Budget 2023, aimed at helping people enter work, increase hours and work longer. It is informational only and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Digital Technologies
summary: HM Government’s review sets out recommendations for a more pro-innovation UK approach to digital technologies, including AI, data access, autonomous vehicles, drones, cyber security, and space/satellite. It is a policy report, not a binding rule, and points to possible future legislation and further policy work rather than immediate obligations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination
summary: OFAC published a sanctions sector determination applying Executive Order 14024 blocking sanctions to persons operating in Russia’s metals and mining sector. It took effect on 2023-02-24 and expands the sectoral sanctions exposure for firms dealing with Russian counterparties or activities.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8E, 58, and 59
summary: OFAC published web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain Russia-related transactions and wind-down/rejection activity, including with Rosbank and specified energy-related entities. The licenses were issued on 2022-12-15, and some had time-limited expiries or were superseded. U.S. persons and financial institutions dealing with Russia-related sanctions should check the precise scope and end dates.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8F, 13D, 60, and 61
summary: OFAC published web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited Russia-related transactions for limited periods and purposes. GL 8F covers certain energy-related transactions through 2023-05-16; GL 13D permits some routine administrative transactions through 2023-06-06; GLs 60 and 61 were also published. Sanctions teams must check scope, expiry and any superseded licenses.

title: Spring Budget 2023
summary: The UK government’s Spring Budget 2023 sets out fiscal and policy measures, including changes to energy support, fuel duty, childcare and labour-market training. It is a budget speech/report rather than a binding regulatory instrument, though it may signal future legislative or policy changes. No direct compliance deadline is created in this publication itself.

title: Bulletin 2023-01: Unfair Billing and Collection Practices After Bankruptcy Discharges of Certain Student Loan Debts
summary: The CFPB issued a compliance bulletin and policy guidance warning student-loan servicers not to bill or collect on private education loans that were discharged in bankruptcy. It applies immediately from 2023-03-23 and says CFPB examiners will scrutinize servicing practices and expect remedial action, including lookbacks and refunds, where firms wrongly resumed collection after discharge orders.

title: Joint HM Treasury and FCA statement on the Criminal Market Abuse Regime
summary: HM Treasury and the FCA say they have completed a review of the UK criminal market abuse regime and identified areas where it should be updated. This is an informational policy statement about potential future changes, with no new rules, obligations or dates in force.

title: Distilled Spirits Plants
summary: This CFR correction republishes a text fix to 27 CFR Part 19 for distilled spirits plants. The corrected rule states that a proprietor must prepay tax when a withdrawal would push outstanding tax liability above bond coverage limits. It is an editorial/technical correction, effective as part of the CFR update rather than a new policy change.

title: General Rules and Regulations, Securities Act of 1933
summary: This SEC/Office of the Federal Register correction updates two Securities Act rules in 17 CFR Part 230 by fixing editorial text in §§ 230.482 and 230.498. It affects SEC-regulated securities offering disclosures and related prospectus materials. There is no substantive policy change, but firms should note the corrected codified text as of the publication date.

title: Regulation S-T-General Rules and Regulations for Electronic Filings
summary: This CFR correction republished an SEC Regulation S-T definition, reinstating the term “Interactive Data Financial Report” in 17 CFR Part 232. It applies to SEC electronic filing requirements and is effective as a codified text correction rather than a new policy change.

title: Income Taxes
summary: This CFR correction updates Title 26, Part 1 to fix an editorial/technical error in the income tax regulations, specifically the temporary partner distributive share provision in § 1.704-1T. It applies to tax rulebook codification rather than introducing new substantive requirements.

title: Publication of Syria Web General License 23
summary: OFAC published Syria General License 23, authorizing certain earthquake-relief transactions otherwise prohibited by the Syrian Sanctions Regulations through 2023-08-08. U.S. financial institutions and U.S.-registered money transmitters may rely on originators for funds transfers within the license, subject to sanctions-screening limits and other exclusions.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2023-24
summary: This is a statutory report to Parliament under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 setting out the Royal Trustees’ determination of the Sovereign Grant for 2023-24 and how it was calculated. It does not impose obligations on regulated firms. It is relevant only as a public-law/UK government finance publication, with no direct compliance deadline for banks.

title: Treasury Minutes – March 2023
summary: Treasury Minutes is HM Treasury’s government response to several Public Accounts Committee reports. It records the government’s replies to recommendations on topics including sport participation, HMRC performance, the UK Infrastructure Bank, integrated care systems and defence digital strategy. It does not itself create new rules or obligations for firms.

title: HM Treasury Evaluation Strategy
summary: HM Treasury sets out its overall strategy for using evaluation in policy-making and for supporting evaluation across government. It is an internal policy paper with no firm-facing rules, obligations, or deadlines.

title: General Rules and Regulations, Securities Exchange Act of 1934
summary: The SEC published a CFR correction to 17 CFR Part 240, reinstating omitted text in Rule 13e-100 for Schedule 13E-3 filing/signature instructions under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. This is an editorial technical fix, not a substantive policy change, but it affects firms using this filing form from publication onward.

title: Terms of reference for the review of foreign direct investment
summary: HMT published terms of reference for a review of how the UK can attract more foreign direct investment into key growth sectors, led by Lord Harrington. It is an information-only policy paper; it does not itself create obligations or set deadlines for firms.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Green Industries
summary: HM Government’s response to the Vallance review on green industries says it accepts all recommendations and will work with regulators on capacity, planning and grid-connection reforms. It signals future actions and an upcoming action plan, but this publication itself does not create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 29, 30, 30A, 31, and 31A
summary: OFAC published five Venezuela general licenses in the Federal Register, reflecting authorizations for certain transactions involving the Government of Venezuela, mainly for NGOs and humanitarian, democracy, education, development, and environmental activities. The licenses are already available on OFAC’s website and are part of the Venezuela sanctions regime; firms dealing with Venezuela should assess whether their activity falls within the authorizations and conditions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 32, 33, 34, 34A, and 35
summary: OFAC published five Venezuela sanctions general licenses that had previously appeared on its website. The licenses authorize certain Venezuela-related transactions, including personal maintenance for U.S. persons in Venezuela, overflight and air ambulance services, and some dealings involving specified Government of Venezuela persons. They affect U.S. persons and other persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction and are effective from the stated issue dates in 2019.

title: Green finance strategy
summary: The UK Treasury’s Green Finance Strategy sets out the government’s policy direction for mobilising green investment, transition planning, a UK green taxonomy, nature markets and support for green finance in emerging markets. It is a strategic policy paper, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice, so it does not itself create binding obligations. Firms may want to track the announced next steps.

title: Publication of Libyan Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5, 6, and 8A.
summary: OFAC published three Libyan sanctions general licenses (5, 6 and 8A) and revoked them from its website. The text restates the permissions and reporting conditions for U.S. persons and transactions involving Libya-related parties, including a 30-day report requirement for certain oil, gas or petroleum transactions. This is relevant for any firm or person transacting in Libya-linked assets or with sanctioned persons.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Committee of the Whole House
summary: A UK Finance Bill amendment changes the multinational top-up tax calculation rules by removing an unnecessary step in clause 174. It affects the new multinational top-up tax regime and is intended to ensure covered tax allocations work as intended. No separate compliance date is stated in the text.

title: Recommendations for the next phase of open banking in the UK
summary: HMT, via the Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee, published recommendations and a 29-action roadmap for the next phase of UK open banking. It sets out a two-year plan to support a more sustainable, scalable ecosystem and greater use of open banking payments and data sharing, but it does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Economic Advisory Council – Terms of Reference – April 2023
summary: HM Treasury publishes an update to the Terms of Reference for the Chancellor’s Economic Advisory Council, which provides independent advice on economic policy. It is informational only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: India-UK 2nd Financial Markets Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury published a joint statement on the second India-UK Financial Markets Dialogue. It describes bilateral discussions between government and regulators on sustainable finance, insurance, asset management, capital markets, payments and cryptoassets. It does not create or change any rules, deadlines or obligations.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted amendments updating the EDGAR Filer Manual and related filing rules, effective 2023-04-20. The changes affect filers submitting electronically to EDGAR, including new XBRL taxonomies, updated tagging for compensation and trading disclosures, revised Form 144 filing hours, and a new checkbox for Form 13F-CTR/A.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 62, 63, 64, and 65
summary: OFAC published four general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. They authorize limited wind-down, divestment, transfer, and related transaction activity involving specified Russian persons and related debt, equity, and derivatives, with some permissions expiring on 2023-07-11. Sanctions teams, payments, and operations should confirm whether any activity is covered and any blocked-account handling is required.

title: Publication of Syrian Sanctions Regulations Web General License 22
summary: OFAC published Syrian Sanctions Regulations General License 22, authorizing certain transactions and funds transfers connected to specified economic sectors in non-regime-held areas of northeast and northwest Syria. U.S. financial institutions and registered money transmitters may rely on originators under stated conditions. The license was issued on 2022-05-12 and republished on 2023-04-26.

title: Interagency Policy Statement on Allowances for Credit Losses (Revised April 2023)
summary: The OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC and NCUA revised their interagency policy statement on allowances for credit losses to remove references to troubled debt restructurings and align it with updated U.S. GAAP. It applies to supervised depository institutions and credit unions using CECL. The statement was issued on 2023-04-27 and is effective immediately as published.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2021-22
summary: HM Treasury publishes examples of best practice for government annual reports and accounts for 2021-22, focusing on performance, accountability and financial information. It is guidance-only and aimed at entities preparing ARAs across government, with no new legal or reporting requirements. The paper points to the Government Financial Reporting Review and the 2022-23 FReM as context.

title: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (Regulation F); Time-Barred Debt
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion stating that the FDCPA and Regulation F prohibit debt collectors from suing or threatening to sue to collect time-barred debt, including in state court foreclosure actions on time-barred mortgage debt. It is effective May 1, 2023 and applies to debt collectors covered by the FDCPA and Regulation F.

title: Joint Statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 10 May 2023
summary: This is a joint statement from the UK and European Commission noting progress on Financial Provisions work streams related to invoices sent by the EU to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is informational only and does not create or change any firm obligations.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Public Bill Committee
summary: A Finance Bill amendment would expand the exceptions to the trustee income tax de minimis rules in ITA 2007 by excluding certain pension funds from the reduction calculation. It affects trusts holding registered pension schemes, superannuation funds and certain occupational pension schemes. No action date is stated in the text.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2023
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on education, NHS backlogs, excess votes, COVID support schemes and DVLA backlogs. It records government responses and target implementation dates such as December 2023 for final evaluations of CJRS and SEISS, but does not itself change rules for firms.

title: Publication of Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations Web General License 7
summary: OFAC published Global Magnitsky Sanctions General License 7, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving TABESA, Tabacos USA Inc. and related entities when ordinary and necessary for payments under the Tobacco Master Settlement Agreement. It does not authorize other blocked-person transactions. The license was issued on 2023-03-31 and published on 2023-05-17.

title: Conflict, Stability and Security Fund: Counter Terrorism Programme Fund programme summaries 2021 to 2022
summary: This is a policy paper publishing annual summaries of UK Conflict, Stability and Security Fund counter-terrorism programmes for 2021 to 2022. It describes the programmes, lead departments, budgets, length and intended outcomes, but does not create requirements for firms. No action date applies.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License O
summary: OFAC published General License O under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Executive Order 13846. It authorizes certain wind-down, docking, crew-safety, emergency repair and environmental mitigation transactions for specified blocked vessels and related entities through 2023-06-30, with blocked payments to be made into blocked accounts and reported to OFAC. New contracts and offloading Iranian-origin petroleum remain prohibited.

title: Technical Amendments to Form BD and Form BDW
summary: The SEC made technical amendments to Form BD and Form BDW, updating the list of SROs and jurisdictions, including Guam, and conforming the definition of “jurisdiction.” The changes are effective immediately on 2023-05-23 and affect broker-dealer registration and withdrawal filings.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2023-02: Reopening Deposit Accounts That Consumers Previously Closed
summary: The CFPB issued a circular stating that a financial institution’s unilateral reopening of a consumer deposit account after closure can be an unfair act or practice under the CFPA, and may also be deceptive or abusive depending on the circumstances. It is an enforcement-oriented interpretation with no new compliance date.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Life Sciences and the government response
summary: This is a UK government review and response on how regulation should better support life sciences innovation, including medicines, devices, AI/digital tools, engineering biology and novel foods. It recommends future policy and regulator improvements, but does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Financial Services & Markets Bill – Overseas Central Counterparties
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper explaining two technical amendments to the Financial Services and Markets Bill on overseas central counterparties. The changes would help UK firms continue using certain non-UK CCPs after the CCP run-off regime exit date of 1 July 2023, if Parliament approves them.

title: Publication of Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 1 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC published web text for four general licenses under its cyber-related, non-proliferation and hostages/wrongfully detained sanctions programs. The licenses authorize limited transactions with the FSB and related activities, while preserving key prohibitions. Sanctions teams and operations should use the current license text for screening and permitted-dealing decisions; this is effective as published and reflects prior issuances.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8G
summary: OFAC published General License 8G under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It temporarily authorises certain energy-related transactions involving named Russian banks and the Central Bank of the Russian Federation through 2023-11-01, replacing GL 8F. Firms must check whether their Russian-related activity falls within the licence or remains prohibited.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – June 2023
summary: UK Treasury progress report updating Parliament on how the Government has implemented accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across multiple sessions. It is an accountability/status publication only, with no new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13E, 66, 67, and 68
summary: OFAC published four web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize limited transactions, including certain administrative payments, wind-down activity, and divestment or settlement transactions involving Public Joint Stock Company Polyus, with expiry dates in August 2023 and July 2023 for one license. U.S. persons and entities they own or control should check scope and expiry before acting.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License 2 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC republished Belarus sanctions general licenses 2 and 2A through 2H. The licenses authorize certain transactions involving named Belarusian entities and require U.S. persons to file a report within 15 days after transactions over $10,000 under the license. Firms dealing with Belarus-linked persons or property should confirm whether any activity is covered and whether reporting is due.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License 1 and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC republishes Belarus Sanctions general licenses 1, 1-A, 1-B, 1-C and 1-D, which authorize certain U.S. person transactions with two named Belarusian blocked entities for specified periods. The publication is informational but reflects sanctions permissions and limits relevant to firms dealing with U.S. persons or sanctioned parties.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7
summary: OFAC published Belarus Sanctions Regulations web general licenses 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, which authorize specified transactions and wind-down activities involving certain Belarusian persons and entities. These licenses affect sanctioned-party screening, transaction processing and sanctions controls for US persons and others subject to the Belarus sanctions regime. The published licenses are already effective on the dates stated in the text.

title: Review of the Oil and Gas Fiscal Regime: Terms of Reference
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for a review of the UK oil and gas fiscal regime. It is a policy paper setting out the review’s context, objectives and scope, not a rule or consultation with obligations. It is relevant mainly for awareness to firms exposed to the oil and gas sector.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Report Stage
summary: This HM Treasury policy paper sets out government amendments and explanatory notes for the Spring Finance Bill 2023 at report stage. The amendments cover tax measures including the domestic top-up tax, full expensing, energy profits levy de-carbonisation allowance, HMRC communications data and deposit schemes. The publication is informational, but it points to binding legislative changes in the bill.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Creative Industries
summary: This government review makes non-binding recommendations for pro-innovation regulatory reforms across the UK creative industries, including video games, advertising, live performance and fashion. It discusses self- and co-regulation, emissions reporting, competition barriers and new technologies, with suggested reforms intended over the next 6-18 months. It does not itself create requirements.

title: Thematic Review of Non-investment Asset Valuation
summary: HM Treasury published the results of a thematic review of non-investment asset valuation in public-sector financial reporting. It finds merit in exploring changes to the current valuation regime and says a formal consultation may follow. This is awareness-only for banks unless they are directly involved in UK public-sector reporting or advisory work.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 69
summary: OFAC published General License 69 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain debt-securities servicing transactions and limited unblocking activity for International Investment Bank debt issued before 2023-04-12. U.S. financial institutions must file an unblocking report when they unblock property under the license. The authorization runs through 2023-06-30 12:01 a.m. EDT.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8L
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 8L, replacing GL 8K and authorizing certain PdVSA-related transactions for specified covered entities until 2023-11-19. The license is limited to essential operations/safe wind-down activities and excludes drilling, petroleum trade, insurance for those activities, new personnel, dividends, loans, and other blocked-person dealings.

title: Treasury Minutes - June 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to Parliamentary committee reports on a range of public-sector topics, including fraud, digital services tax, passport processing and employment support. It does not create or change regulatory requirements for firms. It is for awareness only.

title: UK-EU Memorandum of Understanding on Financial Services Cooperation
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a Memorandum of Understanding creating a framework for EU-UK financial services regulatory cooperation and a Joint Forum. It sets out areas for information sharing and coordination, but does not itself impose new firm-level requirements or deadlines.

title: Economic crime plan 2023 to 2026
summary: HMT publishes the UK Economic Crime Plan 2023 to 2026, setting out government and industry priorities on money laundering, sanctions evasion, fraud, kleptocracy and wider illicit finance.
