It is a strategic policy document rather than a rule or supervision notice, so it does not itself create new obligations. It is relevant mainly for AML, sanctions, fraud and risk teams.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2021-22
summary: HMT explains the 2021-22 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation and its effect on Scottish Government funding for 2024-25. It is an explanatory policy paper, not a rule or supervisory action, and creates no obligations for firms.

title: Data Reporting Services Regulations 2023 - Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury published a near-final draft Statutory Instrument and policy note to replace retained EU law for Data Reporting Service Providers, supporting a UK consolidated tape and updating the rules for APAs, ARMs and CTPs. It invites technical comments by 21 August 2023. The measure is part of the Smarter Regulatory Framework and will affect firms that use or provide data reporting services.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting February 2023
summary: This is a government policy paper summarising the tenth meeting of the Financial Inclusion Policy Forum. It is informational only and does not create or change requirements for firms. No action or deadline is stated.

title: Building a Smarter Financial Services Regulatory Framework: Delivery Plan
summary: HM Treasury published a delivery plan for the UK Smarter Regulatory Framework, explaining how financial services retained EU law will be repealed and replaced over time under FSMA 2023. It is a roadmap and forward look, not itself a rule change. The paper says reforms will be phased and sequenced, with future draft statutory instruments and consultations to follow.

title: Investment Research Review
summary: HM Treasury published the Investment Research Review, an independent policy paper by Rachel Kent on the UK investment research market and capital markets competitiveness. It sets out recommendations to government, the FCA and industry, including a research platform, wider access for retail investors, issuer-sponsored research code of conduct, and review of IPO-related rules. It is an outcome paper and does not itself create rules.

title: Securitisation Regulations 2023 - Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury publishes a near-final draft Statutory Instrument for the UK securitisation regime, plus a policy note, to replace retained EU law with a UK-tailored framework. It is for technical comments only by 21 August 2023. FCA and PRA rules are expected later to replace most firm-facing requirements, so firms involved in securitisation should prepare for further consultations.

title: Digitisation Taskforce
summary: HMT’s Digitisation Taskforce policy paper sets out an interim report and invites industry feedback on proposals to modernise the UK shareholding framework, including eliminating paper share certificates and expanding digitisation options. It is an open-engagement policy paper rather than a binding rule. Feedback on the interim report was requested by 25 September 2023, with final recommendations due in spring 2024.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2022 to 2023
summary: This is the National Insurance Fund Investment Account annual report and accounts for 2022-2023, laid before Parliament under the Social Security Administration Act 1992. It describes the fund’s investment activity, governance, and audited financial results for the year ended 31 March 2023. No new requirements or deadlines are created for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes - July 2023
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on defence, tax compliance, shared services, digital services, restoration and renewal, vetting and alcohol treatment. It records government positions and planned follow-up actions, but does not create financial-services obligations or regulatory requirements. No direct action date is imposed on banks or regulated firms.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updates to EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related rules, effective 2023-07-18. The changes support EDGAR Release 23.2, new Form SD exhibit types for resource extraction disclosures, updated XBRL taxonomies, and stricter taxonomy-version requirements for electronic filings. Filers using EDGAR should update filing processes immediately.

title: Publication of Burma Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5
summary: OFAC published Burma Sanctions Regulations General License 5, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions needed to wind down dealings involving Myanma Investment and Commercial Bank, Myanma Foreign Trade Bank, or their 50%+ owned entities. The authorization runs until 2023-08-05 00:01 EDT, and payments to blocked persons must be made into blocked accounts. Firms dealing with Myanmar counterparties should assess any remaining transactions immediately.

title: Publication of Covid-Related Web General Licenses Related to Syria Sanctions Regulations, Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, and Venezuela Sanctions Regulations.
summary: OFAC published three general licenses extending until 2024 certain COVID-19-related transactions under the Syria, Iran/Global Terrorism, and Venezuela sanctions regulations. The licenses authorize specified exports, imports, and dealings for COVID-19 prevention, diagnosis, or treatment, and replace earlier versions effective June 14, 2023. Firms dealing with sanctioned jurisdictions or persons should review current authorizations immediately.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on Royal Taxation 2023
summary: HM Treasury published a memorandum explaining the voluntary tax arrangements for the King and the Prince of Wales, including income tax, capital gains tax and inheritance tax treatment for royal assets and income. It is a policy/reporting document and does not create obligations for regulated firms.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License P
summary: OFAC published General License P under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving Navyan Abr Arvan Private Limited Company or Arvancloud Global Technologies L.L.C. The licence applied through 2023-07-06 and does not authorize other Iran sanctions-prohibited transactions. Firms with Iran-related activities or payments into blocked accounts should confirm sanctions handling and expiry effects.

title: Report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant Review 2023
summary: This is a parliamentary report on the 2023 Sovereign Grant review under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011. It concludes the grant percentage should be reduced from 25% to 12% and notes the government’s intention to bring forward legislation later to reset the level after Buckingham Palace reservicing is completed, expected in 2026-27.

title: The updated agreement on the Scottish Government’s Fiscal Framework
summary: This is an August 2023 policy agreement between the Scottish and UK governments on the Scottish Government’s fiscal framework, covering block grant adjustments, devolved tax and welfare revenue treatment, borrowing, reserves, reporting and dispute resolution. It is informational and restates the framework and transition timing rather than creating new firm obligations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 70 and 71.
summary: OFAC published web General Licenses 70 and 71 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize certain wind-down transactions involving UMMC entities and certain Russian banks, and permit rejection/return of some transactions, through 2023-10-18. U.S. persons and financial institutions should apply the exemptions and blocked-account requirements immediately.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 40B.
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 40B, authorizing certain LPG export or reexport transactions involving Venezuela, PdVSA and related entities through 2024-07-10. It replaces GL 40A effective 2023-07-10 and excludes payment-in-kind petroleum transactions and other blocked-person dealings outside the licence scope.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5K and 5L.
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations general licenses 5K and 5L, authorizing certain transactions and financing related to Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% Bond on or after 20 July 2023. GL 5L supersedes GL 5K, which had delayed the authorization from 19 April 2023. Sanctions teams and operations should apply the current license terms immediately.

title: Treasury Minutes – August 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes (August 2023) is the government’s response to the Public Accounts Committee on several 2022-23 reports. It sets out the government’s answers and positions on issues including education recovery, investment, pensions, energy bills support, decarbonising the power sector, and local auditor reporting. It does not itself create new binding requirements for firms.

title: Block Grant Transparency: July 2023
summary: HM Treasury publishes an explanatory policy paper and spreadsheet on how block grants for the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive are calculated. It is informational only and does not create requirements for firms.

title: Cuban Assets Control Regulations
summary: This CFR correction updates 31 CFR part 515 (Cuban Assets Control Regulations) by fixing a cross-reference in section 515.570(d). It affects persons subject to U.S. Cuba sanctions and takes effect as published; no new substantive requirement is created, but the codified text is corrected.

title: Additional Guidance on Low-Income Communities Bonus Credit Program
summary: The IRS/Treasury published a correction to the final rule on the Low-Income Communities Bonus Credit Program, fixing amendatory instruction 2 in 26 CFR Part 1. This affects the codified text already issued in the earlier final rule and is relevant to entities relying on the program's tax-credit guidance.

title: Public service pensions: 2020 valuations
summary: The Treasury issued new Public Service Pensions (Valuations and Employer Cost Cap) Directions 2023, replacing the 2014 directions. They set the valuation and cost-cap methodology for public service pension schemes, including scheme actuary reporting, employer contribution rate calculations, and scheme-specific modifications. The directions take effect the day after signing.

title: Publication of Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 1A, 1B, and 2
summary: OFAC published four general licenses for the Chinese Military-Industrial Complex sanctions program, reproducing earlier permissions for certain securities transactions involving covered Chinese military companies. The licenses are time-limited and some are now expired; this publication is a sanctions/watchlist update relevant to sanctions screening and transaction controls.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13F
summary: OFAC published General License 13F under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain tax, fee, import duty, and licensing payments by U.S. persons and entities owned or controlled by U.S. persons for day-to-day operations in Russia, until 2023-11-08. GL 13E was superseded. Sanctions teams must check scope immediately.

title: UK-India 12th Economic and Financial Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: UK and India issued a joint statement after the 12th Economic and Financial Dialogue, highlighting commitments on investment, financial market access, economic resilience, climate action, infrastructure and technology. It is a policy paper and does not itself set new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8 and 9
summary: OFAC published Belarus Sanctions Regulations general licenses 8 and 9. They authorize certain wind-down transactions with designated Belarusian entities and, for Belavia, certain civil aviation safety-related transactions, each only until the stated expiry dates. Firms dealing with sanctioned persons must check the scope, blocked-account requirements and any separate export controls.

title: Treasury Minutes - September 2023
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports across several government departments, including justice, health, transport, home affairs and HMRC. It records government responses and target implementation dates for recommendations, but does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms. Relevant dates mentioned include March 2024 and January 2024 for government actions.

title: Publication of Ethiopia Sanctions Regulations Web General License 4
summary: OFAC published Ethiopia Sanctions Regulations General License 4, which authorizes wind-down transactions involving Hidri Trust or Red Sea Trading Corporation and states the license has expired. This is relevant for firms dealing with sanctioned persons or Ethiopia-related transactions, but it does not create a new ongoing obligation.

title: Publication of Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 2, and Subsequent Iterations
summary: OFAC is publishing general licenses under the Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations that authorize limited wind-down and divestment transactions involving specified blocked persons and subsidiaries, and note that the licenses are expired/superseded. This is relevant for firms dealing with sanctions screening, payments, and blocked-property controls; the operative authorizations were time-limited and have already lapsed.

title: Publication of Determination Pursuant to Section 1(a)(i) of Executive Order 14014
summary: OFAC has added the jet fuel sector of the Burmese economy to the sectors subject to blocking sanctions under Executive Order 14014. The determination took effect on 2023-08-23 and means persons operating in that sector may become sanctionable under US Burma sanctions.

title: Terms of Reference for the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee
summary: HMT published terms of reference for the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee, describing its purpose and membership across the UK Government and devolved governments. It is an informational policy paper with no new rules, deadlines, or obligations.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 42
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 42, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions needed to negotiate settlement agreements with specified Venezuelan National Assembly-related persons and certain Venezuela debt matters. It does not authorize dealings with the Maduro National Constituent Assembly or the 2021 National Assembly. Effective from the license issue date of 2023-05-01.

title: The Commission's Privacy Act Regulations
summary: The SEC adopted updated Privacy Act regulations for SEC records and Privacy Act requests. The final rule clarifies procedures, allows electronic identity verification, adjusts response times and fee provisions, and removes obsolete text. It is effective 2023-10-26.

title: EM on a UK/EU TCA Specialised Committee decision (COM(2023)527)
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory memorandum on an EU Council decision for the UK/EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement Specialised Committee to adopt changes enabling UK association to Horizon Europe and Copernicus from 1 January 2024. It explains eligibility, funding treatment for 2021-2023 calls, and a clawback mechanism, but it is not itself a rule or obligation for firms.

title: UK Government Green Financing: 2021 to 2023 reports
summary: HM Treasury’s 2023 UK Green Financing Allocation and Impact Report sets out how 2022-23 green gilt and Green Savings Bond proceeds were allocated and reports first-year environmental and social impacts from the UK Green Financing Programme. It is an informational report only and does not create new requirements.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 55A and 72
summary: OFAC published two Russian sanctions general licenses: GL 55A authorizes certain Sakhalin-2-related maritime transport transactions for importation into Japan until 2024-06-28, and GL 72 authorizes wind-down transactions involving specified newly blocked entities until 2023-12-13. Both are subject to stated exclusions and sanctions restrictions.

title: Joint statement on the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury issued a joint statement summarising the eighth UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting and its key discussion points and outcomes. It does not create or change any obligations for firms.

title: Payment service contract termination rule changes: implementation, timings, and next steps
summary: HM Treasury sets out how it will amend the Payment Services Regulations 2017 to extend payment account/framework contract termination notice to 90 days and require clear, tailored reasons for termination, subject to limited exceptions. The policy statement clarifies scope, expected practice, and next legislative steps for payment service providers, including banks and other firms with payment accounts.

title: EM on a TCA Specialised Committee decision (12523/23, COM(23)504)
summary: HM Treasury’s explanatory memorandum supports an EU Council decision on the UK/EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement VAT cooperation committee. It describes technical implementing decisions on information exchange forms, recovery assistance, service levels and UK financial contributions, with payment due within 60 days of adoption. It is informational and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updates to the EDGAR Filer Manual and related rules/forms, changing filing formats and submission types for certain forms, including new XML and Inline XBRL requirements. The changes took effect on 2023-10-03, with some EDGAR filing functionality moving to test and live phases through 2024. Filers affected include investment company and issuer filers using EDGAR.

title: World Bank 108th Development Committee Meeting: UK Governor's statement
summary: UK ministers’ statement to the World Bank Development Committee calls for a concerted international effort to improve the global finance system and increase World Bank financing and ambition. It is a policy speech/statement with no direct obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Consumer Information Requests to Large Banks and Credit Unions
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion on section 1034(c) of the Consumer Financial Protection Act, explaining that large banks and credit unions must timely respond to consumer requests for account information, subject to limited exceptions. It is effective immediately as of 2023-10-16, and the CFPB said it does not intend to seek monetary relief for pre-2024 violations.

title: Fairness Group Joint Public Statement
summary: HMT and partners published a joint public statement on how government will work with the debt advice sector to improve treatment of people in debt, especially vulnerable customers. It reaffirms use of Fairness Principles and a joint programme of work, but does not create new rules or deadlines.

title: EM on Windsor Framework customs arrangements
summary: HMRC’s explanatory memorandum describes the EU’s Commission Delegated Regulation under the Windsor Framework, which changes customs formalities for trusted traders and parcels moving from Great Britain to Northern Ireland. It explains what is already in force and notes further arrangements will apply from 30 September 2024. The memo itself does not create obligations, but it points to the underlying EU measure and UK implementation context.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, October 2023
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording topics discussed at the first EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum. It is a policy paper and does not itself change rules or set deadlines for firms.

title: Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Bill 2022: overarching documents
summary: This is an HMT policy paper page collecting background documents for the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Bill/Act, including the draft bill and fact sheets on the register of overseas entities, unexplained wealth orders and sanctions. It is informational only and does not itself create obligations.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 26 October 2023
summary: This is a joint statement from HMT and the European Commission noting progress on Financial Provisions work streams related to EU invoices under the Financial Settlement. It is informational only and does not create or change obligations for firms.

title: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023: ECHR memoranda
summary: This policy paper republishes ECHR memoranda for the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 and notes that the Bill received Royal Assent on 26 October 2023. It is informational and does not itself create new requirements for firms.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting – July 2023
summary: This is a record of a meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA about the FCA’s Perimeter Report and the financial services regulatory perimeter. It does not create or change rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Update on plans for the regulation of fiat-backed stablecoins
summary: HM Treasury sets out its planned UK regime for fiat-backed stablecoins. It says secondary legislation will bring issuance and custody of UK-issued fiat-backed stablecoins, and their use in payment chains, into the regulatory perimeter, with FCA oversight and Bank of England/PSR powers for systemic arrangements. It expects to bring legislation forward as soon as possible and by early 2024, subject to parliamentary time.

title: Publication of Nicaragua Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 2, and 2A
summary: OFAC published web general licenses under the Nicaragua Sanctions Regulations, including GLs 1, 2 and 2A, which authorize certain wind-down and official U.S. government transactions and clarify the prior licenses' status. This is relevant to firms processing sanctions-related payments or transactions involving the Nicaraguan National Police and related blocked persons.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 73
summary: OFAC published General License 73 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes limited safety, crew-welfare, emergency repair, and environmental mitigation transactions involving two blocked vessels through 2024-01-08, subject to restrictions and blocked-account payment rules. Firms dealing with the listed persons, vessels, or related transactions must check sanctions permissions before acting.

title: Extending the transitional period for third country benchmarks in the UK
summary: HM Treasury has laid a statutory instrument extending the UK Benchmarks Regulation transitional period for third-country benchmarks from 31 December 2025 to 31 December 2030. The change comes into force on 1 January 2024 and affects firms using or relying on third-country benchmarks in the UK.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 3I, 5M, 9H, 43, 44, and 45
summary: OFAC published web versions of six Venezuela general licenses under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions in specified bonds and related activities, with some superseding earlier licenses and one license expiring on 2024-04-18. Firms dealing in Venezuela-related persons or securities should confirm transaction permissibility against the updated licenses.

title: International Joint Statement on the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework
summary: HMT published a joint policy statement announcing signatory jurisdictions’ intention to implement the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and related amendments to the Common Reporting Standard, with exchanges expected to begin by 2027. It is an announcement of future implementation, not a binding rule or consultation.

title: Treasury Minutes – November 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s November 2023 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee recommendations on COVID grant schemes, fraud and corruption, digital transformation, and resetting programmes. It is a parliamentary response and progress update, not a rule or supervisory requirement. No direct obligations are created for banks or other regulated firms.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Advanced Manufacturing
summary: This is a UK government review report on how regulation and standards could better support advanced manufacturing innovation, including automation, hydrogen, clean fuels, recycling and building materials. It makes policy recommendations for government and regulators; it does not itself change rules or impose deadlines.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13G, 74, 75, and 76.
summary: OFAC published four Russian sanctions general licenses covering certain administrative transactions, wind-down/rejection activity involving East-West United Bank, and related divestment/transfer permissions. The licenses were issued on 2023-11-02 and generally expire on 2024-01-31. U.S. persons and covered entities should check whether their Russia-related transactions now fall within these temporary authorizations.

title: Autumn Statement 2023 Research and Development Tax Reliefs Reform
summary: HM Treasury published a technical note on Autumn Statement 2023 reforms to UK R&D tax reliefs. It explains the proposed merged R&D expenditure credit and enhanced support for R&D-intensive SMEs, with legislation to follow in the Autumn Finance Bill. No immediate filing or conduct deadline is set out in this note.

title: UK Retail Disclosure Framework – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury publishes a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note for a new UK retail disclosure framework for Consumer Composite Investments under the Designated Activities Regime. It is replacing retained EU PRIIPs rules and gives the FCA rule-making powers and related supervision/enforcement provisions. Technical comments on the draft are invited by 2024-01-10.

title: Short Selling Regulations 2024
summary: Draft UK statutory regulations for short selling under FSMA 2000/2023. They designate short selling-related activities, give the FCA powers to make rules on settlement arrangements and notification of significant net short positions, and set a 0.2% notification threshold. This is a draft laid before Parliament, so it is not yet in force, but it signals the future UK regime for relevant market participants.

title: Government response to the 2023 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s 2023 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report explains the government’s fiscal risk management approach and planned policy actions on inactivity, energy resilience and debt sustainability. It is informational and does not impose new requirements on firms. No immediate compliance date applies.

title: Shared Outcomes Fund Round Three
summary: UK government policy paper summarising Round 3 projects under the Shared Outcomes Fund, including pilot funding for cross-government initiatives on health, housing, courts, data and net zero. It is informational only and does not create obligations or deadlines for banks.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Cross-Cutting
summary: HM Treasury published a review making non-binding recommendations on how government and regulators can support pro-innovation regulation, including better coordination, a concierge service for innovators, and changes to the Regulators’ Growth Duty. It is a policy paper and does not itself change requirements. No immediate compliance date applies.

title: Government response to the National Infrastructure Commission report on improving nationally significant infrastructure planning
summary: The UK government published a policy paper responding to the National Infrastructure Commission’s report on nationally significant infrastructure planning in England. It sets out the government’s response to six recommendations and signals longer-term reform intentions, but it does not itself create binding requirements.

title: Autumn Statement 2023: National Insurance Factsheet
summary: UK government factsheet announcing National Insurance cuts for employees and the self-employed, and the abolition of Class 2 NICs as part of the Autumn Statement 2023. It is informational only and does not itself create the tax change or set an implementation deadline.

title: The mortgage guarantee scheme
summary: HM Treasury’s policy paper announces and explains a mortgage guarantee scheme to support homeownership and high loan-to-value lending. It is descriptive and consultative in tone, setting out the intended design and policy rationale, but it does not itself impose binding requirements or deadlines on lenders.

title: The Harrington Review of Foreign Direct Investment
summary: HMT publishes Lord Harrington’s review of foreign direct investment with recommendations for a new cross-government business investment strategy, investment committee and support machinery. It is an advisory report, not a rule or consultation, so it creates no direct obligations for firms. Any future government response may affect investment-facing businesses, including financial institutions.

title: UK-Japan Financial Dialogue and Financial Regulatory Forum joint statement
summary: Joint UK-Japan statement recording discussions at the Financial Dialogue and Financial Regulatory Forum in Tokyo on 27 November 2023. It is informational only and does not create or change any regulatory requirements or deadlines.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 21 December 2021
summary: HMT published the provisional agenda for the first meeting of the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is an informational meeting agenda only and does not create obligations or deadlines.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 22 September 2022
summary: This is a provisional agenda for a UK-EU committee meeting under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement about UK association to EU programmes. It does not create or change obligations, deadlines, or supervisory expectations.

title: Autumn Statement 2023
summary: The UK Autumn Statement 2023 is a government policy paper and fiscal statement setting out economic and tax measures, spending decisions and forecasts for the UK. It includes policy announcements affecting businesses and households, with some corrected wording in the published document. It is informational rather than a binding rule or supervisory notice.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 4 December 2023
summary: The UK government published a provisional agenda for the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes meeting on 4 December 2023. It is an administrative notice about the UK-EU trade and cooperation governance forum and does not create or change obligations for firms.

title: Further detail on HMT analysis of borrowing and interest rates
summary: HMT published a policy paper with a methodological annex and supplementary data explaining how it estimates the impact of additional government borrowing on interest rates. It is informational only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 22 September 2022
summary: Minutes of the second meeting of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It records discussion of participation in Union programmes, but does not itself create or change any obligations.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2023
summary: UK Treasury progress report updating Parliament on how the Government has implemented accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across many sessions. It is an accountability and status update only, with no new rules, deadlines or requirements for firms.

title: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (The Ombudsman Scheme) Regulations 2024 – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury publishes a draft statutory instrument and policy note to extend the Financial Ombudsman Service’s fee-charging scope so it can charge claims management companies and other professional representatives, not just respondent firms. It is tied to the FOS Plans and Budget consultation closing on 2024-01-30, and HM Treasury says it intends to legislate before the FOS makes new charging rules.

title: Decision No 1/2023 of the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement adopting Protocols I and II and amending Annex 47 to the Trade and Cooperation Agreement
summary: This EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement decision adopts Protocols I and II and amends Annex 47. It confirms UK participation and contribution terms for certain Union programmes from 1 January 2024, including Horizon Europe-related funding mechanics. Relevant teams should note the updated participation, contribution, and call-for-funds rules for affected UK entities and programme activities.

title: Money Market Funds – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HMT publishes a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note to replace retained EU law on money market funds with a new UK framework. It invites technical comments by 2024-01-24. The SI deletes certain passporting provisions, while authorisation/approval requirements for MMFs remain, with detailed firm-facing rules to follow in the FCA rulebook.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2021-22
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy note on the 2021-22 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC income tax outturn and ONS population data adjust Welsh Government funding for 2024-25, with a net £107 million increase. No firm obligations are created for financial institutions.

title: Customs simplification measures: December 2023
summary: HM Treasury and HMRC published a policy paper summarising next steps to simplify UK customs import and export processes for traders. It is informational and outlines government plans only; it does not itself impose new customs requirements or deadlines.

title: EM about an amendment to EU decision 2021/512 (COM(2023)704)
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU proposal to extend the UK’s Northern Ireland VAT fuel derogation until 31 December 2026. It would keep the flat-rate method allowing businesses to reclaim VAT on fuel for company cars without full mileage records. This is an explanatory memorandum only, not the binding decision itself.

title: Thematic review of performance reporting
summary: HMT published a thematic review of government performance reporting in annual reports and accounts, with recommendations to streamline guidance, improve communication with preparers and users, and publish best-practice/training materials. It does not itself change binding requirements, but signals possible updates to the FReM and PES guidance for government departments and preparers.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update 2023
summary: HM Treasury publishes a progress update on its own Women in Finance Charter commitments, noting female representation in senior management rose from 43% to 50% by March 2023. It is an informational update only and does not create new obligations for firms.

title: Response to the VRP Working Group’s Blueprint for non-sweeping VRPs
summary: HMT/PSR/FCA publish the JROC response to the industry blueprint for phased rollout of non-sweeping VRPs in open banking. It discusses future use cases, consumer protection and commercial model issues, but does not itself create binding requirements or dates for firms.

title: Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee update on actions to enable the next phase of open banking in the UK
summary: The JROC provides a progress update on work to move UK open banking into its next phase, including plans for a future entity, governance, funding and phased development of new services. It is an update and roadmap rather than a binding rule, with further decisions and proposals expected in 2024.

title: Technical note: Electricity Generator Levy – new investment exemption
summary: HM Treasury published a technical note on a new investment exemption for the UK Electricity Generator Levy. Where the substantive decision to proceed with a new generating station or expansion is made on or after 22 November 2023, the new capacity or station receipts may be exempt from EGL. It is an interpretive note, not formal guidance; HMRC will issue that separately.

title: Publication of Syria-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 1, 2, and 3
summary: OFAC published Syria-related general licenses 1, 2 and 3 under 31 CFR part 569. The licenses authorize specified transactions for U.S. government official business, certain wind-down activities involving Turkish ministries, and official activities of certain international organizations, subject to stated limits. This is a sanctions update affecting firms dealing in Syria-/Turkey-related transactions and should be applied immediately.

title: Publication of Burma Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 3 and 4
summary: OFAC published Burma sanctions General Licenses 3 and 4, which authorize certain NGO-related transactions and the wind-down of transactions involving MEC, MEHL and related entities. GL 4 had already expired on 2021-06-22; GL 3 remains a standing authorization unless otherwise limited by OFAC. Relevant teams should confirm sanctions screening and payment controls reflect the Burma sanctions permissions and expiry status.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 78
summary: OFAC published General License 78 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain safety, crew welfare, emergency repair and environmental mitigation transactions for specified blocked vessels and related persons through 2024-02-29. It does not permit new commercial contracts, cargo offloading except for vessel emergencies, or transactions otherwise prohibited by the RuHSR.

title: Notification of Inflation Adjustments for Civil Money Penalties
summary: The OCC updates 2024 maximum civil money penalties for inflation under federal penalty inflation statutes. The new amounts apply to OCC penalties assessed on or after 2024-01-08 for conduct on or after 2015-11-02, including national banks and Federal savings associations.

title: Group of Creditors to Ukraine: Statement on extending the debt deferral for Ukraine
summary: The UK, as part of Ukraine’s group of bilateral creditors, issued a statement extending debt deferral for Ukraine. It is an informational policy statement only and does not create new regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Policy Design Document
summary: HM Treasury’s policy design document sets out the proposed design, mandate, capitalisation and operating model for the UK Infrastructure Bank, including its headquarters, funding capacity and intended areas of focus. It is an informational policy paper about a future institution, not a binding rule. The document notes that legislation will be brought forward later to place the Bank on a statutory footing.

title: Keepwell Agreement
summary: HMT publishes an amended keepwell agreement with UK Infrastructure Bank, replacing the earlier agreement and confirming HMT’s funding commitment up to a £22 billion cap if UKIB cannot meet certain liabilities. It is a bilateral agreement document, not a rule, and it does not set a compliance deadline for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: March 2023
summary: Minutes of an HMT advisory group meeting on government financial reporting topics, including performance reporting, local government, Whole of Government Accounts and sustainability reporting. It is an informational record of discussions only and does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: UKIB Framework Document
summary: HMT publishes the UK Infrastructure Bank Framework Document, setting out the governance, accountability, ownership and operating framework for UKIB and its relationship with HMT and UKGI. It describes the bank’s mission, investment principles, capitalisation and board arrangements, and notes the document may be reviewed within 12 months. It is a framework/governance document rather than a rule or obligation for regulated firms.

title: Central Counterparties Special Resolution Regime Code of Practice
summary: The UK Treasury has issued a Code of Practice under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 for the CCP special resolution regime. It explains how the Bank of England and Treasury may use CCP resolution powers, including bridge CCPs, and the objectives and governance they must consider. It applies to UK CCP resolution and reflects international resolution standards.

title: Third Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin Minutes
summary: Minutes of the third UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin meeting under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It records discussion of customs cooperation, rules of origin, customs facilitation and related customs matters; it does not itself change requirements or set deadlines.

title: Sovereign Infrastructure Guarantee
summary: HM Treasury and UK Infrastructure Bank have executed an amendment and restatement of the Sovereign Infrastructure Guarantee. This is a binding contractual/public guarantee document affecting the UK state-backed infrastructure financing arrangement, effective from the agreement date. No filing or compliance deadline is stated, but the document is legally operative for the parties.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2024
summary: Treasury Minutes records the UK government’s responses to PAC reports across several departments, including smart meters, urgent care, Bulb Energy, active travel, asylum transformation, supported housing, prison leavers and net zero innovation. It is an informational parliamentary response, not a rule or supervisory requirement. No direct compliance date or new obligation is created by the document itself.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 81, 82, 83, 84, and 85
summary: OFAC published general licenses 81-85 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain limited transactions and wind-down activity involving specified blocked persons and vessels. The authorisations run to March 19, 2024 for GLs 81, 82 and 84, February 21, 2024 for GL 83, and March 21, 2024 for GL 85, with strict exclusions and blocked-account payment requirements.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 45A
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 45A, replacing GL 45. It authorizes certain repatriation, aircraft maintenance, and non-commercial flights involving specified Conviasa-related aircraft and persons, effective 2023-11-16. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related activity or screening blocked parties and aircraft should update sanctions controls immediately.

title: Report on the annual review of National Insurance contributions
summary: HM Treasury published a report explaining why it did not lay a draft order to change Class 2, Class 3 or Class 4 National Insurance thresholds or rates for 2024-25. It notes that the annual re-rating statutory instrument was laid on 15 January and recaps previously legislated NIC rate cuts and changes effective from January and April 2024.

title: Fair Credit Reporting; Background Screening
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion under FCRA on background screening reports, saying consumer reporting agencies must use reasonable procedures to avoid duplicative or legally restricted public record information and to handle adverse-item reporting periods appropriately. It is effective immediately from 2024-01-23 and is aimed at consumer reporting agencies, including background screening companies.

title: Fair Credit Reporting; File Disclosure
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion interpreting FCRA section 609(a) file-disclosure duties for consumer reporting agencies. It says consumers need not use specific words to request a file disclosure and that agencies must disclose both the original source and any intermediary or vendor source of information. Effective January 23, 2024; applies to consumer reporting agencies, including nationwide specialty and tenant-screening or employment background screening companies.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updates to the EDGAR Filer Manual and related filing rules to implement recent SEC rule changes, including cybersecurity incident disclosure, beneficial ownership reporting, investment company name disclosure taxonomy changes, and removal of obsolete forms. The rule is effective 2024-01-24, with some EDGAR functionality tied to other effective dates such as 2024-02-05.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2024
summary: HM Treasury published the 2024 public service pensions increase note and multiplier tables. It states that public service pensions in payment for a year will rise by 6.7% from 8 April 2024, with proportionate increases for pensions in payment for less than a year. The tables are for scheme administrators to apply the annual increase correctly.

title: The Digital Pound Taskforce and Forums
summary: HM Treasury and the Bank of England updated the Digital Pound Taskforce terms of reference and accountabilities for the CBDC design phase. This is governance and status information only: it does not create binding requirements or a decision to issue a digital pound. The Taskforce will oversee design work, risks, costs and benefits, and international monitoring.

title: Procedure and Administration
summary: The IRS published a CFR correction to 26 CFR Part 301 that reinstates an omitted rule on penalties for failure to file correct information returns. For returns not due on February 28 or March 15, including certain Forms 8300, the corrected penalty amounts are restored to $15 if fixed within 30 days and $50 if fixed later. This is a point-in-time codification update, not a new policy.

title: National Infrastructure and Construction Pipeline 2023
summary: HMT and the Infrastructure and Projects Authority published the 2023 National Infrastructure and Construction Pipeline, giving an overview of planned and projected UK infrastructure spending, procurement and workforce demand over the next 10 years. It is a market and policy update, not a rule, and does not impose compliance deadlines on firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 4 December 2023
summary: Minutes of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes meeting of 4 December 2023. It is a policy paper/minutes document describing a joint forum under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, with no new rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Joint statement on the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting - January 2024
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury published a joint statement on the ninth UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It is a public record of discussions and outcomes only; it does not itself create or change any requirements for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports, including HMRC’s Making Tax Digital programme. It describes Parliament-facing updates and responses to prior recommendations, but does not itself create new binding requirements for firms. The Making Tax Digital timetable mentioned remains a government/HMRC programme matter, with no new firm action date set in this document.

title: Update to the Transition from Existing Digital Services Taxes to Pillar 1
summary: The UK and several other countries extended their political compromise on the transition from existing digital services taxes to Pillar 1 through 30 June 2024. This is an update on ongoing multilateral tax negotiations, not a binding rule or enforcement action.

title: Joint Statement: UK – U.S. Covered Agreement. Third meeting of the Joint Committee
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury issued a joint statement recording the third meeting under the UK-U.S. Covered Agreement on insurance and reinsurance prudential measures. It summarizes what was discussed and the key outcomes, but does not itself create or change requirements.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5N
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 5N, which authorizes certain transactions and financing related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% bond on or after 2024-04-16. It replaces GL 5M effective 2024-01-16. Firms with sanctions exposure to Venezuela should update screening and transaction handling now.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, and 27
summary: OFAC published six web general licenses under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations authorizing specified transactions involving Ansarallah, including certain humanitarian, telecommunications and communications-related activities. GL 22 takes effect on 2024-02-16; GL 27 expires on 2024-03-22. Firms dealing with Yemen-linked or sanctioned-person transactions should confirm whether activity falls within the new authorisations and continue blocking other prohibited dealings.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13H and 86
summary: OFAC published two Russian sanctions general licenses, GL 13H and GL 86, under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. They authorize limited transactions for U.S. persons and certain blocked vessel safety/environmental activities through 2024-04-17, with specific carve-outs and prohibitions. Firms dealing with Russia-related activity must check whether any transactions fall within the licenses before acting.

title: Supervisory Appeals Process
summary: The CFPB revised its supervisory appeals process, effective 2024-02-22. Institutions subject to CFPB supervision may now appeal any compliance rating and certain adverse findings, with updated committee membership and a new remand option. The process applies to appeals pending on publication date.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 87
summary: OFAC published General License 87 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing limited vessel safety, anchoring, crew welfare, and emergency repair/environmental mitigation transactions for two newly blocked shipping-related persons through 2024-05-08. Firms must still avoid other prohibited transactions, including new commercial contracts and most cargo or oil-related activity.

title: Publication of Burma Sanctions Regulations Web General License 6
summary: OFAC published Burma Sanctions General License 6, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving Shwe Byain Phyu Group of Companies and entities it owns 50% or more of. The authorization runs until 2024-03-01 00:01 EST and payments to blocked persons must go into blocked accounts. Firms dealing with Burma-related counterparties should check scope before relying on it.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: February 2024
summary: HM Treasury publishes economic evidence for the 2024-25 public sector pay round, covering inflation, growth, labour market conditions and affordability. It is background material for the independent Pay Review Bodies and does not impose requirements on firms. No action date applies beyond the publication date.

title: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023: Factsheets
summary: HMT and other UK bodies published factsheets explaining measures in the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023, including Companies House reform, identity verification, limited partnerships, cryptoassets, SLAPPs and new SFO powers. This is informational only and does not itself create new requirements. It is relevant to firms with UK corporate, legal and financial crime exposure.

title: Investment Zones update
summary: The UK government published an update giving further details on six Investment Zones in England, including spending and tax interventions for five zones and location, sector and anchor investor details for Tees. It is informational and does not itself create or change obligations for firms.

title: Spring Budget 2024: Non-UK domiciled individuals - Policy Summary
summary: The UK government published a policy summary announcing that from April 2025 it will abolish the current tax regime for non-UK domiciled individuals and replace domicile with a residence-based tax regime. It is an announcement of intended tax reform, not the legislation itself.

title: Spring Budget 2024: Personal Tax Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury’s Spring Budget 2024 personal tax factsheet explains announced changes to National Insurance and the High Income Child Benefit Charge. It is an informational policy paper, not the legal instrument itself, and does not set firm action dates in the text provided.

title: Spring Budget 2024
summary: UK Spring Budget 2024 announces fiscal and tax measures, including cuts to employee and self-employed National Insurance from 6 April 2024. It is a government budget/policy paper rather than a regulatory rule or supervisory notice, so it is for awareness rather than direct compliance action.

title: Memorandum of Understanding for the "Trailblazer" Single Settlements for Greater Manchester and West Midlands Combined Authorities
summary: This is a government memorandum of understanding setting out how single settlements will work for Greater Manchester and West Midlands Combined Authorities. It describes scope, governance, funding flexibility and accountability arrangements, with further details to be agreed and published by spring 2024. It does not create bank-specific regulatory obligations.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 43A
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 43A, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving Minerven and related entities until 2024-02-13. The license replaced General License 43 and is now expired. It affects persons and firms subject to the Venezuela sanctions regime.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determinations.
summary: OFAC published two Russia sanctions determinations under Executive Order 14068, as amended, making the import prohibitions apply to certain non-industrial diamonds, diamond jewelry, and unsorted diamonds, including items mined/produced in Russia or exported from Russia. This affects U.S. importers and firms handling covered goods immediately upon the February 8, 2024 determinations.

title: Publication of Western Balkans Stabilization Regulations Web General Licenses 2 and 3
summary: OFAC published General Licenses 2 and 3 under the Western Balkans Stabilization Regulations. GL 2 authorizes wind-down transactions involving Orka Holding AD through 2024-03-15; GL 3 authorizes certain agricultural, medical, treatment, research, and clinical-trial-related transactions involving Orka Holding AD. Firms must ensure any activity stays within the licenses’ scope.

title: Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC issued a final rule effective 2024-03-12 reissuing and expanding the Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations in full. The rule adds interpretive guidance, definitions, general licenses, and other provisions implementing the Global Magnitsky Act, E.O. 13818, and related authorities. Sanctions screening, payments, onboarding, and asset-freeze controls may need updating immediately for any US-person or US-dollar activity.

title: The Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024 – policy note
primary_functions: Legal; Regulatory change; Compliance; Financial crime; Product
summary: HM Treasury’s near-final policy note explains a statutory instrument that would amend the Payment Services Regulations 2017 to let payment service providers delay outbound payments by up to four business days when there are reasonable grounds to suspect fraud or dishonesty. It is aimed at PSPs such as banks and is part of the UK’s response to APP fraud. The document invites technical comments before the final instrument is laid.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-01: Preferencing and Steering Practices by Digital Intermediaries for Consumer Financial Products or Services
summary: The CFPB issued Circular 2024-01 explaining that digital comparison-shopping tools and lead generators may violate the Consumer Financial Protection Act if they steer consumers toward products or providers based on remuneration or other benefits to the operator. It is guidance on abusive practices for consumer financial products and services, with no new deadline or rule text.

title: British Council framework document
summary: HMT published a policy paper setting out the governance and accountability framework between the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office and the British Council, including core responsibilities and how their day-to-day relationship works. It does not create regulatory obligations for financial services firms.

title: Payment service contract termination rule changes – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury has published a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note to change the Payment Services Regulations 2017 on payment service contract terminations. The reforms will apply to providers of payment services and framework contracts for an indefinite period entered into on or after commencement, with targeted exceptions for intermediated business models. The draft SI is still being checked before it is laid before Parliament.

title: Communiqués from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee
summary: A UK government policy paper republishes communiqués from Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee meetings, noting regular discussions between the Chief Secretary to the Treasury and devolved finance ministers on economic and finance matters affecting the UK. It does not create or change any rules or deadlines.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 83A
summary: OFAC published General License 83A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, replacing GL 83. It authorizes certain otherwise prohibited transactions related to importing specified seafood derivative products into the United States, for cargo loaded before 2024-02-20 and under pre-existing written contracts, through 2024-05-31.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 45B
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 45B, replacing GL 45A. It authorizes certain repatriation transactions involving Conviasa for Venezuelan nationals returning from non-U.S. jurisdictions in the Western Hemisphere, and related aircraft maintenance, effective 2024-02-29. Firms must still comply with other OFAC restrictions and any BIS export controls.

title: Building a Smarter Financial Services Regulatory Framework: Next Phase
summary: HM Treasury sets out progress on the UK Smarter Financial Services Regulatory Framework and next-phase work to repeal and replace assimilated law. It is an update on the programme, including planned reforms to insurance capital, prospectus, market data, securitisation and payments rules, rather than a rule or consultation with direct obligations. No immediate action date is set in this publication.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General License 29
summary: OFAC published General License 29 under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving Haleel Commodities LLC and related entities. The license is effective through 2024-04-10 12:01 a.m. EDT, subject to blocked-account conditions for payments to blocked persons. Firms dealing in sanctioned transactions should check exposure immediately.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 88, 88A, 89, 90, 91, 91A, 92, and 93
summary: OFAC published eight Russia-related general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize limited wind-down transactions involving specified blocked Russian entities, with each license expiring on dates in April or May 2024. Firms dealing with Russia-related counterparties should check whether any transactions fall within the new permissions and the listed exclusions.

title: Public Service Pensions and Judicial Offices Act 2022: Treasury Directions - December 2022 to March 2024
summary: The UK Treasury made and brought into force amendments to the Public Service Pensions (Exercise of Powers, Compensation and Information) Directions 2022, applying to chapter 1 schemes, judicial schemes and local government schemes. The changes update interest calculations, compensation/tax treatment and related pension payment rules from 2024-03-21.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2024-25
summary: The Royal Trustees report under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 on the 2024-25 Sovereign Grant calculation and confirms £86.3 million will be paid to the Royal Household. This is a public report to Parliament and includes a correction slip for publication details; it does not impose obligations on banks or regulated firms.

title: Accelerated Settlement Taskforce
summary: HM Treasury published the Accelerated Settlement Taskforce report and government response. It recommends the UK move to a T+1 securities settlement cycle no later than 31 December 2027 and sets up a technical group to work through implementation details. This is an update and direction of travel, not a binding rule.

title: Treasury Minutes – March 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s March 2024 Treasury Minutes records the government’s responses to PAC reports on flooding, defence inventory management, whole of government accounts, HS2 and illegal drugs. It mainly sets out agreement to recommendations and intended implementation timetables, including flood-risk measurement work through end-2025. It is an informational parliamentary response, not a rule or supervisory requirement.

title: Seizing the Opportunity: Delivering Efficiency for the Public
summary: HM Treasury sets out a policy paper on improving public-sector efficiency through procurement, fraud reduction, major projects, asset management and digital transformation. It describes the government’s Public Sector Productivity Programme and related plans, but does not create obligations for banks or firms. No compliance date or binding rule is stated.

title: UK Independent Film Tax Credit
summary: This policy note explains the UK Independent Film Tax Credit and gives extra detail on eligibility criteria and how the credit will be calculated. It is informational and does not itself create or change obligations. It applies to UK independent film productions and was published on 2024-04-12.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and Proper Use of Sample Forms
summary: The CFPB issued a circular reminding creditors that adverse action notices under ECOA/Regulation B must give specific, accurate principal reasons for denial or other adverse action. It says lenders cannot rely on sample-form checklist reasons if they are too broad or do not accurately reflect the actual decision, including when using AI or complex credit models.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-02: Deceptive Marketing Practices About the Speed or Cost of Sending a Remittance Transfer
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining when remittance transfer providers may violate the Consumer Financial Protection Act’s prohibition on deceptive acts or practices in marketing about transfer speed or cost. It says providers can be liable even if they comply with Remittance Rule disclosure requirements, and gives examples such as misleading “free,” “no fee,” or delivery-time claims. No new deadline is stated.

title: Zimbabwe Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC issued a final rule effective 2024-04-17 removing the Zimbabwe Sanctions Regulations from the CFR after the U.S. terminated the national emergency underlying the program. The change affects banks, brokers, and other persons subject to U.S. sanctions screening and recordkeeping, but preserves prior liabilities and pending matters as of 2024-03-04.

title: Publication of Directive 1 Under Executive Order 14014 of February 10, 2021
summary: OFAC published Directive 1 under Executive Order 14014, confirming that U.S. persons are prohibited from providing, exporting, or reexporting financial services to or for the benefit of Myanma Oil and Gas Enterprise (MOGE) on or after 2023-12-15, unless authorized or licensed. This is a sanctions update affecting Burma-related dealings and screening controls.

title: Memorandum of understanding: between the Financial Conduct Authority and the Bank of England (exercising its prudential regulation functions)
summary: This Memorandum of Understanding updates the coordination and information-sharing framework between the FCA and the Bank of England/PRA. It replaces the 2019 MoU and sets out how the regulators will cooperate on supervision, enforcement, competition and cross-border issues under existing UK legislation. It is effective from April 2024 and does not itself create new firm obligations.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and related Rule 301 edits, reflecting EDGAR Release 24.1. It updates filing mechanics for Inline XBRL, Form 11-K, certain settlement-cycle forms, beneficial ownership filing cut-off times, and removes references tied to the vacated share repurchase disclosure rule. It is effective April 19, 2024.

title: Proposals for the design of the future entity for UK Open Banking
summary: HMT, FCA, PSR and CMA have published a consultation on proposals for the Future Entity for UK open banking and an interim entity. It asks for comments by 2024-05-20 on governance, funding, scope and transition arrangements for the body that will develop open banking standards for ASPSPs and TPPs in the UK.

title: Changes to the taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals
summary: HMT published a policy paper describing planned tax changes for non-UK domiciled individuals that will apply from 6 April 2025. It is an informational technical note for affected individuals and practitioners, and says further updates and draft legislation will follow later in the year.

title: World Bank 109th Development Committee Meeting: UK Governor's statement
summary: The UK Governor’s statement to the World Bank Development Committee calls on the World Bank Group, IMF and international community to increase scale, impact and financing for development, including an ambitious IDA 21 replenishment. It is a policy speech/statement with no direct obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 24 April 2024
summary: This is a joint statement from HM Treasury and the European Commission saying there was good progress on work under the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, including EU invoices to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It does not set rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2022 to June 2023
summary: HM Treasury publishes annual statistical information on basic bank accounts held by the nine designated UK providers for July 2022 to June 2023. It also notes forthcoming legislative changes that will strengthen payment account termination rules and create corresponding changes to basic bank account refusal and termination rules, but this document itself does not change requirements.

title: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: Supervision Report 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury published its 2022-23 AML/CTF Supervision Report for the UK. It reviews the performance of UK AML supervisors, highlights supervisory activity and enforcement, and signals ongoing government work on supervisory reform, updated Money Laundering Regulations and a new effectiveness framework. It is an informational report, not a rule change.

title: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: Supervision Report 2020-22
summary: HM Treasury’s AML/CFT supervision report covers UK supervisors’ activity for 2020-22, including thematic findings, enforcement data and commentary on planned supervisory reform. It is an information-only report and does not itself change rules or set deadlines for firms.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5O, 8M, and 44A
summary: OFAC published web versions of General Licenses 8M, 5O and 44A under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorise certain Venezuela-related transactions for named covered entities and set expiry dates in May and August 2024. Firms dealing with Venezuela, PdVSA or the named entities should check scope, exclusions and remaining validity immediately.

title: Record of Financial Stability Report meetings: December 2020 to April 2024
summary: Record of meetings between the Chancellor and the Governor after each Financial Stability Report, covering December 2020 to April 2024. It is a retrospective policy paper/minutes publication and does not impose new requirements or deadlines on firms.

title: UK and Singapore strengthen collaboration in sustainable finance and FinTech
summary: HM Treasury and the Monetary Authority of Singapore issued a joint statement on their ninth Financial Dialogue, covering cooperation on sustainable finance and FinTech. It is a record of discussions only and does not itself create requirements or deadlines.

title: Sustainability Disclosure Requirements: Implementation Update 2024
summary: HM Treasury sets out an implementation update on the UK’s Sustainability Disclosure Requirements programme. It explains the planned endorsement of ISSB standards as UK Sustainability Reporting Standards, possible future FCA and government disclosure requirements, and forthcoming consultations on transition plan disclosures. No binding requirements are created in this update.

title: Establishment of the Upper Cumberland Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalizes a new codified viticultural area, “Upper Cumberland,” in Middle Tennessee, effective 2024-06-14. The rule updates the AVA list and boundary provisions used on wine labels and in wine advertising. It mainly affects wine producers using geographic origin claims, rather than general banking activities.

title: Privacy policy for the Green Book Network
summary: HM Treasury published a privacy notice for the Green Book Network mailing list. It explains what personal data is collected, the lawful basis for processing, who can access it, retention, and how individuals can exercise UK GDPR rights or complain to the ICO. No new obligations are created for firms; it is informational only.

title: Northern Ireland Executive’s Interim Fiscal Framework
summary: HM Treasury and the Northern Ireland Executive announce an interim fiscal framework for Northern Ireland, including a new 24% needs-based factor in the Barnett formula from 2024-25, increased capital borrowing capacity from 2024-25, and future review points at the relevant Spending Review. It is a policy agreement setting out planned funding arrangements rather than a binding regulatory rule for firms.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, May 2024
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording discussions at the second EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 24 May 2024. It is a public record of the forum under the UK-EU Memorandum of Understanding on Financial Services Cooperation, and does not itself create new requirements.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – May 2024
summary: The Treasury published a progress report on how the UK Government is implementing previously accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across many past parliamentary sessions. It is a status update only and does not create new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Government Action on Fraud in Covid Support Schemes
summary: UK government policy paper announcing action against fraud in Covid support schemes and efforts to recover stolen taxpayer money. It is informational only and does not create new obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8N
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 8N, authorizing certain limited maintenance and wind-down transactions involving PdVSA for specified covered entities until 2024-11-15. It replaces GL 8M and excludes oil transactions, insurance, new services, dividend payments, diluent exports, and new debt or subsidization of PdVSA.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determinations
summary: OFAC published two sanctions determinations under Russian Harmful Foreign Activities regulations. From 2024-04-12, imports into the United States of Russian-origin aluminum, copper and nickel are prohibited, and certain metal-related services tied to those metals are also covered. Firms dealing in these commodities or related services should screen activity and update sanctions controls immediately.

title: Publication of the List of Areas of Northeast and Northwest Syria in Which Activities Are Authorized by 31 CFR 542.533
summary: OFAC published the list of areas in northeast and northwest Syria where activities are authorized under 31 CFR 542.533. The list is effective June 6, 2024 and replaces the prior annex to GL 22. Firms dealing with Syria-related transactions should confirm scope against the updated sanctioned-area list and general license conditions.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 95, 96, and 97
summary: OFAC published General Licenses 95, 96 and 97 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize limited transactions involving specified Russian-related blocked persons and vessels, including civil aviation safety, vessel safety/environmental, and certain wind-down activity, with expirations on July 30, 2024 and June 17, 2024. Firms must check whether any dealings fall within the licenses and stop relying on them after expiry.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General License 28
summary: OFAC published General License 28 under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving Ansarallah for third-country diplomatic and consular missions to Yemen. The license was issued on 2024-02-16 and is now publicly republished. Sanctions teams and operations should use it immediately to assess permitted activity and payment restrictions.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Foreign Terrorist Organization Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13
summary: OFAC published five general licenses under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Foreign Terrorist Organization Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited dealings involving Ansarallah and related entities for specified U.S. government, international organization, NGO, and related activities. These licenses were previously posted on OFAC’s website and were revoked in 2021, so this is a publication of sanctions permissions rather than a new substantive rule.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8I, 13I, and 94
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 8I, 13I and 94 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize limited Russian-related transactions for specified parties and activities, with expirations on July 11, 2024 and November 1, 2024, while also replacing prior versions of GL 8H and setting conditions and exclusions.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-03: Unlawful and Unenforceable Contract Terms and Conditions
summary: The CFPB issued Circular 2024-03 stating that covered persons and service providers can violate the CFPA’s ban on deceptive acts or practices by using unlawful or unenforceable contract terms in consumer financial products and services. It is an interpretive enforcement communication, not a new rule, and it points to examples such as waiver, arbitration, and other prohibited terms.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Regarding Al-Huda Bank as a Financial Institution of Primary Money Laundering Concern
summary: FinCEN imposes a section 311 special measure on Al-Huda Bank, a foreign bank in Iraq found to be of primary money laundering concern. Covered U.S. financial institutions must not open or maintain correspondent accounts for or on behalf of the bank and must take steps to avoid processing related transactions. The rule is effective 2024-08-02.

title: Policy statement on onshore wind
summary: This policy statement changes UK planning policy so onshore wind is treated the same as other energy development in the National Planning Policy Framework. It is a policy announcement, not a rule or consultation, and it does not create direct compliance obligations for banks.

title: Draft Charter for Budget Responsibility text on the fiscal lock
summary: HM Treasury published draft Charter text for the planned fiscal lock, to be incorporated into the Charter for Budget Responsibility in due course. It says the forthcoming Budget Responsibility Bill will require fiscally significant government announcements to receive independent assessment by the OBR. No immediate compliance deadline is set in this paper.
