title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determination
summary: OFAC published a Russia sanctions determination expanding E.O. 14071 prohibitions to IT consultancy and design services, and IT support/cloud services for certain enterprise management and design/manufacturing software. US persons and services exported from the US to persons in Russia are prohibited unless licensed or otherwise authorized. The rule takes effect on 2024-09-12.

title: Interagency Guidance on Reconsiderations of Value of Residential Real Estate Valuations
summary: The OCC and other US agencies issued final interagency guidance on reconsiderations of value for residential real estate valuations. It explains how supervised financial institutions may build ROV processes and controls into risk management and gives example policies to identify and mitigate valuation deficiencies and discrimination. It is effective July 26, 2024 and does not create new legal requirements.

title: Notice of Reporting Instructions Under the Rebuilding Economic Prosperity and Opportunity for Ukrainians Act
summary: OFAC issued reporting instructions for financial institutions holding Russian sovereign assets under the REPO for Ukrainians Act. Covered institutions must report such assets to OFAC by 2024-08-02 or within 10 days of detection, with limited ability to rely on certain existing reports instead of re-reporting. The notice also updates the related reporting form and OMB collection.

title: Changes to the Energy (Oil and Gas) Profits Levy
summary: HM Treasury policy paper announces planned changes to the Energy (Oil and Gas) Profits Levy: the rate will rise to 38% from 1 November 2024, the levy will be extended to 31 March 2030, and investment allowances will be reduced. It is aimed at upstream oil and gas activities and further details will come at the Budget.

title: Fixing the foundations: public spending audit 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury’s public spending audit sets out the government’s spending pressures, immediate savings and planned fiscal framework reforms, with further decisions to be confirmed in the October Budget. It is an informational policy paper and correction slip, not a binding rule or supervisory action for firms.

title: 2024: Non-UK domiciled individuals- Policy Summary
summary: HMT published a policy summary on changes to UK taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals. It says that from 6 April 2025 the government will remove domicile status from the tax system and replace it with a residence-based regime. The note is informational and does not itself create rules, but it signals upcoming tax changes affecting affected individuals and firms supporting them.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-04: Whistleblower Protections Under CFPA Section 1057
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining that overly broad employee confidentiality agreements can violate CFPA section 1057 whistleblower protections if they deter reporting suspected consumer-law violations or cooperation with investigations. It is guidance/interpretation for covered persons and service providers, with no new compliance date.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updated EDGAR Filer Manual Volume II and amended Rule 301 of Regulation S-T, effective 2024-08-09. The update reflects EDGAR Release 24.2, adds filing support for security-based swap execution facility forms, allows Item 1607 SPAC exhibits as EX-98, and removes obsolete Forms 10-KSB and 10-QSB. Filers using EDGAR should align their submission processes now.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 6D, 8J, 25D, 98, 99, and 100
summary: OFAC published six web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified transactions involving agricultural commodities, medicines, medical devices, COVID-19-related activity, clinical trials, and certain energy-related transactions, while preserving listed exclusions and expiry dates. Firms dealing with Russia-related counterparties or payments should check whether their activities fall within the updated license scope and dates.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2023
summary: Minutes for the Government Financial Reporting User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 10 October 2023. The agenda covers updates on local government, a performance report thematic review, ICAEW, GFR review progress, and future thematic reviews, with terms of reference noted only. No new rules, guidance, or obligations are created.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 40C
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions General License 40C, authorizing certain liquefied petroleum gas export/reexport transactions involving Venezuela, PdVSA, and PdVSA-owned entities through 2025-07-08. It replaces GL 40B effective 2024-07-08 and does not authorize certain payments-in-kind or other blocked-person transactions. Sanctions screening and trade/payment controls should be updated immediately.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 13J and 55B
summary: OFAC published two updated general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 13J authorizes certain day-to-day administrative transactions for U.S. persons in Russia through 2024-10-09, and GL 55B authorizes certain Sakhalin-2-related services for crude oil importation into Japan through 2025-06-28. These replace prior versions and exclude otherwise prohibited or blocked-party transactions.

title: Truth in Lending (Regulation Z); Consumer Protections for Home Sales Financed Under Contracts for Deed
summary: The CFPB issued an advisory opinion, effective August 23, 2024, stating that home sales financed under contracts for deed are generally credit transactions under TILA and Regulation Z, and that dwelling-secured transactions generally receive residential mortgage protections. It clarifies existing interpretation rather than creating a new rule.

title: Anti-Money Laundering Regulations for Residential Real Estate Transfers
summary: FinCEN has issued a final rule requiring certain persons involved in residential real estate closings and settlements to report and keep records for certain non-financed transfers to legal entities and trusts nationwide. Transfers to individuals are excluded. The rule is effective 2025-12-01 and will require reporting persons to file Real Estate Reports and retain specified information.

title: Treasury Minutes – September 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to multiple Public Accounts Committee reports. It sets out the government’s comments and planned follow-up on issues such as BBC regional delivery, government resilience, student loans, Universal Credit, health accounts, legal aid, asylum accommodation, mobile connectivity, whistleblowing, home heating and rail reform. It does not create direct obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations and Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 101
summary: OFAC published General License 101 under the Belarus Sanctions Regulations and Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It temporarily authorizes certain civil aviation safety and wind-down transactions involving specified blocked entities through 2024-09-10, subject to stated exclusions. Firms dealing with Belarus/Russia sanctions exposure should check whether any activity is covered and stop relying on it after expiry.

title: Publication of Russia Harmful Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 99A, 100A, and 102
summary: OFAC published three web general licenses under the Russia sanctions regulations: GL 99A, GL 100A and GL 102. The licenses authorize certain wind-down, divestment, settlement, currency conversion and related transactions involving MOEX, NCC, NSD and related blocked entities, with expiries in October and November 2024. Firms must check the scope and expiry dates before relying on them.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 103, 104, 105, 106, and 107
summary: OFAC published five web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing specified transactions tied to imports of certain diamond jewelry/diamonds and limited safety, environmental, and cargo-unloading activities. The licenses were issued on 2024-08-23; some expire in October 2024, while GL 104 runs until 2025-09-01. Firms dealing with Russia-linked trade, shipping, or blocked persons should check whether any activity falls within the new authorizations.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5P
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 5P, replacing GL 5O. From 2024-11-12, it authorizes certain transactions and financing related to Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% Bond, subject to the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations and other OFAC restrictions. Firms dealing in Venezuela-related assets or payments should check whether their activity is newly authorized.

title: Joint statement on the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting - September 2024
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury published a joint statement recording the tenth UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It summarises topics discussed and outcomes, but does not create or change requirements for firms.

title: Income Taxes
summary: This is a CFR correction to Title 26, Part 1, removing an incorrectly included paragraph in section 1.430(h)(2)-1. It applies to the US tax regulations as published in the CFR and takes effect as a technical correction published on 2024-09-11.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Determinations
summary: OFAC publishes determinations under the Russian sanctions regime, including a determination on foreign financial institutions and new/amended determinations covering certain Russian-origin goods such as fish/seafood and gold. These sanctions are already effective, including one that took effect on 2023-12-22. Firms involved in payments, trade, or correspondent banking with Russia should review exposure now.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 25E, 25F, 108, and 109
summary: OFAC published web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain telecom, internet communications and related transactions with Russia, subject to stated exclusions. GL 25E supersedes GL 25D; GL 25F supersedes GL 25E. GLs 108 and 109 are also published, with stated expiry dates in November 2024. Sanctions teams should check whether any Russia-related activity relies on these authorisations.

title: Publication of Global Magnitsky Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8.
summary: OFAC published Global Magnitsky Sanctions General License 8, authorizing certain transactions involving entities blocked solely because of Ly Yong Phat or L.Y.P. Group interests, if those entities are not separately designated. It is effective from 2024-09-12 and is relevant for sanctions screening, payments and transaction processing.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2018-19
summary: HM Treasury publishes best-practice examples for central government annual reports and accounts, illustrating how departments should present performance, accountability and financial information. It points to expectations under the FReM, including clear narrative, trend data and accessible reporting, for those preparing ARAs across government. No new filing date is set, but the guidance is relevant to reporting periods covered by the FReM.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-05: Improper Overdraft Opt-In Practices
summary: The CFPB issued a circular saying banks and credit unions can violate EFTA and Regulation E if they cannot show affirmative consumer consent before charging overdraft fees on ATM and one-time debit card transactions. It also reminds firms to retain compliance records for at least two years. The circular is effective on publication and is relevant to overdraft practices and evidence of opt-in controls.

title: The Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024
summary: The UK Treasury has drafted regulations amending the Payment Services Regulations 2017. Payment service providers may delay certain domestic sterling payment orders where there are reasonable grounds to suspect fraud or dishonesty, must notify the payer promptly, and may be liable for charges and interest if delay occurs. The regulations come into force on a stated date to be inserted.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2022-23
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy note on the 2022-23 Welsh Rates of Income Tax reconciliation. It explains how HMRC outturn data updates Welsh Government funding and block grant adjustments, resulting in a net £53 million increase in overall funding for 2025-26. No obligations are created for firms.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8H
summary: OFAC published General License 8H under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain energy-related transactions involving specified Russian banks and the Central Bank of the Russian Federation through 2024-05-01, subject to stated exclusions. It replaces GL 8G and is relevant to firms dealing in cross-border payments, trade finance or other sanctioned transactions.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 76A
summary: OFAC published General License 76A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving certain blocked Russian entities through 2024-01-31, subject to stated exclusions. It replaces General License 76. Firms dealing with sanctioned persons or Russia-related transactions should check whether current activity falls within the authorization.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 79 and 80
summary: OFAC published General Licenses 79 and 80 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. They authorize limited wind-down, divestment, settlement and derivative-termination transactions involving specified blocked Russian entities and Highland Gold Mining Limited through 2024-03-11, subject to restrictions and exclusions.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving PM2BTC
summary: FinCEN issued a final order, effective 2024-10-11, prohibiting certain fund transmittals involving PM2BTC, a non-U.S. virtual asset service provider identified as a primary money laundering concern linked to Russian illicit finance. Covered financial institutions must stop the prohibited transmittals immediately.

title: National Wealth Fund: Mobilising Private Investment
summary: HM Treasury sets out plans to turn UK Infrastructure Bank into the National Wealth Fund, with a broader mandate to mobilise private capital into clean energy, infrastructure and wider industrial strategy priorities. It describes the fund’s intended structure, capitalisation and investment approach, but does not itself create binding obligations for firms.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee - 3 October 2024
summary: A UK government communiqué reports on a meeting of the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee held on 3 October 2024. It is informational only and does not create or change any rules or obligations for firms.

title: Financial Services Policy Update
summary: HMT publishes a policy update on the UK special resolution regime, noting the Bank of England’s consultation on changes to MREL setting and the planned update to the Code of Practice. It is an informational update, not itself a rule change, and signals future consultation and possible secondary legislation affecting banks, especially around resolution and MREL calibration.

title: Commission Guidance Regarding the Listing of Voluntary Carbon Credit Derivative Contracts
summary: The CFTC issued final guidance for designated contract markets on listing voluntary carbon credit derivative contracts. It sets factors to consider on contract design, market manipulation risk, monitoring underlying markets, and product submission requirements under existing CFTC rules. The guidance is issued on 2024-10-15 and applies to DCMs and firms involved in listing these products.

title: UK Government Green Financing: Allocation Report 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s 2024 Green Financing Allocation Report explains how UK sovereign green bond and Green Savings Bond proceeds raised in 2023–24 were allocated to eligible green expenditures. It is an annual transparency report on the government’s green financing programme, not a rule change. No new compliance deadline or obligation is created for firms.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC adopted updates to the EDGAR Filer Manual and related Rule 301 changes, effective 2024-10-22. The changes update electronic filing procedures, including co-registrants in certain draft registration statements, Inline XBRL filing for SBSEF reports, and a cybersecurity taxonomy for relevant SEC filings. Filers using EDGAR should update their filing processes and systems immediately.

title: Publication of Western Balkans Stabilization Regulations Web General Licenses 3A, 4, and 5
summary: OFAC published Western Balkans Stabilization Regulations General Licenses 3A, 4 and 5, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions and wind-down activity involving specified blocked entities. General License 3A replaced GL 3 effective 2024-06-18, and GL 4 permits wind-down transactions through 2024-08-17. Sanctions screening and payment controls should be updated immediately for the named persons and any 50%+ owned entities.

title: Treasury Minutes – October 2024
summary: Treasury Minutes 2024 is HM Treasury’s government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on government finance, BBC regional delivery, non-executive appointments, and major project value for money. It records the government’s responses and planned next steps, including future consideration of recommendations, but it does not itself create new regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 30 and 31
summary: OFAC published two Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations general licenses that authorize certain wind-down, divestment, transfer, clearing, settlement, and derivative close-out transactions involving specified blocked persons. The licenses were issued on 2024-10-07 and expire on 2024-11-21. U.S. persons and firms dealing with the named parties must follow the scope limits and blocked-account requirements.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13K
summary: OFAC published General License 13K under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, replacing General License 13J. It authorizes certain day-to-day administrative transactions for U.S. persons and entities they own or control in Russia, including taxes, fees, import duties, and certain permits and registrations, through 2025-01-08, subject to stated limits.

title: World Bank 110th Development Committee meeting 2024: UK Governor's statement
summary: UK ministers’ written statement to the World Bank Development Committee calls for a fairer global financial system, stronger support for fragile states and conflict zones, and the largest ever IDA replenishment. It is a policy position statement only and does not create requirements for firms.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 25 October 2024
summary: A joint statement from HMT and the European Commission says the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions made good progress on work streams about EU invoices to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is informational only and does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: Post-implementation review of the Bank Referral Scheme
summary: HM Treasury published a post-implementation review of the Bank Referral Scheme for SMEs under the Small and Medium Sized Business (Finance Platforms) Regulations 2015. It says the scheme has broadly met its objectives, but identifies frictions, data issues and possible scope for a less burdensome design. HMT plans a future consultation to consider whether changes are needed.

title: Tackling offshore tax non-compliance
summary: HMRC/HMT published a policy paper on the UK government’s strategy for tackling offshore tax non-compliance. It describes HMRC’s approach and additional resources announced at Autumn Budget 2024, but does not itself impose new rules or deadlines.

title: Corporate Tax Roadmap 2024
summary: HM Treasury published a corporate tax roadmap setting out its intended approach to Corporation Tax for the rest of Parliament, including stability on rates, capital allowances, R&D reliefs, intangible assets and territorial taxation, plus planned consultations and improved guidance. It is a policy/roadmap document for businesses and investors, not a binding rule. No immediate compliance date is stated.

title: Response to the OBR review of the March 2024 forecast for departmental expenditure limits
summary: HM Treasury published a government response to the OBR’s review of the March 2024 forecast for departmental expenditure limits. It explains the evidence provided to the OBR, updates on spending pressures and control totals, and the Treasury’s response to the OBR’s recommendations. It is an informational government document and does not create regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury publishes a review of best-practice examples from 2022-23 government annual reports and accounts. It is a guidance-style reference document for public-sector reporting teams, highlighting clear, balanced, transparent narrative and financial reporting, but it does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Transforming business rates
summary: HM Treasury has published a policy paper on reforming business rates in England and Wales. It sets out the government’s intended direction, including lower multipliers for retail, hospitality and leisure properties from April 2026-27, and invites engagement on further reform options. This is a consultation-style discussion document rather than a final rule, with no immediate compliance action required beyond monitoring and responding by stakeholders.

title: Terms of reference for the review of technology adoption
summary: HMT published terms of reference for a cross-government review of barriers to technology adoption for growth, innovation and productivity. It sets the review’s scope and asks the Government Chief Scientific Adviser and National Technology Adviser to lead it, with recommendations feeding into the industrial strategy and sector plans alongside the spring Spending Review. No obligations are created for firms.

title: Autumn Budget 2024
summary: HMT’s Autumn Budget 2024 sets out the UK government’s fiscal, tax, welfare and spending plans, including new fiscal rules and a new Charter for Budget Responsibility. It is a policy and budget announcement rather than a regulatory instrument, so it does not itself create direct compliance obligations for firms. Some measures may flow into later legislation or consultations.

title: Reforming the taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals
summary: HM Treasury sets out draft policy changes to UK taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals from 6 April 2025, replacing domicile-based rules with a residence-based regime, including a 4-year foreign income and gains relief, changes to trust and anti-avoidance rules, a Temporary Repatriation Facility, updated overseas workday relief, and inheritance tax reforms. It is aimed at affected individuals and their advisers, with draft legislation still subject to Parliament.

title: Post-implementation review of the Commercial Credit Data Sharing scheme
summary: HM Treasury published a post-implementation review of the UK Commercial Credit Data Sharing scheme. It finds CCDS continues to meet its objectives but highlights data-quality and access issues, and says it intends to explore possible enhancements through a future consultation. No new requirements are created in this paper.

title: A strong fiscal framework
summary: HM Treasury explains the UK government’s updated fiscal framework and Charter for Budget Responsibility. It sets out new fiscal rules for the stability and investment framework, including a current budget balance rule and a debt reduction rule based on public sector net financial liabilities. The document is explanatory policy material, not a rule itself, but it signals the framework now in place for the Parliament.

title: Agricultural property relief and business property relief reforms
summary: HMT published a policy paper announcing planned reforms to agricultural property relief and business property relief for inheritance tax from 6 April 2026, and an extension of agricultural property relief to certain environmental land management agreements from 6 April 2025. This is informational and sets out the government’s intended changes, not a binding instrument itself.

title: Soft Drinks Industry Levy review
summary: HM Treasury and HMRC published a policy paper announcing a review of the Soft Drinks Industry Levy’s sugar thresholds and exemptions for milk-based and milk substitute drinks. It is not a rule change; it sets out the review’s scope and invites stakeholder input, with responses open until 2025-07-21.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2023 to 2024
summary: Annual report and accounts for the UK National Insurance Fund Investment Account for year ended 31 March 2024. It describes how the fund was invested, performance, governance and audit information; it does not create new obligations for firms. No action date is set.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the Bank of England, FCA and PRA
summary: This Memorandum of Understanding sets out how the FCA, PRA and Bank of England will coordinate under the UK critical third parties regime in FSMA, including the new consultation and coordination forum, information sharing, and how they will handle recommendations and policy differences. It is laid before Parliament and reflects the framework in force from November 2024 for firms in scope of the CTP regime.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-06: Background Dossiers and Algorithmic Scores for Hiring, Promotion, and Other Employment Decisions
summary: The CFPB issued a circular explaining that employers using background dossiers, algorithmic scores and similar third-party consumer reports for hiring, promotion, reassignment or retention must comply with the Fair Credit Reporting Act. It highlights permissions, adverse-action notices and permissible-purpose limits, and also reminds consumer reporting agencies of accuracy, disclosure and dispute-investigation duties. No new compliance date is stated.

title: Burma Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC has issued a final rule reissuing and expanding the Burma Sanctions Regulations, effective 2024-11-13. The rule adds interpretive guidance, definitions, general licenses and other provisions, and incorporates a sectoral sanctions directive under Executive Order 14014. Firms dealing with U.S.-connected property or persons should update sanctions controls immediately.

title: Next steps for reforming the UK Markets in Financial Instruments Directive
summary: HM Treasury announced planned technical reforms to the UK MiFID framework, including giving the FCA stronger tools over off-exchange commodity derivatives trading and revoking detailed legislation on investment firm organisation, operation and transaction reporting. The changes need legislation and will be timed so replacement rules are ready before revocations commence.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 8K, 25G, 110, 111, and 112
summary: OFAC published five web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited Russia-related transactions, including energy-related dealings and telecommunications/internet communications. GLs 8K and 25G replace earlier versions and the authorizations run through the stated expiry dates unless renewed. Firms dealing with Russia-linked counterparties or services should update sanctions screening and transaction handling accordingly.

title: Publication of Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License 10
summary: OFAC published Belarus Sanctions Regulations General License 10, authorizing wind-down transactions involving Tabak Invest LLC and related entities until 2024-02-02 at 12:01 a.m. EST, subject to payment into a blocked account at a U.S. financial institution. The license is now expired, and no further transactions are authorized absent separate authorization.

title: Pensions Investment Review: interim report
summary: HM Treasury’s interim Pensions Investment Review sets out the government’s policy direction on consolidating defined contribution workplace pensions and reforming the Local Government Pension Scheme to support longer-term investment in UK productive assets. It is an interim report and calls ahead to further consultations and the upcoming Pensions Schemes Bill; it does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Publication of an Iran-Related Determination
summary: OFAC published an Iran-related sector determination applying E.O. 13902 sanctions to persons operating in Iran’s petroleum and petrochemical sectors. The determination took effect on 2024-10-11 and expands the sectors subject to blocking sanctions. Sanctions teams and operations should treat the new sector coverage as immediately effective.

title: Publication of Covid-Related Web General License Related to Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations and Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations
summary: OFAC republishes General License N, which authorizes certain COVID-19-related transactions with Iran and under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations, subject to conditions and exclusions. The license was effective through 2022 and is now presented as a web publication of the existing authorization. Sanctions teams should confirm current applicability before any Iran- or terrorism-related activity.

title: Meeting minutes – October 2024
summary: Minutes of a meeting between the Chancellor and the Governor of the Bank of England about the latest Financial Stability Report. It is a published record of a required meeting, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory action. No direct obligations or deadlines are created for firms.

title: Debt Collection Practices (Regulation F); Deceptive and Unfair Collection of Medical Debt
summary: The CFPB revised the effective date of its advisory opinion on debt collection practices and medical debt to January 2, 2025. The advisory opinion itself is not binding and does not change firms’ obligations under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act.

title: Publication of Western Balkans Stabilization Regulations Web General License 5A
summary: OFAC published General License 5A under the Western Balkans Stabilization Regulations. It authorizes certain transactions needed to manufacture, distribute, install, operate, maintain, or repair specified drinking-water pumps linked to named entities, effective November 6, 2024, and replaces General License 5.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 11 December 2024
summary: A UK government policy paper publishes the provisional agenda for a UK-EU joint committee meeting under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement on 11 December 2024. It is an agenda notice only and does not itself create or change any obligations.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: 2025-26 Pay Round
summary: HM Treasury publishes economic evidence for the 2025-26 Public Sector Pay Review Body round. It is background material on inflation, productivity, labour market conditions and fiscal context for frontline public sector pay decisions; it does not itself set pay rules or obligations for firms. No direct compliance action is created for banks.

title: India-UK 3rd Financial Markets Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and India’s Ministry of Finance issued a joint statement on the third India-UK Financial Markets Dialogue. It describes discussions on capital markets, insurance, pensions, fintech, financial data and sustainable finance to support cross-border trade and investment, but it does not create any new requirements or deadlines.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 53A, 55C, 113, and 114
summary: OFAC published four Russian sanctions general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. The licenses authorize specified transactions involving Russian missions, Gazprombank, and Sakhalin-2-related activity, with some replacements of prior licenses and expiries through 2025 or earlier. Financial institutions and other U.S. persons dealing with Russia-linked activity should check the new authorizations and expiry dates.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5Q and 8O
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 5Q and 8O under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. GL 5Q authorizes certain transactions involving PdVSA's 2020 8.5% bond on or after 2025-03-07, replacing GL 5P. GL 8O authorizes limited maintenance or wind-down transactions for specified entities through 2025-05-09, subject to exclusions. Sanctions teams should update screening and payments handling immediately.

title: Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales
summary: The IRS issued final regulations requiring brokers that regularly effect digital asset sales to file information returns and furnish payee statements reporting gross proceeds on customer digital asset dispositions. The rules are effective 2025-02-28, with applicability dates in the regulation. Firms active as digital asset brokers or similar intermediaries should update reporting processes and controls.

title: Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-07: Design, Marketing, and Administration of Credit Card Rewards Programs
summary: The CFPB issued Circular 2024-07 on credit card rewards programs, stating that issuers and their service providers may violate UDAAP rules if rewards are devalued, hard to redeem, or points are deducted without receiving the promised benefit. It affects covered persons offering, providing, or operating rewards programs and their service providers. No compliance date is given; the circular was released on 2024-12-18.

title: 2025 UK-China Economic and Financial Dialogue: policy outcomes
summary: HMT published a policy paper/fact sheet on the outcomes of the 2025 UK-China Economic and Financial Dialogue. It is an informational government publication summarising bilateral discussions and outcomes, with no direct rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Truth in Lending (Regulation Z); Consumer Credit Offered to Borrowers in Advance of Expected Receipt of Compensation for Work
summary: The CFPB rescinds a 2020 advisory opinion on one type of earned wage access product under Regulation Z and the Truth in Lending Act. The rescission is applicable from 2025-01-15 and affects providers offering consumer credit in advance of expected wages. Firms offering paycheck advance or earned wage products should reassess Truth in Lending treatment and related disclosures.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory policy note on the 2022-23 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC and population data are used to update Scottish Government funding and says the net effect is a £451 million increase in overall funding for 2025-26. No firm obligations are created.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: Autumn 2024
summary: The UK government updated the Charter for Budget Responsibility, which sets the fiscal policy framework, fiscal mandate, debt management approach and guidance to the OBR. It is laid before Parliament under the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011 and applies to UK fiscal policy; no bank-specific compliance deadline is set out in the excerpt.

title: Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 122
summary: The SEC issued Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 122, effective 2025-01-30, rescinding prior guidance in Topic 5.FF on accounting for obligations to safeguard crypto-assets held for platform users. Entities should apply contingency liability recognition and measurement under FASB ASC 450-20 or IAS 37, with retrospective application for annual periods beginning after 2024-12-15 and related disclosure expectations.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
primary_functions: Regulatory change; Compliance; Ops; Product; Prudential
summary: The SEC updated EDGAR Filing Manual Volume II and related filing formats, effective 2025-01-30. Filers using EDGAR, including Form SHO reporters and issuers/registrants affected by new annuity filing requirements and Form 24F-2 changes, must use the revised manual and updated system formats for submissions.

title: UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the Japan Financial Services Agency published a joint statement recording the third UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum meeting and its key discussion points and outcomes. It is informational only and does not create obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: 2025 Retrocession Agreement between HM Treasury and Pool Re
summary: HM Treasury and Pool Re have entered into a new 2025 retrocession agreement, replacing earlier 1993, 2015 and 2019 arrangements and updating the terms of the 2022 agreement. It sets the indemnity, retention and payment mechanics for terrorism risk cover from the effective date, with the new arrangement referenced as taking effect from 1 April 2025. This is relevant to firms using Pool Re-backed terrorism insurance structures.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2025
summary: HM Treasury published the 2025 public service pensions increase note and multiplier tables. Public service pensions in payment for at least a year rise by 1.7% from 7 April 2025, with shorter-duration pensions increased proportionately. Scheme administrators should use the tables to apply the annual increase correctly.

title: UK CBAM International Group
summary: HMT has published terms of reference for a UK CBAM International Group. It is a forum for communicating UK CBAM policy updates and gathering feedback from international stakeholders; countries can apply for membership and meetings will be held at least annually. No new obligations or dates are created.

title: NS&I main estimates memorandum 2024 to 2025 (July 2024)
summary: National Savings and Investments’ Main Estimates memorandum for 2024-25 explains its spending controls, budget totals, efficiency plans and performance priorities. It is a parliamentary estimates document describing planned funding and operations, not a rule, supervisory notice or enforcement action. No compliance deadline or obligation is created for firms.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, February 2025
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording topics discussed at the third EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum. It is informational only and does not create or change requirements for firms.

title: Memorandum of Understanding Between HM Treasury and the Bank of England 2025
summary: HM Treasury and the Bank of England updated their Memorandum of Understanding after a 5-year review of the Bank’s capital framework. The review says the existing target, floor and ceiling remain adequate and the financial arrangements support the Bank’s transition to a repo-backed operating framework. No new firm obligations are set for market participants.

title: Technical Amendments to Commission Rules and Forms
summary: The SEC adopted technical amendments to numerous rules and forms under the Securities Act and Exchange Act, correcting typographical errors, outdated references and cross-references. The changes were effective on 2025-02-18 and apply to SEC-registered securities filings and related forms. No new substantive requirements were introduced.

title: Meeting minutes – January 2025
summary: Meeting minutes record the Chancellor and Bank of England Governor’s statutory post-Financial Stability Report discussion. It does not create or change obligations for firms and is for awareness only.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee - 27 February 2025
summary: This is a communiqué from the UK Finance Interministerial Standing Committee describing a regular ministerial meeting on economic and finance matters. It is informational only and does not create or change rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Fourth Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin Minutes
summary: Minutes of the fourth UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is an informational policy paper about customs cooperation and rules of origin matters; it does not itself create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Chancellor meeting with Gilt-edged Market Makers: Minutes
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes of the Chancellor’s meeting with gilt market primary dealer firms (GEMMs) on 6 March 2025. It is an informational record of an engagement session on UK and global economic prospects and does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update 2024
summary: HM Treasury published a progress update on its own Women in Finance Charter commitments, including a rise in female senior management representation to 50% as of March 2024. It is an informational update on the department’s progress and future priorities, not a new rule or requirement for firms.

title: Performance Review of Digital Spend
summary: HM Treasury publishes a review of digital spend in government, with recommendations on funding models, training, guidance and outcome metrics for public-sector DDaT spending. It is aimed at UK central government spending decisions for SR25/SR27, not regulated financial firms. No binding requirements or compliance dates are created.

title: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: Supervision Report 2023-24
summary: HM Treasury published its annual AML/CTF Supervision Report 2023-24, describing how UK supervisors registered and monitored supervised firms, used enforcement, and supported compliance during the year. It is a retrospective transparency report, not a rule or supervisory direction. It may inform future reform of the MLRs and supervisory system, but it does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Issuance of a Geographic Targeting Order Imposing Additional Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements on Certain Money Services Businesses Along the Southwest Border
summary: FinCEN issued a Geographic Targeting Order effective 2025-04-14 for certain money services businesses along the southwest border. Covered businesses must report currency transactions over $200 and up to $10,000 on CTRs within 15 days, retain records, and verify the identity of persons presenting the transactions. Existing BSA obligations remain in place.

title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive Organisational Regulation – Draft Statutory Instrument and Policy Note
summary: The UK Treasury laid a draft statutory instrument to amend FSMA 2000, the Regulated Activities Order, recognition requirements and MiFIR-related retained law. It changes organisational and trading-rule provisions for investment firms and markets, including suspension/removal from trading, position reporting and execution/client order rules. It comes into force when the FSMA 2023 revocation of MiFID organisational requirements takes effect.

title: Announcement of Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise for the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) Pilot
summary: HMT and the DMO announced a preliminary market engagement exercise for the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot, seeking industry views to inform the pilot’s design and commercial strategy. It is aimed at potential suppliers and investors in the UK financial services sector. Responses to the engagement notice are due by 13 April 2025.

title: Statement of Strategic Priorities to the National Wealth Fund
summary: HM Treasury sets out the government’s strategic priorities for the National Wealth Fund and asks it to produce a new Strategic Plan aligned to growth and clean energy missions. It also signals that legislation will be introduced when parliamentary time allows to broaden the Fund’s mandate beyond infrastructure. This is directed at the NWF, not firms generally.

title: Launch of the UK Strategic Public Investment Forum
summary: The UK Treasury published a policy paper launching a new Strategic Public Investment Forum and summarising the public financial institutions landscape. It is an internal government coordination initiative for UK-investing public financial organisations and senior civil servants, with no direct obligations for firms and no compliance deadline.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant Review 2025-26
summary: This is a statutory report under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 setting out the Royal Trustees’ determination of the Sovereign Grant for 2025-26 and how it was calculated. It applies to the UK public finance arrangements for the Royal Household, with no direct obligations for regulated firms. No action date for firms is set.

title: Spring Statement 2025 document
summary: The UK Spring Statement 2025 is a government fiscal and policy announcement setting out spending, defence, planning and growth measures. It does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms, though it references future reform and investment plans. No direct compliance action date is stated in the excerpt.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – March 2025
summary: A Treasury Minutes progress report updating Parliament on the Government’s progress implementing Public Accounts Committee recommendations across many prior reports and sessions. It is an accountability/status document, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice, and it imposes no direct obligations on firms.

title: Debt management report 2025-26
summary: HM Treasury’s annual Debt Management Report sets out the UK government’s 2025-26 borrowing plans, debt management policy, and the financing remits for the DMO, NS&I and Exchequer cash management. It is an informational policy paper, not a rule or consultation, and does not create direct obligations for firms. The report is relevant mainly for market awareness.

title: Supporting documents for Spring Statement 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s Spring Statement 2025 supporting analysis sets out the expected distributional impact of tax, welfare and public service spending decisions on UK households in 2028-29. It is an explanatory policy paper, not a rule or consultation, and creates no direct obligations. The publication is for awareness of the policy package and its household-income effects.

title: Treasury Minutes – April 2025
summary: Treasury Minutes: April 2025 is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports across several departments, including HMRC, DfE, DWP, the Home Office and others. It records government agreement or disagreement with PAC recommendations and proposed follow-up actions and target dates, but it does not itself create new legal or regulatory obligations for firms.

title: UK-India 13th Economic and Financial Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: UK and India’s finance ministers issued a joint statement on deepening economic and financial cooperation, including trade, capital markets, listings, pensions, insurance and rupee internationalisation. It notes future collaboration and regulatory cooperation, but it does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting – March 2025
summary: Record of a meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA about the FCA’s Perimeter Report and the financial services regulatory perimeter. It is informational only and does not change rules or impose deadlines for firms.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the OBR and HMT – macroeconomic models
summary: HM Treasury and the OBR publish a non-binding memorandum of understanding setting out joint governance, management, development and transparency arrangements for shared macroeconomic models. It describes model ownership, access, maintenance and review processes, but does not create legal obligations or compliance deadlines for firms.

title: Reappointment of Financial Conduct Authority Chief Executive Officer
summary: HM Treasury reappoints the FCA Chief Executive for a second five-year term and sets expectations for the FCA to embed its competitiveness and growth objective, maintain consumer protection and market integrity, and work with government on reducing regulatory burden and developing a Financial Services Growth and Competitiveness Strategy.

title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers and Large Hedge Fund Advisers
summary: The SEC and CFTC adopted final amendments to Form PF for private fund advisers, correcting errors and cross-references and restoring omitted text. The changes apply to SEC-registered private fund advisers, including those also registered as CPOs or CTAs, and are effective April 11, 2025, with the broader Final Form PF compliance date previously extended to June 12, 2025.

title: Simplification of Share Insurance and Succession Planning Final Rules; Solicitation of Comments
summary: The NCUA is not issuing a new rule here; it is asking for 60 days of public comment on two already-final rules, Simplification of Share Insurance and Succession Planning, because they have not yet fully taken effect. Comments are due by 2025-06-23. The notice affects federally insured credit unions and is for awareness and potential regulatory-change tracking.

title: Government response: Bringing goods into the UK temporarily
summary: HM Treasury and HMRC published a policy response announcing planned simplifications to the UK Temporary Admission customs procedure for traders importing goods temporarily. The changes cover timing requirements, guidance, and eligibility/use restrictions, and are expected to be implemented during 2025. No exact commencement date is given.

title: Economic Crime Levy Report 2023-24
summary: HM Treasury’s report explains how the Economic Crime Levy was collected and spent in 2023-24, including funding allocated to anti-money laundering and economic crime programmes. It is an informational annual report on levy operation and spending, not a new rule. No action date is set, though it notes the levy has applied since 2022-23 and funding allocations ran from 2023-24 onward.

title: Interpretive Rules, Policy Statements, and Advisory Opinions; Withdrawal
summary: The CFPB withdraws many guidance documents, interpretive rules, policy statements and advisory opinions, effective 2025-05-12. The bureau says the materials should not be enforced or relied on while it reviews them, and may later retain or reissue some. This affects CFPB-regulated consumer finance firms, including banks and credit unions, but does not itself create new substantive obligations.

title: Sanctions implementation and enforcement: cross-government review, May 2025
summary: This UK policy paper sets out the background, objectives and conclusions of a cross-government review of sanctions implementation and enforcement. It is an intelligence-style publication with no direct rule changes, compliance deadline or enforcement action. Firms should note the strategic direction only, with sanctions/financial crime teams monitoring for any follow-on measures.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a Government response to the Public Accounts Committee on several 2024-25 reports, including NHS financial sustainability and public charge points for electric vehicles. It records the Government’s agreement or response to committee recommendations and cites target implementation points such as December 2025 for NHS planning guidance, but it does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Pensions Investment Review: Final Report
summary: HMT’s final report on the Pensions Investment Review sets out the government’s conclusions and planned direction for pensions reform, including larger DC schemes, LGPS consolidation, and measures to deepen the UK investment pipeline. It is a policy report and roadmap rather than a rule, but it signals future legislation and further phases of review. No immediate compliance deadline is stated.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 11 December 2024
summary: Minutes of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes on 11 December 2024. The discussion covered UK association to Horizon Europe and Copernicus, participation trends, security-related exclusions, future collaboration after 2027, visa and health surcharge costs, and implementation issues with financial provisions. It records dialogue and intentions only, with no new binding requirements.

title: Green Book Review 2025: Findings and actions
summary: HM Treasury publishes the 2025 Green Book Review findings and planned actions on UK public-sector appraisal guidance. It discusses simplifying and shortening guidance, improving treatment of transformational and place-based projects, and publishing business cases for major projects. No binding requirements are created for financial services firms.

title: Government Response to the 2024 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response explains the government’s fiscal framework reforms and how they relate to the 2024 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report. It is informational only and does not create binding requirements for firms. The document references fiscal rules, OBR reporting, contingent liabilities and broader economic policy changes.

title: Northern Ireland Interim Fiscal Framework Implementation Update: Relative Funding Methodology
summary: HM Treasury published an implementation update explaining the methodology for measuring relative funding between the Northern Ireland Executive and comparable UK Government spending. It sets out how the Barnett-related needs-based factor is assessed, including treatment of block grant funding, tax devolution, and non-domestic rates. It is informational and does not itself create new compliance deadlines or obligations.

title: Departmental Efficiency Delivery Plans
summary: UK government policy paper setting out Spending Review 2025 departmental efficiency plans and targets across Whitehall, including planned savings through 2028-29. It is informational only and does not create obligations for regulated firms. No action dates or compliance deadlines are set for the bank.

title: Tax Policy Making Principles
summary: HM Treasury sets out high-level principles for UK tax policy making: a single major fiscal event cycle, targeted consultation where needed, and greater transparency on rationales and impact. It is an explanatory policy paper only and does not itself change tax law or create deadlines.

title: Update: domestic premises suppliers and Buy-Now, Pay-Later (BNPL)
summary: The UK government will lay a negative statutory instrument to exempt domestic premises suppliers from needing credit broking permissions to offer BNPL as a payment option. This affects firms selling on domestic premises and using BNPL, and it will become binding once the SI is laid and takes effect under the exemption.

title: Treasury Minutes – June 2025
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Committee of Public Accounts reports on government AI, energy bills support, COVID-19 loans, NHS dentistry and biomass. It records government positions and planned actions for departments, including timelines for some follow-up work, but does not create rules or obligations for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: March 2025
summary: Minutes of HMT’s User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting on 5 March 2025. The paper is informational only and covers IFRS 18/19, the government financial reporting framework, local government updates, and a thematic review of non-investment asset valuation changes, including prospective historic-cost treatment for intangible assets from 1 April 2025.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2024
summary: Minutes of the User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 10 October 2024. The paper records discussion updates on IFRS 18 and 19, a thematic review of non-investment assets, Whole of Government Accounts, local government matters and GFR review progress. It does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: April 2024
summary: HM Treasury published minutes and agenda for the User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting on 11 April 2024. The paper discusses public-sector financial reporting topics including the FReM, performance reporting, Sustainability Reporting, WGA cycle updates and related consultation/activity items. It is informational and does not itself change requirements or set deadlines for firms.

title: UK Infrastructure: A 10 Year Strategy
summary: HM Treasury published a 10-year UK infrastructure strategy setting out the government’s long-term priorities for economic, housing and social infrastructure, alongside the new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority. It is an नीति/strategy paper rather than a binding rule and does not itself impose compliance deadlines on firms.

title: UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group June 2025: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and U.S. Treasury issued a joint statement recording the 11th UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting and summarising topics discussed and outcomes. It is informational only and does not itself create or change requirements.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 25 June 2025
summary: This is a joint statement from HM Treasury and the European Commission on progress in the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions. It is informational only and does not create or change obligations for firms.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 26 June 2025
summary: A UK government communiqué reports on a meeting of the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee on 26 June 2025. It is an informational policy paper with no rule change, obligation, or deadline for firms.

title: Supporting documents for Spending Review 2025
summary: HM Treasury published a distributional analysis paper for Spending Review 2025 showing estimated household impacts of tax, welfare and public service spending decisions in 2028-29. It is an analytical companion document only and does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: 10 Year Infrastructure Strategy Working Paper
summary: HM Treasury’s working paper sets out the UK government’s planned 10-year infrastructure strategy and invites stakeholder views. It is a discussion paper only: it describes intended priorities, governance and pipeline design for UK social, economic and housing infrastructure, with publication planned for June alongside the Spending Review. No obligations are created yet.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving CIBanco S.A., Institución De Banca Multiple
summary: FinCEN issued an order imposing a special measure that prohibits certain transmittals of funds involving CIBanco S.A., a Mexico-based bank identified as a primary money laundering concern linked to illicit opioid trafficking. The order is effective 21 days after publication in the Federal Register and applies to covered U.S. financial institutions.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving Vector Casa de Bolsa, S.A. de C.V.
summary: FinCEN issues a notice ordering a special measure that prohibits certain funds transmittals involving Mexico-based Vector Casa de Bolsa, S.A. de C.V. The action takes effect 21 days after publication in the Federal Register and applies to covered U.S. financial institutions. It is a sanctions/financial-crime restriction under FEND Off Fentanyl Act authority.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving Intercam Banco S.A., Institución de Banca Multiple
summary: FinCEN issued an order imposing a special measure that prohibits certain transmittals of funds involving Mexico-based Intercam Banco, effective 21 days after Federal Register publication. Covered U.S. financial institutions must block the relevant funds transfers and comply with the new restriction.

title: Spending Review 2025 document
summary: HM Treasury’s Spending Review 2025 is a government policy paper setting out public spending plans. It is informational and does not itself impose regulatory obligations on banks or other regulated firms.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC updated the EDGAR Filer Manual and Regulation S-T to reflect EDGAR Release 25.2 and the EDGAR Next changes. Filers using EDGAR, including open-end fund filers reporting on Form N-CEN, must follow the updated filing instructions; Version 76 is a preview until the September 15, 2025 compliance date, when EDGAR Next validations are expected to apply.

title: Ancillary Activities Exemption – Draft Legislation
summary: HM Treasury publishes draft legislation to replace the existing ancillary activities test for the commodity derivatives exemption with a simpler FCA-led regime. It would revoke current test elements, give the FCA rulemaking power over the new test and threshold, and is open for technical comments by 28 August 2025. The new regime is expected to come into force on 1 January 2027.

title: 10th UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue July 2025: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the Monetary Authority of Singapore published a joint statement recording the discussion and outcomes of the 10th UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue. It is a summary of what was discussed, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory requirement, so it creates no direct obligations.

title: FSCS Annual Report and Class Statements 2024/25
summary: FSCS published its 2024/25 annual report and class statements, covering its performance, finances, recoveries, and governance for the year ended 31 March 2025. It also notes future work on deposit protection limit consultation outcomes and its next five-year plan, but it does not itself create new obligations for firms.

title: Thematic Review of Sustainability Reporting
summary: HM Treasury’s thematic review assesses sustainability reporting in UK central government and signals planned changes to the Sustainability Reporting Guidance, including decoupling it from Greening Government Commitments and retaining TCFD-aligned disclosures. It also says HMT will explore further changes and set out a proposal for the FRAB in November 2025.

title: Post Implementation Review of IFRS 16
summary: HMT published a post-implementation review of IFRS 16 in central government, summarising feedback from preparers, users and FRAB on the 2022-23 reporting implementation. It does not introduce new rules, but identifies lessons for future standards such as IFRS 17, IFRS 18 and IFRS 19. It is relevant mainly for public sector financial reporting and standard-setting oversight.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Foreign Terrorist Organizations Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 22A, 23A, 24A, 25A, 26A, and 28A
summary: OFAC published six updated general licenses under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Foreign Terrorist Organizations Sanctions Regulations, replacing earlier licenses effective 2025-03-05. The licenses authorize certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving Ansarallah, including humanitarian goods, telecommunications, mail, internet communications, and related services, subject to restrictions. Sanctions teams and operations should update screening, blocking, and payment handling accordingly.

title: Imposition of Special Measures Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving CIBanco S.A., Institution de Banca Multiple, Intercam Banco S.A., Institución de Banca Multiple, and Vector Casa de Bolsa, S.A. de C.V.; Extension of Effective Date
summary: FinCEN extended by 45 days, to 2025-09-04, the effective date of three special-measures orders prohibiting certain funds transmittals involving CIBanco, Intercam and Vector, Mexico-based institutions identified as primary money laundering concerns. The substantive prohibitions remain unchanged. Firms dealing with cross-border payments or correspondent flows involving these institutions should note the delayed start date.

title: Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales
summary: The IRS and Treasury removed from the CFR a final rule on gross proceeds reporting by brokers that facilitate digital asset sales. The rule was revoked under the Congressional Review Act and has no legal force or effect. The action is effective 2025-07-11 and restores the prior section 6045 text.

title: Updating the UK’s regulatory framework for central counterparties
summary: HM Treasury published a policy note on draft 2025 statutory instruments to replace parts of the UK EMIR CCP framework once the relevant provisions are revoked. It is for technical comment and explains future rules for CCP recognition, overseas CCPs and systemic-importance criteria. No immediate firm action date is stated, but the companion draft rulebook and legislation are being prepared for implementation.

title: Memorandum of Understanding: Overseas Recognition Regimes
summary: HM Treasury, the Bank of England, the PRA and the FCA set out how they will coordinate on Overseas Recognition Regimes, including designating overseas jurisdictions and recognising overseas-authorised firms operating in the UK. It describes the process for requesting and providing regulatory advice, scope setting and review arrangements. No fixed compliance deadline is stated, but firms in affected regimes should monitor future designations.

title: Overseas Recognition Regimes Guidance Document
summary: HM Treasury publishes guidance on Overseas Recognition Regimes, explaining how it assesses whether overseas jurisdictions should be designated and how designations are monitored. It describes the UK’s recognition framework and the roles of HM Treasury and regulators, but does not itself change rules or create new obligations. No action date is stated.

title: Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) Pilot Update
summary: HM Treasury publishes an update on the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot, setting out additional features the government wants to test after reviewing supplier and market feedback. It is an informational policy paper about the pilot’s next steps, with no binding requirements or deadline in this publication.

title: Wholesale Financial Markets Digital Strategy
summary: HM Treasury publishes a policy paper setting out the UK government’s strategy for digitalising wholesale financial markets, including use of distributed ledger technology and appointing a Digital Markets Champion. It is an agenda-setting document for government, regulators and industry rather than a rule or consultation, and it does not set binding requirements or deadlines.

title: Reclaim Fund Ltd Annual Report and Accounts 2024/25
summary: Reclaim Fund Ltd’s 2024/25 annual report and accounts describes the operation and performance of the UK Dormant Assets Scheme, including transfers, reclaims and distributions to good causes. It is an informational annual report presented to Parliament, with no new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Financial Services Regulators Complaints Commissioner Annual Report and Accounts 2024-25 and regulator responses
summary: This is the Complaints Commissioner’s annual report and accounts for 2024/25, covering complaint handling, themes and regulator responses. It does not create new rules or obligations, but highlights complaint trends in areas such as P2P lending and SIPPs and signals further engagement with the FCA.

title: Treasury Minutes – July 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on HMRC, government cyber resilience, DHSC accounts, and violence against women and girls. It sets out the government’s responses and intended follow-up actions, including a summer 2025 HMRC Transformation Roadmap, but it does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: National risk assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing 2025
summary: HM Treasury published the 2025 National Risk Assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing for the UK. It updates the government’s view of ML/TF threats, sector risks and system responses, including banks and other regulated sectors, and says the findings will inform future policy, regulatory and operational priorities. It is awareness-only and does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13M
summary: OFAC published Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions General License 13M, authorizing certain day-to-day administrative transactions by U.S. persons and U.S.-owned or controlled entities in Russia through 2025-07-09, while preserving key sanctions prohibitions. GL 13M replaced GL 13L effective 2025-04-07.

title: Publication of Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations Web General License 33
summary: OFAC published Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations General License 33, authorizing limited wind-down transactions involving International Bank of Yemen and related entities. The authorization ran until 2025-05-17, and any payment to a blocked person had to be made into a blocked account. This is relevant to sanctioned-transaction screening and payment operations.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 55D and 115B
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 55D and 115B under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. They authorize certain Russia-related transactions for Sakhalin-2 and civil nuclear energy through 2025-12-19, and replace prior licenses 55C and 115A. Sanctions teams, operations, and any businesses touching Russia-related payments or trade flows should update screening and transaction controls immediately.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13N
summary: OFAC published General License 13N under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain day-to-day administrative transactions by U.S. persons and entities they own or control in Russia through 2025-10-09. It replaces GL 13M and excludes transactions involving blocked persons or certain accounts of Russian state entities. Sanctions teams and operations should check activity against the revised authorization immediately.

title: Digitisation Taskforce - July 2025
summary: HMT’s Digitisation Taskforce final report sets out recommendations to modernise the UK shareholding framework by removing paper share certificates and improving intermediated share ownership. It calls for stakeholders and government/regulators to develop an implementation timetable and identify any legislative or regulatory changes needed. No direct legal obligation is created by the report itself.

title: Policy statement: The Appointed Representatives Regime
summary: The UK government sets out policy to change the Appointed Representatives regime. It intends to require authorised firms to obtain FCA permission before appointing ARs and to extend FOS coverage in limited cases where an AR dispute is not the authorised firm’s responsibility. The changes would need legislation and would affect authorised firms using ARs.

title: 31 CFR Part 528
summary: OFAC published General License 1 under the International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations. It authorized wind-down transactions involving specified ICC-related blocked persons only through 2025-07-08, with payments to be made into blocked interest-bearing US accounts. The license has already expired, but it confirms the sanctioned persons and scope of permitted activity.

title: Publication of International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 8
summary: OFAC published General License 8 under the International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving Francesca Paola Albanese and related entities through 2025-08-08. Firms dealing with blocked persons under the ICC sanctions regime must ensure any permitted payments go to blocked accounts and that no other prohibited transactions are undertaken.

title: Publication of Syrian Sanctions Regulations Web General License 25
summary: OFAC published General License 25 under multiple Syria- and other sanctions regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions with the Government of Syria, listed blocked persons, and entities they own 50% or more of, subject to exclusions. It also does not unblock previously blocked property or authorize transactions with non-listed SDNs or related to Iran, Russia, or DPRK. Effective from May 23, 2025.

title: Treasury Minutes – August 2025
summary: UK Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on government spending and performance across several departments, including digital procurement and local government finance. It records government agreements, implementation updates, and target dates for recommendations, including digital procurement role clarity and coordination by December 2025. It does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2023-24
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy note on the 2023-24 Welsh Rates of Income Tax reconciliation. It explains how HMRC outturn data updates Welsh Government funding and block grant adjustments, with a net £53 million increase for 2026-27. No obligations are created for firms.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2023-24
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy paper on the 2023-24 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC outturn data and revised population estimates update Scottish Government funding, with a net funding increase of £406 million for 2026-27. It is informational and creates no obligations for firms.

title: Imposition of Special Measures Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving CIBanco S.A., Institución de Banca Multiple, Intercam Banco S.A., Institución de Banca Multiple, and Vector Casa de Bolsa, S.A. de C.V.; Extension of Effective Date
summary: FinCEN extends to 2025-10-20 the effective date of its special measures orders prohibiting certain funds transmittals involving CIBanco, Intercam and Vector, three Mexico-based institutions previously found to be of primary money laundering concern. The underlying prohibitions remain unchanged; only the start date is pushed back.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on financial crisis management
summary: HMT published a policy paper setting out the Memorandum of Understanding between the Treasury, Bank of England and PRA on resolution planning and financial crisis management. It describes how the authorities will coordinate in a potential financial crisis; it does not itself create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Proposed amendments to the Money Laundering Regulations - draft SI and policy note
primary_functions: Regulatory change; Financial crime; Compliance; Ops; Product
summary: HM Treasury has published a draft statutory instrument and policy note amending the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 for technical consultation. It proposes changes to customer due diligence, cryptoasset-related scope, bank insolvency onboarding, and other AML/CTF measures. The consultation closes on 2025-09-30; the final instrument is expected in early 2026 and would take effect 21 days after being made, with some cryptoasset provisions tied to the FSMA perimeter commencement.

title: Get Britain Working White Paper
summary: The UK government published a White Paper setting out proposals to reform employment, health and skills support to reduce economic inactivity and promote good work. It is a policy paper and does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms. No compliance date is stated.

title: EM on EU excise duty applied to tobacco products COM(2025)581)
summary: HM Treasury’s explanatory memorandum covers EU proposals to recast tobacco excise duty rules and amend excise movement arrangements. It is an early-stage EU legislative proposal that could affect Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework, but it is not yet binding. HMRC says there was no UK consultation and the Commission proposes an in-force date of 1 January 2028 with a four-year transition for some rate increases.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5S
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 5S, replacing GL 5R. From 2025-12-20, it authorizes certain transactions, financing and other dealings in the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% bond, subject to the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations and other sanctions restrictions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 40D
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 40D, which authorizes certain LPG delivery and offloading transactions involving the Government of Venezuela, PdVSA and PdVSA-owned entities through 2025-09-05, if the cargo was loaded by 2025-07-07. It supersedes General License 40C. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related sanctioned parties must check whether transactions fall within the license.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published General License Q under the Iran sanctions program, authorizing limited vessel-related transactions for the blocked vessel M.V.
