Tinos I and related parties, including safety, repairs, sale, and certain services, subject to restrictions and use of blocked interest-bearing accounts for payments to blocked persons. It was issued May 20, 2025 and published September 10, 2025.

title: Geographic Targeting Order Imposing Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements on Certain Money Services Businesses Along the Southwest Border
summary: FinCEN issued a new Geographic Targeting Order for certain money services businesses along the southwest border. Covered MSBs in specified Arizona, Texas and California locations must report and retain records for currency transactions of $1,000 to $10,000 and verify customer identity, with compliance due by 2025-10-10 for firms not already covered by the earlier order.

title: Business rates: forward look
summary: HM Treasury has published a policy paper giving an overview of the expected timeline for business rates reforms and how stakeholders can engage. It says the government will consider wider reforms over this Parliament, alongside 2026 and 2029 revaluations, and recalls the planned two lower multipliers for retail, hospitality and leisure properties under £500,000 rateable value.

title: Transforming Business Rates: Interim Report
summary: HM Treasury’s interim report on business rates reviews stakeholder feedback and sets out areas for further exploration, including a move from ‘slab’ to ‘slice’ taxation, stronger Small Business Rates Relief, improvement relief changes, and possible valuation/admin reforms. It is not a final policy decision. Further updates are expected at Autumn Budget 2025; no immediate compliance date is set.

title: Treasury Minutes – September 2025
summary: Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports, including the Department for Education’s response on T Levels, immigration, teacher numbers, infrastructure finance, tax and water regulation. It is a government response and progress update, not a new rule or supervisory action. The document does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: Chancellor meeting with Gilt-edged Market Makers: Minutes - September 2025
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes of a 22 September 2025 Chancellor meeting with gilt market primary dealers (GEMMs) on views of global and UK economic prospects. It is an informational policy paper only and does not create obligations or set deadlines for firms.

title: UK-Australia Financial Regulatory Forum September 2025: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the Australian Treasury published a joint statement recording the inaugural UK-Australia Financial Regulatory Forum held on 24 September 2025. It summarises the discussions and outcomes from the meeting, but does not create or change any regulatory requirements.

title: Publication of an Iran-Related Determination.
summary: OFAC published an Iran-related sector determination under Executive Order 13902 applying sanctions to the financial sector of the Iranian economy. The determination took effect on 2020-10-08 and expands the scope of sanctioned Iranian sectors for U.S. persons and property interests subject to OFAC rules.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published General License R under the Iranian sanctions program, authorizing certain safety, environmental, repair, and cargo offloading transactions involving specified blocked vessels/persons through 2025-10-01 12:01 a.m. EDT. Firms dealing with the listed vessels or persons must ensure payments to blocked persons go to blocked interest-bearing U.S. accounts and that no other Iran-related prohibitions are breached.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 104A
summary: OFAC published General License 104A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain otherwise prohibited diamond import transactions into the United States through 2026-09-01, subject to the stated origin and size conditions. It replaces General License 104 effective 2025-08-27.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum- October 2025
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording discussions at the fourth EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 1 October 2025. It is an informational public record only and does not create or change requirements.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group Statement on AI and Cybersecurity
summary: The G7 Cyber Expert Group published a statement on AI and cybersecurity for the financial sector. It encourages jurisdictions to monitor AI developments, foster public-private-academic collaboration, and address emerging cybersecurity risks from GenAI, agentic AI and other advanced systems. No binding requirements or deadlines are set.

title: Block Grant Transparency: October 2025
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper and explanatory note explaining how block grants for the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive are calculated, covering changes from the 2015 Spending Review through Spending Review 2025. It is informational and does not create bank-specific obligations.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Regarding Huione Group, as a Foreign Financial Institution of Primary Money Laundering Concern
summary: FinCEN’s final rule designates Huione Group as a foreign financial institution of primary money laundering concern and prohibits covered U.S. financial institutions from opening or maintaining correspondent accounts for it or on its behalf. Covered institutions must also apply special due diligence to correspondent accounts to prevent Huione-related transactions. The rule is effective 2025-11-17.

title: Reclaim Fund Limited – Framework Document 2025
summary: HMT published the 2025 Framework Document for Reclaim Fund Ltd, setting out governance, accountability, reporting, risk, fraud, remuneration and FOIA arrangements for RFL. It is a point-in-time governance document for the dormant assets operator and does not itself create new regulatory obligations. It applies to RFL and its subsidiary/joint venture arrangements, with existing FCA and legal requirements prevailing. Published 2025-10-16.

title: World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund 2025 Annual Meetings, Development Committee: UK Governors' statement
summary: This is a UK government statement by the UK Governors to the World Bank Group/IMF Development Committee. It is a speech-style policy paper with no new rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: An introduction to the UK public investment landscape
summary: HMT published an explainer on the UK public investment landscape, describing the roles of institutions such as the British Business Bank, National Wealth Fund, UK Export Finance, Innovate UK, Homes England and devolved investment bodies. It highlights collaboration examples and contact points, but does not create new rules, obligations or deadlines.

title: Joint statement on regional investment from UK public investment bodies
summary: UK public investment body CEOs issued a joint policy statement on supporting regional growth and investment across the UK. It is a non-binding commitment to work with government and the private sector on Local Growth Plans and regional priorities; no compliance deadline or legal change is set out.

title: Statement of strategic priorities to the British Business Bank
summary: The UK government published a 5-year statement of strategic priorities for the British Business Bank, setting its mission from April 2026 to support smaller businesses and mobilise finance. It also raises the bank’s economic capital limit to £25.6 billion. This is a policy announcement for the public bank, not a rule for regulated firms.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 17 October 2025
summary: This is a government communique on the Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) meeting on 17 October 2025, discussing Scotland’s fiscal framework. It is informational only and does not set out any new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 17 October 2025
summary: A UK government communiqué reports a meeting of the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee on 17 October 2025. It is informational only and does not create or change any obligations for firms.

title: Fair Credit Reporting Act; Preemption of State Laws
summary: The CFPB issued an interpretive rule, effective October 28, 2025, clarifying that the Fair Credit Reporting Act generally preempts state laws covering the enumerated credit-reporting subjects. Firms involved in consumer reporting and related credit decisioning should align state-law compliance positions to the federal preemption analysis.

title: Meeting minutes – July 2025
summary: These are meeting minutes recording the Chancellor’s discussion with the Bank of England Governor on the latest Financial Stability Report. They do not themselves change any rules or deadlines, but note the statutory post-report meeting requirement under the Bank of England Act 1998 as amended.

title: Social Impact Investment Advisory Group
summary: HMT publishes a policy paper from the Social Impact Investment Advisory Group setting out a roadmap for government to mobilise impact capital and the wider impact economy. It discusses leadership, an Office for the Impact Economy, flagship projects and possible reforms to pension, philanthropy and corporate giving. It is an advisory/strategic publication only, with no binding requirements or dates.

title: Financial Inclusion Strategy
summary: UK HM Treasury’s Financial Inclusion Strategy sets out government policy and planned initiatives to improve access to banking, affordable credit, savings and financial education across the UK. It signals industry collaboration and possible future regulatory or policy follow-up, but it does not itself create binding requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Updating the UK’s exemption framework for intragroup Over the Counter Derivatives
summary: Draft UK Regulations would amend EMIR intragroup exemption rules for OTC derivatives, including transactions between UK counterparties and third-country group entities. UK firms would need FCA notification and, in some cases, non-objection before using the exemption. The regulations come into force when the related FSMA 2023 revocation takes effect.

title: Strategy for future retail payments infrastructure
summary: HM Treasury publishes a strategy for future UK retail payments infrastructure, setting high-level outcomes for the next generation of infrastructure and the governance model to take it forward. It is an outlook paper rather than a binding rule, with no direct compliance date. Firms in payments, including banks and payment service providers, should monitor the planned redesign and any later implementation measures.

title: Accelerated Settlement (T+1)
summary: Draft UK regulations would shorten settlement for transferable securities executed on a UK trading venue from T+2 to T+1, with exemptions for certain privately negotiated, bilateral-reported, initial-book-entry and securities financing transactions. The rules are laid before Parliament and, if approved, come into force on 2027-10-11.

title: 10 Year Efficiency Projections
summary: HMT and the Office for Value for Money publish a 10-year efficiency projection methodology and illustrative projections for selected government programmes funded at Spending Review 2025. It is a prototype and invitation for external insight, not a binding rule or requirement, and does not set compliance deadlines for firms.

title: Reforming the spending control and accountability framework
summary: HMT’s policy paper sets out planned reforms to the UK government’s spending control and accountability framework, including more delegation, streamlined approvals, and updated rules and guidance. It is an announcement of intended policy direction, with phased implementation to follow, rather than a binding rule for firms.

title: Entrepreneurship in the UK
summary: HMT publishes a policy paper on entrepreneurship in the UK, setting out the government’s economic agenda for start-ups and scale-ups, including R&D, procurement, tax and public finance institutions. It discusses intended future policy direction and a call for evidence on tax support, but it is not itself a rule, consultation, or binding requirement.

title: Government Response to the 2025 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury publishes its government response to the OBR’s 2025 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report. It explains the UK’s fiscal strategy, including debt reduction, new fiscal rules, balance-sheet management reforms and measures on pensions and climate-related long-term sustainability. It is an explanatory policy paper and does not itself impose new requirements on firms.

title: Evaluation of the Office for Value for Money
summary: HM Treasury published an evaluation of the Office for Value for Money, a time-limited internal government unit. It reviews whether the unit delivered its remit and lasting impact, and assesses spending review efficiency plans and related government processes. This is informational only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Digital Services Tax Review
summary: HM Treasury’s Digital Services Tax Review is a report to Parliament assessing the UK’s interim Digital Services Tax and its administration. It discusses international tax reform, the OECD two-pillar work, and the UK’s policy position, but does not itself change tax rules or impose new deadlines.

title: Effects of the business rates retail, hospitality and leisure multipliers and high-value multiplier
summary: HMT published an analysis of the effects of planned business rates multipliers for retail, hospitality and leisure properties and a higher multiplier for high-value properties in England. It explains the 2026-27 rates, the scope of properties affected, and the policy rationale. It does not itself introduce the rules; it reports on measures already set out in legislation and referenced for 2026-27.

title: Independent Review of the Loan Charge
summary: HMT publishes an independent review of the Loan Charge and associated settlement approach, with recommendations for a new final settlement opportunity for affected taxpayers. It is an awareness-only review and does not itself change the law or create new requirements. The report focuses on bringing the long-running dispute to a close for people still to settle and their families.

title: Supporting documents for Budget 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s Budget 2025 supporting document sets out distributional analysis of tax, welfare and public service spending decisions and lists Budget measures affecting households. It is informational and accompanies the Budget, rather than creating obligations itself. The document highlights timing for several tax and welfare measures, but the publication itself imposes no direct requirements.

title: Budget 2025 document
summary: UK HM Treasury’s Budget 2025 document was published as a policy paper. It is a government fiscal statement, not a regulatory rule, consultation, or supervisory notice, and it does not itself impose compliance deadlines or obligations on firms.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements of Collective Cyber Incident Response and Recovery in the Financial Sector
summary: G7 non-binding principles for collective cyber incident response and recovery in the financial sector. It sets out high-level guidance on governance, use and maintenance of a CCIRR arrangement for financial authorities, financial entities and relevant third-party providers, but creates no regulatory obligations or deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2025
summary: This is a Treasury progress report to Parliament on how the government is implementing outstanding Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across multiple prior sessions. It does not create new rules or obligations for firms. No action date applies.

title: Creating a Provisional Licences Authorisation Regime: Policy Update 2025
summary: HM Treasury sets out a proposed UK provisional licence regime for unauthorised firms seeking FCA permission for existing regulated activities. The FCA would set modified, proportionate authorisation expectations for a time-limited period before full authorisation. This is policy-only for now; primary legislation and FCA detailed rules will follow when parliamentary time allows.

title: Joint Statement for the automatic exchange of information on immovable property
summary: The UK and 24 other jurisdictions say they aim to implement the OECD’s new automatic exchange framework for information on immovable property by 2029 or 2030. It is a policy paper and joint statement, not a binding rule, and it mainly signals future tax transparency cooperation between tax authorities.

title: UK Government Green Financing Framework 2025
summary: HM Treasury has updated the UK Government Green Financing Framework for green gilts and Green Savings Bonds. The 2025 framework adds nuclear energy as an eligible green expenditure, sets out the eligibility and exclusion criteria, and confirms annual allocation reporting plus new annual impact reporting where relevant and feasible. It came into force on 2025-11-27.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda 15 December 2025
summary: HMT published a provisional agenda for the EU-UK Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes meeting on 15 December 2025. It is a joint forum agenda only and does not itself change requirements or set deadlines for firms.

title: Publication of International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 10
summary: OFAC published General License 10 under the International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving specified blocked persons through 2025-10-04. Firms dealing with these persons had to ensure any permitted payments went into a blocked interest-bearing U.S. account. The license has now expired, but the publication confirms the scope and timing of the temporary authorization.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations and Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 125
summary: OFAC published General License 125 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations and Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain transactions incident to meetings between the US and Russian governments in Alaska through 2025-08-20, subject to exceptions for blocked property and other prohibited transactions.

title: Publication of International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 9
summary: OFAC published General License 9 under the International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving specified blocked persons through 2025-09-19. Firms dealing with the named persons or entities they control needed to rely on the licence terms and blocked-account payment restrictions; the licence had already expired when this was published in the Federal Register.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: 2026-27 Pay Round
summary: HM Treasury published an economic evidence paper for the 2026-27 pay round, setting out labour market and fiscal context for the independent Pay Review Bodies. It is background material only and does not itself set pay rates or create compliance obligations.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s December 2025 Treasury Minutes is a government response to Committee of Public Accounts reports across several departments. It is mainly an accountability and progress update, not a rule, supervisory notice or enforcement action. One section notes planned legislative measures in a future Armed Forces Bill, but this publication itself does not create binding requirements.

title: Fees for Reviews of the Rule Enforcement Programs of Designated Contract Markets and Registered Futures Associations
summary: The CFTC sets annual fees for designated contract markets and registered futures associations to recover the cost of reviewing their rule enforcement programs. Affected entities must electronically remit the applicable fee by 2026-02-13. The notice includes the 2023 assessed fees and the calculation method used.

title: Regulatory regime for cryptoassets (regulated activities) – Draft SI and Policy Note
primary_functions: Regulatory change; Legal; Compliance; Product; Ops
summary: Draft UK statutory instrument and policy note would create and amend regulated cryptoasset activities, including issuing qualifying stablecoins, operating trading platforms, dealing as principal, and staking. It would also change related FCA/PRA permissions, guidance and rules, and amend the Money Laundering Regulations. It is laid before Parliament and, once commenced, will bind UK firms in scope.

title: Withdrawal of Interpretive Guidance: Retail Commodity Transactions Involving Certain Digital Assets
summary: The CFTC withdraws its 2020 interpretive guidance on when “actual delivery” occurs for retail commodity transactions involving certain digital assets. The withdrawal is effective December 10, 2025 and signals that the CFTC will reevaluate the issue in light of market developments and the President’s Working Group recommendations.

title: NS&I Contingent Liabilities Arising from Transitioning to a Multi Supplier Model
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper/Departmental Minute explaining NS&I’s contingent operational and fraud loss liabilities as it moves to a multi-supplier delivery model. It notes a combined potential exposure of £2m to 2029 and apologises for procedural non-compliance with Parliamentary requirements. No new regulatory obligations are created for firms.

title: Mortgage Charter
summary: HMT published a Mortgage Charter setting out voluntary commitments by major UK mortgage lenders, with FCA and PRA support, to help regulated residential mortgage borrowers facing higher rates. It signals expected lender actions and FCA rulebook changes, but this document itself is a policy announcement and does not itself create binding requirements.

title: Privacy Act Exemption; Correction
summary: NCUA issued an interim final rule, effective 2026-01-12, correcting a Privacy Act system-of-records reference and exempting one additional NCUA system of records from certain Privacy Act requirements. Comments are due by 2026-02-11. The rule affects NCUA Privacy Act procedures and internal handling of records, not private credit unions directly.

title: List of Rules To Be Reviewed Pursuant to the Regulatory Flexibility Act
summary: The SEC published its annual Section 610 RFA review list and invited comments by 2026-02-11 on listed 2016 rules, asking whether they should be continued, amended, or rescinded. It does not itself change rules, but flags SEC registration/reporting provisions under the Exchange Act for review.

title: Advancing a Coordinated Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography in the Financial Sector
summary: The G7 Cyber Expert Group issued a non-binding roadmap encouraging financial authorities, financial entities and third-party providers to plan a coordinated transition to post-quantum cryptography. It offers high-level considerations and indicative timelines, but expressly does not set regulatory expectations or guidance. No compliance date or mandatory requirement is created.

title: Geographic Targeting Order Imposing Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements on Certain Financial Institutions in Minnesota
summary: FinCEN issued a Geographic Targeting Order requiring banks and money transmitters in Hennepin and Ramsey Counties, Minnesota to retain and report certain funds transfers of $3,000 or more. It applies from 2026-02-12 and uses the FinCEN FI Portal and specified CSV submission template. Covered institutions should prepare reporting and recordkeeping processes for the affected geographic area.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2026
summary: Treasury Minutes 2026 is the UK government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports across several departments, including local bus services, defence, animal disease resilience, overseas estate costs, Afghanistan response, NHS waiting times and BBC accounts. It records whether the government agrees with recommendations and sets target implementation dates for follow-up actions, but it does not itself create new binding obligations for firms.

title: Delegation of Authority To Grant or Deny Exemptions From Rule 612 of Regulation NMS Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934
summary: The SEC made a technical amendment to its rulebook delegation provision, updating the cross-reference for staff authority to grant or deny exemptions from Regulation NMS Rule 612. The change is effective January 16, 2026 and reflects a prior renumbering only; it does not create a new substantive exemption standard.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 132
summary: OFAC published Web General License 132 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving the Paks II civil nuclear power plant project in Hungary and listed Russian financial institutions and the Central Bank of the Russian Federation. Firms must still observe the stated carve-outs, including correspondent/payable-through restrictions and blocked-person prohibitions. Issued on 2025-11-21 and published in the Federal Register on 2026-01-20.

title: Publication of Transnational Criminal Organizations Sanctions Regulations Web General License 1
summary: OFAC published General License 1 under the Transnational Criminal Organizations Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving certain blocked Prince Group entities until 2025-11-13, subject to payment into a blocked account and other TCOSR restrictions. Sanctions teams and operations should check whether any current dealings involve the listed parties or 50%-owned entities.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 129
summary: OFAC published General License 129 under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. It authorizes certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving Rosneft Deutschland GmbH and RN Refining & Marketing GmbH, and entities they own 50% or more of, through 2026-04-29. Firms dealing with these entities should check scope and any excluded blocked persons.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 13O
summary: OFAC published Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations General License 13O, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited administrative transactions for U.S. persons and U.S.-owned/controlled entities in Russia, through 2026-01-09. It replaces General License 13N and excludes dealings with blocked persons or debits to certain Russian central bank and ministry accounts.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update 2025
summary: HM Treasury published a progress update on its own Women in Finance Charter commitments, noting it increased female senior management representation to 50% by March 2025 and describing future priorities. It is an informational update only and does not impose new requirements on firms.

title: Joint readout of the first UK-China Financial Working Group
summary: HMT and Chinese authorities issued a joint readout of the inaugural UK-China Financial Working Group. It records discussions on financial stability, CCP supervision, crisis management, FATF cooperation, capital markets, RMB clearing, wealth management, pensions and green finance. It does not create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Budget Information Security Review
summary: HM Treasury published a review of Budget information security following leaks and early access to OBR fiscal publications. It recommends tighter internal controls, a new ‘BUDGET - MARKET-SENSITIVE’ classification, and changes to publishing arrangements before the March 2026 EFO and the 2026 Budget. This is an informational review and does not itself impose rules on firms.

title: Applying the FSMA 2000 model of regulation to the Capital Requirements Regulation
summary: Draft UK statutory regulations would create the Overseas Prudential Requirements Regime for credit institutions and investment firms, including rules for designating overseas jurisdictions and the prudential treatment of certain exposures and capital instruments. If approved, they come into force on 1 January 2027. Banks, investment firms and CRR groups should assess any impacted overseas jurisdiction relationships and capital treatment.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2026
summary: HM Treasury published a policy note and multiplier tables for the 2026 public service pensions increase. Pensions in payment for a year will rise by 3.8% from 6 April 2026, with proportionate increases for shorter payment periods. The tables are for scheme administrators to apply the annual CPI-linked uplift correctly.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General License 5T
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations General License 5T, authorizing certain transactions and financing related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% bond on or after 2026-02-03. It replaces General License 5S effective 2025-12-19. Banks and other U.S.-sanctions exposed firms should check whether any blocked activity is newly permitted and update screening, controls and permissions accordingly.

title: Publication of a Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published General License 13 under the Belarus Sanctions Regulations, authorising certain transactions involving JSC Belarusian Potash Company, Agrorozkvit LLC, Belaruskali OAO and majority-owned entities. It does not authorise unblocking blocked property or other prohibited transactions. The license was issued on 2025-12-15 and published in the Federal Register on 2026-03-02.

title: Publication of a Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published Belarus Sanctions Regulations General License 12, authorizing certain transactions involving three specified blocked aircraft and related use by designated persons. It also unblocks those aircraft, while preserving restrictions on pre-existing blocked funds and other prohibited transactions. Effective as of November 4, 2025.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 124B, 128A, 130, and 131
summary: OFAC published four Russia-related general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 124B authorizes certain petroleum-services and related transactions for specified Caspian pipeline/CPC projects; GL 128A authorizes limited transactions for Lukoil retail stations outside Russia until 2025-12-13; GLs 130 and 131 cover specified Lukoil-related transactions, with some licenses already expired or time-limited.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 124A, 126, 127, and 128
summary: OFAC published four web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations. GL 124A authorizes certain petroleum-services and related transactions for CPC and Tengizchevroil projects; GLs 126 and 127 authorize limited wind-down and divestment activity involving Rosneft and Lukoil through 2025-11-21; GL 128 is also published. Sanctions teams should update screening and transaction handling immediately.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 128B
summary: OFAC published General License 128B under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions involving Lukoil retail service stations outside Russia through 2026-04-29. It replaces GL 128A and excludes several prohibited transactions, including transfers to Russia and dealings with other blocked persons.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations and Web General License 131A
summary: OFAC published General License 131A under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain transactions for negotiating and entering contingent sale contracts for Lukoil-related entities, and limited maintenance/wind-down activity, through 2026-01-17. It also allows use of blocked accounts for authorized maintenance transactions and replaces GL 131. The general license is now expired.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General License 131B
summary: OFAC published Russian sanctions General License 131B, which authorizes certain transactions related to the sale and wind-down of Lukoil International GmbH and related entities. It replaces GL 131A and is effective from 2026-01-14 through 2026-02-28. Firms dealing with sanctioned persons or blocked property must follow the license limits and exclusions.

title: Debt Management Report 2026-27
summary: HM Treasury’s annual Debt Management Report sets out the UK government’s borrowing plans for 2026-27, including the financing remit for the DMO, NS&I and Exchequer cash management. It describes the debt management framework, target issuance mix and market principles, but does not create obligations for banks or other firms.

title: Fair Housing Home Loan Data System
summary: The OCC is rescinding its Fair Housing Home Loan Data System rule in 12 CFR part 27. For national banks and their subsidiaries, the final rule removes the specific OCC data-collection and recordkeeping regime, effective 2026-04-03. The OCC says other legal authorities already require relevant home-loan data collection and retention.

title: Treasury Minutes – March 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on fees and charges, DWP follow-up, MoJ follow-up, and children’s care homes. It sets out the government’s responses and planned actions, including a cross-department working group and future operational guidance, but does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: Geographic Targeting Order Imposing Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements on Certain Money Services Businesses Along the Southwest Border
summary: FinCEN issued a Geographic Targeting Order requiring certain money services businesses in specified southwest border counties and ZIP codes to retain records and report currency transactions of $1,000 to $10,000, and to verify customer identity. It takes effect 2026-03-07, with a 2026-04-06 compliance date for businesses not covered by the prior 2025 order.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, March 2026
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording topics discussed at the fifth EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 11 March 2026. It is a public record only and does not itself create or change any requirements.

title: Fifth Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin Meeting Minutes
summary: UK government minutes record the fifth UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee meeting on customs cooperation and rules of origin under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is an informational record of discussions held on 16 October 2025 and does not itself create new requirements or deadlines.

title: UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum Joint Statement, March 2026
summary: HM Treasury and the Japan Financial Services Agency published a joint statement recording the fourth UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum meeting. It is informational only and does not itself create new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Northern Growth Strategy: Case for change
summary: HMT published a policy paper on the Northern Growth Strategy setting out the government’s next steps to support growth in the North, including connectivity, business investment, skills and future devolution. It is a strategic, non-binding document for awareness only and does not create compliance deadlines or legal obligations.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant 2026-27
summary: This report sets the Royal Trustees’ determination of the Sovereign Grant for 2026-27 under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 and explains how it was calculated. It is a statutory report laid before Parliament, not a consultation or guidance document. It affects the Treasury and Royal Household rather than regulated financial firms.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 19 March 2026
summary: This is a communiqué from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee about a meeting held on 19 March 2026. It is informational only and does not set new rules, obligations, deadlines or supervisory expectations for firms.

title: Cabinet Office and HM Treasury small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) action plan: 2025 to 2028
summary: Cabinet Office and HM Treasury published a policy paper setting out a 2025 to 2028 SME action plan for public sector procurement. It describes targets and actions to increase SME participation and spend with government, mainly affecting businesses seeking public contracts rather than creating regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Chancellor meeting with Gilt-edged Market Makers: Minutes - March 2026
summary: Summary minutes of the Chancellor’s meeting with gilt market primary dealers and economists. It discusses views on global and UK economic prospects and does not create any new obligations or regulatory changes.

title: Establishment of the Nashoba Valley Viticultural Area
summary: TTB finalizes a new codified wine appellation rule establishing the Nashoba Valley American viticultural area in Worcester County, Massachusetts. The rule takes effect on 2026-04-23 and affects wine labeling and geographic origin claims for vintners using the new AVA name.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) - 19 March 2026
summary: This is a policy paper communique on the Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland), describing a meeting between HM Treasury and the Scottish Government about Scotland’s fiscal framework. It is informational only and creates no requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Mortgage Charter 2026
summary: The UK government published a policy paper on the Mortgage Charter 2026. It restates lenders’ voluntary commitments to give borrowers short-term flexibility if mortgage payments are under pressure, following discussions with lenders on 26 March 2026. No new legal obligations or deadlines are set out in the text.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: November 2025
summary: HMT published minutes/agenda for the Government Financial Reporting User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting. It is an informational record of discussion topics such as accountability in small government bodies, ICAEW/CIPFA updates, future financial reporting, and Whole of Government Accounts, with no rule changes or deadlines stated.

title: Treasury Minutes – April 2026
summary: Treasury Minutes responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on several public-sector topics, including energy-efficiency retrofit failures and NS&I transformation. It sets out the government’s position and planned actions, including continued supervision of NS&I and further updates in Autumn 2026, but it does not itself create bank-facing rules or obligations.

title: U.S. – UK Financial Regulatory Working Group Winter 2026: Joint Statement
summary: This joint statement records the discussion and outcomes of the 12th U.S.–UK Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It does not create rules, obligations, or deadlines for firms.

title: Decision No 1/2026 of the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, amending Protocol I of the Trade and Cooperation Agreement
summary: This decision amends Protocol I to the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement to confirm the UK’s participation in Erasmus+ from 1 January 2027, with related eligibility and implementation conditions. It also sets out that UK award procedures for 2021-2026 budget commitments remain outside the protocol. Relevant teams should review cross-border programme participation and any designated national authority, agency and audit body arrangements.

title: OFSI Strategy: 2026 - 2029
summary: OFSI sets out its 2026-2029 strategy for UK financial sanctions implementation, focusing on clearer expectations, faster guidance and licensing, stronger enforcement, and more digital and data-driven tools. It is an intelligence/strategy publication rather than a rule or notice, so it does not itself create new obligations.

title: EM on EU Decision on TCA Specialised Committee Erasmus+ position
summary: HM Treasury explains the UK/EU Council Decision on the UK’s association to Erasmus+ under the TCA. It describes the legal and financial terms, including UK participation from 1 January 2027, governance arrangements, and the UK’s contribution for 2027. This is an informational memorandum rather than a rule, consultation or supervisory notice.

title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting Certain Transmittals of Funds Involving CIBanco S.A., Institución de Banca Multiple; Amendment
summary: FinCEN amends its special-measure order restricting certain transmittals of funds involving CIBanco, a Mexico-based bank designated as a primary money laundering concern. The amendment allows limited transfers needed for the Government of Mexico to liquidate CIBanco, effective 2026-04-16. Covered financial institutions handling cross-border payments involving the bank should update sanctions/AML controls immediately.

title: Adoption of Updated EDGAR Filer Manual
summary: The SEC updated the EDGAR Filer Manual and related rules, effective 2026-04-16, to reflect EDGAR Release 26.1 and incorporate technical filing changes. Filers must use the revised manual for electronic submissions, including new handling for filing-fee information, lower ACH fee transaction limits, and updated Schedule 13D/13G CUSIP capacity. EDGAR access-code references were removed and Form ID guidance was clarified.

title: World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund 2026 Spring Meetings, Development Committee: UK Governors' statement
summary: UK Governors’ statement delivered at the IMF/World Bank Development Committee meeting. It is a policy statement and commentary, not a rule or supervisory requirement, and creates no direct obligations. It is relevant for awareness only to governance, regulatory change and prudential teams.

title: Policy note: Draft statutory instrument amending the Cryptoasset Regulations
summary: HM Treasury has published a draft statutory instrument and policy note to amend the UK cryptoasset regulations, mainly to carve UK-issued qualifying stablecoin payment activity out of the cryptoasset dealing/arranging perimeter ahead of wider payments reforms. The note also says lending and borrowing involving UK qualifying stablecoin will stay in scope for now, and HMT will consult further soon. No immediate compliance date is stated in the note.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Performance Reviews
summary: HM Treasury has published records of six-monthly performance review meetings between the Economic Secretary to the Treasury and the FCA Chief Executive. The paper is informational only and does not create any new requirements, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: HM Treasury and Prudential Regulation Authority Performance Reviews
summary: HM Treasury published minutes of six-monthly performance review meetings between the Economic Secretary to the Treasury and the PRA Chief Executive. The document records discussion of the PRA’s performance and the government’s move to formalise sponsor-department reviews, but it does not create new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Changes to the Risk Transformation Regulations
summary: The UK government has published a consultation response on changes to the Risk Transformation Regulations. It plans to take reforms forward through primary and secondary legislation, including changes to funding expectations for transformer vehicles and powers to let protected cell companies carry out insurance contracts. Further secondary legislation and regulator rule changes are expected, but no commencement date is given.

title: Publication of Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses
summary: OFAC published web general licenses S and T under the Iranian sanctions program, authorizing limited transactions involving specified blocked vessels/persons for short periods. The licenses are already expired and include detailed conditions and exclusions. Relevant for sanctions screening, payments, trade/shipping and operational handling of affected transactions.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 46, 46A, and 46B
primary_functions: Financial crime; Compliance; Ops; Regulatory change
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 46, 46A and 46B under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. They authorize certain U.S.-entity transactions involving Venezuelan-origin oil, subject to conditions, exclusions, and detailed reporting every 90 days for covered exports or sales to non-U.S. destinations. The licenses were issued on January 29, February 10 and March 13, 2026.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 47, 48, 49, and 50
summary: OFAC published Venezuela Sanctions Regulations general licenses 47 to 50, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited Venezuela-related transactions, including U.S.-origin diluents and certain oil and gas goods, technology, software and services. GL 47 includes reporting and contractual conditions, with reports due 10 days after the first transaction and every 90 days while ongoing. Some licenses were superseded.

title: Publication of Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 55E, 115C, 13P, and 131C
summary: OFAC published four web general licenses under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain Russia-related transactions for Sakhalin-2 and civil nuclear energy, plus two other time-limited authorizations. The licenses are already in effect or have specific expiry dates, including 2026-06-18 for GLs 55E and 115C, 2026-04-09 for GL 13P, and 2026-04-01 for GL 131C.

title: Publication of a Democratic Republic of the Congo Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published General License 1 under the Democratic Republic of the Congo Sanctions Regulations, authorizing wind-down transactions involving the Rwanda Defence Force and certain owned entities, subject to blocked-account rules. The license is dated March 2, 2026 and runs through 2026-04-01 at 12:01 a.m. EDT. Firms dealing with DR Congo sanctions exposure should confirm any residual transactions are separately authorized.

title: Publication of a Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Illicit Drug Trade Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published General License 34 under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations and Illicit Drug Trade Sanctions Regulations. The license authorizes wind-down transactions involving Kovay Gardens, and related entities, through 2026-03-21, subject to blocked-account requirements and other sanctions restrictions.

title: Publication of a Belarus Sanctions Regulations Web General License
summary: OFAC published General License 14 under the Belarus Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving specified Belarusian entities and entities they own 50% or more. It does not authorize unblocking of blocked property or other prohibited transactions. The license was issued on 2026-03-26 and is being published now.

title: Reforms to Money Market Fund Regulations
summary: HM Treasury and the FCA announced plans to replace and reform the UK Money Market Fund regime. The government will bring forward legislation when parliamentary time allows, with most detailed requirements to sit in FCA rules and guidance; UK MMFs should expect higher liquidity expectations. The new regime is expected by Q4 2026, subject to Parliamentary approval.

title: Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor Investment Prospectus
summary: HM Treasury’s Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor Investment Prospectus is a promotional policy paper encouraging investors, developers and businesses to locate or invest in the corridor. It highlights government support, infrastructure and tax incentives, but it does not itself create new regulatory obligations or deadlines.

title: Safeguarding Stability, Enabling Growth: The Ring-Fencing Review
summary: HMT published the Ring-Fencing Review, setting out proposed reforms to UK bank ring-fencing, including new flexibilities, a proposed New Growth Allowance, and possible movement of some requirements from legislation into PRA rules. The paper also signals future consultations and reviews, with some steps expected in summer 2026 and via the upcoming Financial Services and Markets Bill.

title: Public service pensions: 2024 valuations
summary: The Treasury made amending directions for the 2024 public service pensions valuations and employer cost cap process. They take effect the day after signing and revise valuation assumptions, cost-cap calculations and related earning-growth rates for public service pension schemes, including special schemes for the security services. Relevant scheme operators and public-sector employers must apply the updated rules immediately on commencement.

title: Getting Britain Building: Reforming Judicial Review for Infrastructure
summary: The UK government proposes two optional reforms to judicial review for nationally significant infrastructure projects: a parliamentary authorisation route for critical energy projects and a structured challenge window for all NSIPs. The proposals are subject to further detail and underpinning legislation, with no specific compliance date stated. They aim to reduce delay and make consents harder to challenge.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Committee of Public Accounts reports on public spending, reporting and oversight, including excess votes and departmental controls. It is a parliamentary accountability publication, not a regulatory rule or supervisory notice, and it creates no direct obligations for regulated firms.

title: Whole of Government Accounts, 2023-24
summary: This is HM Treasury’s annual Whole of Government Accounts report for 2023-24. It provides retrospective analysis of the UK public sector balance sheet, missing local authority audit data, and future plans for WGA and local audit reform. It does not create new requirements for firms.

title: National Wealth Fund Framework Document
summary: HMT has issued a new framework document for the National Wealth Fund, setting out its governance, reporting, risk, financial control and accountability arrangements. It updates how the company, HMT and the shareholder representative will operate, including board responsibilities, financial reporting and controls, audit, conflicts, and financial crime expectations. It is a point-in-time governance document, not a new rule with a separate compliance date.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 4 June 2026
summary: The UK and European Commission issued a joint statement on progress in work streams around EU invoices sent to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is an informational update only and does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – June 2026
summary: A Treasury Minutes progress report updating Parliament on the Government’s progress against outstanding Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across multiple prior reports and sessions. It is an informational status update only and does not create new obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Introducing the AI Economics Institute
summary: HM Treasury and DSIT announce a joint AI Economics Institute to study AI’s economic impacts on productivity, labour markets, firms and income distribution, and to support evidence-based UK policy making. It is a policy paper and does not itself create obligations or deadlines.

title: AI Economics Institute Prospectus
summary: HM Treasury has published a policy paper setting out the initial prospectus for the AI Economics Institute. It describes the Institute’s research agenda on AI’s economic effects, including evidence building, modelling and scenario analysis, but it does not create any rules or obligations for firms.

title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 5U and 5V
summary: OFAC published web general licenses 5U and 5V under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations. They authorize certain transactions and financing related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5% bond from the stated effective dates, and 5V supersedes 5U. Firms dealing with Venezuela-related transactions should check sanctions screening and transaction permissions against the current license terms.

title: Publication of Iran-Related Web General Licenses U and V
summary: OFAC published two Iran-related general licenses, GL U and GL V, that temporarily authorize specified transactions otherwise prohibited by US sanctions. GL U covered certain crude oil and petroleum product transactions through 2026-04-19; GL V covered wind-down transactions involving Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co., Ltd. These licenses were previously available on OFAC’s website and are now published in the Federal Register record.

title: Publication of International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 11
summary: OFAC published General License 11 under the International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving named blocked persons through 2026-01-17. Firms dealing with sanctioned persons or entities they own must ensure any permitted payments go into a blocked U.S. interest-bearing account. This is a sanctions change for affected transactions, but the license itself had already expired when published in the Federal Register.

title: Publication of Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations Web General License 2
summary: OFAC published General License 2 under the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations, authorizing certain otherwise prohibited transactions involving Anco Water Supply Co. Ltd. for the treatment and distribution of drinking water. It was issued on 2026-04-23 and published in the Federal Register on 2026-06-10. Firms dealing with the named party should check whether their sanctions controls and transaction handling can rely on the licence.

title: HM Treasury Market Engagement Group
summary: HM Treasury sets out the terms of reference for a new Market Engagement Group, including membership, meeting cadence, publication of minutes, confidentiality and competition-law expectations, plus a privacy notice for applicants. It is an engagement forum rather than a rule, and does not itself create regulatory obligations for firms. Market participants invited to join should note confidentiality, competition and data-handling considerations.

title: HM Treasury Market Engagement Group summary minutes – June 2026
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes from the June 2026 Market Engagement Group meeting. The note describes a senior-level forum where market participants discuss UK financial market developments with the Chancellor; it does not create rules, requirements, or deadlines.

title: Report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant Review 2026
summary: This is HMT’s report of the Royal Trustees’ review of the Sovereign Grant under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011. It explains past spending, expected future costs, and the Trustees’ conclusion on the grant formula, including the government’s planned legislation to allow a lower grant amount from 2027-28. It is informational and does not itself change rules for firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 15 December 2025
summary: Minutes of the fifth meeting of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes, held on 15 December 2025. It is an informational policy paper only and does not set new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: UK–Australia Investment Partnership Memorandum of Understanding
summary: The UK and Australia signed a voluntary memorandum of understanding to promote cooperation on cross-border investment, especially for superannuation and pension funds. It encourages policy discussions, sharing expertise and reducing barriers, but does not impose binding requirements or deadlines.

title: The Defence Investment Plan
summary: HMT published a Defence Investment Plan setting out multi-year UK defence spending priorities, including funding for nuclear deterrent renewal, drones, AI-enabled targeting, cyber, space, air and missile defence, and protection of critical underwater infrastructure. It is an সরকারের policy document, not a rule or consultation, and does not create compliance deadlines for firms.

title: Green Book discount rate review 2026
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper on the 2026 Green Book discount rate review, including findings, recommendations and technical annexes. It is informational only and does not itself change rules or impose deadlines on firms.

title: Green Book Review 2025: One year on
summary: HM Treasury reviews progress one year after the Green Book review, describing planned improvements to UK public-sector appraisal guidance, business case transparency, and place-based investment decisions. It is an informational policy paper with no direct new obligations for firms and no stated compliance deadline.

title: FSCS Annual Report and Accounts and Class Statements 2025/26
summary: FSCS published its 2025/26 Annual Report and Accounts, describing its activities, financial results, governance and future strategy. It notes operational developments such as the higher deposit protection limit and preparation for FCA targeted support, but it does not itself create new rules or obligations. This is mainly for awareness.

title: National Payments Vision
summary: HM Treasury’s National Payments Vision sets out the UK government’s strategic direction for payments, including stronger regulatory coordination, infrastructure upgrades, Open Banking progress and measures to support innovation, competition and security. It is a policy paper and does not itself create binding requirements, though it signals future work by regulators and industry.

title: A new approach to ensure regulators and regulation support growth
summary: HM Treasury’s policy paper reports progress on the UK Regulation Action Plan and announces future legislative intentions to cut regulatory burdens, strengthen the Growth Duty, and create broader sandbox powers to support innovation. It signals upcoming bills affecting competition, financial services, water, nuclear, energy and aviation, but it is not itself a binding rule. No immediate action date is set.

title: HM Treasury British Sign Language (BSL) 5-year plan: 1-year update, July 2026
summary: HM Treasury published a one-year progress update on its British Sign Language 5-year plan. It reports, for England, Scotland and Wales, how the department is promoting or facilitating BSL in communications with the public under the BSL Act 2022. This is an annual update only and does not set new requirements.

title: Recommendations of the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future
summary: HMT published a policy paper with initial recommendations from the UK-US Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future on digital assets, tokenisation and capital markets cooperation. It also includes a joint UK-US statement on stablecoins. This is an agenda-setting publication only; it does not itself impose obligations or set compliance deadlines.

title: Dematerialisation Market Action Taskforce
summary: HMT’s working draft report sets out a roadmap for the UK withdrawal of paper share certificates and introduction of digital registers for UK-traded shares of UK-incorporated companies. It is an implementation plan and policy proposal, with further consultation and later legislation/secondary measures still needed before the changes take effect. The report also discusses Step 2 and Step 3 next-stage reforms and indicative timing.

title: One Year On: Delivering the FS Growth and Competitiveness Strategy
summary: HM Treasury’s one-year progress report on the UK Financial Services Growth and Competitiveness Strategy describes actions already taken and future priorities on regulatory reform, cryptoassets, wholesale market digitisation, retail investment, capital markets, skills and clusters. It does not itself create new binding requirements. The publication is for awareness only.

title: Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulation – Draft SI and Policy note
summary: Draft UK statutory instrument laid before Parliament to remake the AIFM regime, including authorisation, registration, marketing, depositary liability, control/disclosure rules for AIFs, and FCA information/reporting powers. It applies to UK AIFMs, AIFMs marketing in the UK, RVECA and SEF managers, and certain Gibraltar firms. Commencement is on a future date to be specified.

title: Financial Services Regulators Complaints Commissioner Annual Report and Accounts 2025-26 and regulator responses
summary: This is the Complaints Commissioner’s annual report to Parliament on how UK financial regulators handled complaints in 2025/26. It describes complaint themes, statistics and examples, and includes regulator responses. It does not create new rules or obligations for firms.

title: Meeting minutes - February 2026
summary: Minutes of the Chancellor’s meeting with the Bank of England Governor after the latest Financial Stability Report. It is an informational record of a statutory meeting requirement and does not itself impose new obligations or deadlines.

title: Update on the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot issuance
summary: HM Treasury says the DIGIT pilot issuance is expected by Q1 2027 and that HSBC and LSEG have signed an MoU to improve investor access. It is an update on the government’s digital gilt pilot, with no new rule or obligation created for firms.

title: EM on customs duty on distance imported goods sales (C(2026)2760)
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU delegated regulation on customs declarations and data elements for the temporary €3 duty on low-value imported goods, as it applies in Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework. It is an explanatory memorandum, not the binding instrument itself. The regulation has applied since 1 July 2026; HMRC says any CDS instruction changes will be communicated in due course.

title: Treasury Minutes – July 2026
summary: Treasury Minutes setting out HM Treasury’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports on public spending and programme oversight, including hospital building, public bodies accountability, RTGS renewal and economic crime. It records government agreements, disagreements and target implementation dates for some responses, but does not itself create new rules or obligations for firms.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting – April 2026
summary: A record of a meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA discussing the FCA’s March 2026 Perimeter Report. It explains the financial services regulatory perimeter and summarises the discussion, but does not itself change any rules or requirements.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group: Reconnection Framework Technical Annex
summary: This G7 Cyber Expert Group technical annex shares best practices for disconnection, remediation, assurance, reconnection and recovery after a cyber incident. It is aimed mainly at financial-sector organisations and suggests ways to prepare attestation and data-sharing during reconnection, but it does not create regulatory requirements. No compliance date or binding obligation is set.
